data.title: RubyUI (Former PhlexUI): Ruby Gem for RubyUI Components
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: RubyUI 是一个开源的 Ruby gem，提供可复制粘贴的 UI 组件，旨在加速开发过程。它并非传统的组件库，而是通过生成或复制组件代码供开发者自由定制使用。其特点包括高速性能（基于 Phlex，比 Rails ERB 模板快 12 倍）、精美且可高度自定义的 UI、低依赖性以及易于复用。安装简便，通过命令行即可完成，并提供详细文档和组件生成器。RubyUI 强调开发者对组件设计的完全控制，适合构建个性化的组件库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Phlex项目及其在Ruby和Rails开发中的应用和价值

不同观点：
• GenericCanadian: 认为Phlex使前端开发变得有趣，特别提到通过使用纯Ruby和私有方法作为局部视图来改进UI的 refactoring。提供了一个具体项目链接，展示了Phlex在Rails项目中的应用。
• Sophira: 对Phlex是否适用于原生Ruby应用提出疑问，指出安装过程依赖Rails命令，暗示该项目更偏向于Web开发。
• budu: 赞赏RubyUI团队的工作，表示Phlex已成为其新项目的首选工具之一。
• bdcravens: 对组件名称全局命名空间问题表示关注，但认为手动解决可能不难。
• drumpkid: 对Phlex的性能声称表示怀疑，指出缺乏明确的基准测试，并提到微基准测试可能具有误导性。
• anonygler: 强烈反对Phlex的实现方式，认为其对垃圾收集器造成压力、调试困难，且模板作为代码无法缓存。认为前端开发应更多依赖JS/JSX，并对Ruby社区的未来表示担忧。
• daviding: 对Phlex持观望态度，指出Date Picker组件演示页面存在问题，影响其对库质量的判断。
• alexmccain6: 关注Phlex在大型应用中的扩展性及其在内存使用和调试方面的潜在权衡。
• dzonga: 对Phlex在实际项目中的应用效果表示好奇，询问是否有人用Phlex构建过实质性项目。
• jspash: 对Phlex使用PascalCase作为DSL命名约定表示不解，猜测是为了吸引React开发者。
• ajmaia: 分享了团队在当前Rails 8项目中使用Phlex预发布版本的经验，表示非常有用。
• cbeltrao: 简单表达了对Phlex项目的赞赏。
• desireco42: 对Phlex项目表示赞赏，并对Ruby社区的创新表示高兴。
• justinko: 对Phlex不支持直接复制/粘贴HTML表示不满。
• ramesh31: 对Phlex组件的视觉效果表示赞赏，但对其使用场景和用户群体表示困惑。

补充讨论：
• Phlex的性能声称及其基准测试的透明性是争议的焦点，特别是anonygler对此提出强烈批评。
• Phlex在实际项目中的应用效果和扩展性是多个评论者关注的重点，尤其是其在大型应用中的表现。
• Phlex的DSL命名约定和全局命名空间问题引发了部分讨论，显示出开发者对其设计决策的不同看法。
• 部分评论者对Phlex的实用性和易用性提出具体问题和意见，如演示页面问题和HTML复制/粘贴支持。

总体而言，评论中对Phlex的态度从高度赞赏到强烈反对不等，展现了不同开发者对其价值和适用性的多样看法。

RubyUI (former PhlexUI) 🚀
Beautifully designed components that you can copy and paste into your apps. Accessible. Customizable. Open Source.
This is NOT a component library. It's a collection of re-usable components that you can generate or copy and paste into your apps.
Pick the components you need. Copy and paste the code into your project and customize to your needs. The code is yours.
Use this as a reference to build your own component libraries.
Key Features:
Built for Speed
⚡: RubyUI leverages Phlex, which is up to 12x faster than traditional Rails ERB templates.
Stunning UI
🎨: Design beautiful, streamlined, and customizable UIs that sell your app effortlessly.
Stay Organized
📁: Keep your UI components well-organized and easy to manage.
Customer-Centric UX
🧑‍💼: Create memorable app experiences for your users.
Completely Customizable
🔧: Full control over the design of all components.
Minimal Dependencies
🍃: Uses custom-built Stimulus.js controllers to keep your app lean.
Reuse with Ease
♻️: Build components once and use them seamlessly across your project.
How to Use:
Find the perfect component
🔍: Browse live-embedded components on our documentation page.
Copy the snippet
📋: Easily copy code snippets for quick implementation.
Make it yours
🎨: Customize components using Tailwind utility classes to fit your specific needs.
Installation 🚀
1. Install the gem
bundle add ruby_ui --group development --require
false
or add it to your Gemfile:
gem
"ruby_ui"
,
group
:
:development
,
require
:
false
2. Run the installer:
bin/rails g ruby_ui:install
3. Done! 🎉
You can generate your components using
ruby_ui:component
generator.
bin/rails g ruby_ui:component Accordion
Documentation 📖
Visit
https://rubyui.com/docs/introduction
to view the full documentation, including:
Detailed component guides
Themes
Lookbook
Getting started guide
Speed Comparison 🏎️
RubyUI, powered by Phlex, outperforms alternative methods:
Phlex: Baseline 🏁
ViewComponent: ~1.5x slower 🚙
ERB Templates: ~5x slower 🐢
See the original
view layers benchmark
by @KonnorRogers and its
variations
.
Importmap notes:
If you run into importmap issues this stackoverflow question might help:
https://stackoverflow.com/questions/70548841/how-to-add-custom-js-file-to-new-rails-7-project/72855705

data.title: Generate autounattend.xml files for Windows 10/11
data.author: nixass
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows系统安装与配置的技巧和工具

不同观点：
• chem83认为可以通过在安装时选择英文（全球）语言来避免安装多余的垃圾软件，虽然Windows Store在该模式下无法工作，但可以在首次启动后改回首选语言解决。他还提到，即时更改语言仍会自动添加垃圾软件，需要重启一两次来避免。
• juujian批评Windows系统需要大量变通方法，表示对这种情况感到惊讶。
• atVelocet分享了多年的经验，推荐使用LTSC或IoT/Enterprise版本，并提供了一系列工具和步骤来优化和配置Windows系统，例如使用NTLite工具、配置GroupPolicies、安装防火墙和NextDNS等。他还建议禁用一些安全功能以提高性能。
• ralphc质疑这些复杂方法对于普通用户的实用性，提到普通用户如在Costco购买预装Windows 11的笔记本后，直接使用“无网络”技巧是否仍然有效。

补充讨论：
• j1elo希望有一个.reg文件生成器网站，帮助应用一些Windows设置，如始终显示文件扩展名、使用经典右键菜单等。
• cwillu提到无法关闭粘滞键快捷方式的问题，表示在新电脑上经常误触。
• _JamesA_分享了自己使用生成器部署Windows 11 Enterprise虚拟机的正面经验。
• teknopaul希望有一个类似的工具用于.deb文件，以便更容易配置。
• CSDude和nullwarp表达了对某些设置选项的喜爱和工具的实用性。
• theandrewbailey分享了自己使用unattend.xml文件将C:\Users放在硬盘上的经验，尽管文档明确警告不要这样做。
• kalev询问是否可以通过该方法禁用autopilot/mdm。
• nicman23请求添加企业IoT版本的支持。
• 7bit则认为使用Windows ADK才是专业做法，贬低该工具的实用性。

争议焦点：
• 关于通过选择安装语言避免垃圾软件的有效性存在争议，尤其是重启后是否仍会添加垃圾软件。
• 对于普通用户来说，复杂的安装和配置方法是否实际有效存在不同看法。
• 7bit对工具实用性的批评与其他用户对工具的正面评价形成对比。

data.title: A dramatic Einstein ring seen by Webb
data.author: programd
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）观测到的一个显著的爱因斯坦环。爱因斯坦环是由于引力透镜效应造成的，当一个遥远的星系正好被一个较近的星系遮挡时，其光线会被引力弯曲成一个圆形。这种现象验证了广义相对论的预测。尽管爱因斯坦曾认为无法直接观测到这种现象，但现代望远镜已经发现了数十个爱因斯坦环。文章提到的图像显示了一个螺旋星系的光被前方椭圆星系引力透镜化，形成了几乎完美的环状。这种景象依赖于观测者的独特视角，展现了宇宙的美妙。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对引力透镜效应下天文图像的科学分析与解释

不同观点：
• [dylan604] 提出是否已有方法将通过爱因斯坦环观察到的扭曲图像还原为原始形状，并提到利用太阳作为引力透镜的可能性，暗示了这种技术的潜在数学挑战。
• [rimeice] 询问前景的椭圆星系是否仅为中心的小光点，而后面的螺旋星系因透镜效应被放大，提出了对图像中天体实际位置的疑问。
• [timdiggerm] 回应关于观测点独特性的评论，指出虽然我们能观测到独特的图像，但其他星系的观测者也能看到我们无法看到的奇观，强调不同观测点各有独特价值。
• [JayDustheadz] 询问地球到图像中星系的距离，关注图像中天体的具体位置信息。
• [comrade1234] 对图像中缺少衍射尖峰感到疑惑，询问是因为图像中的天体都是星系而非恒星，还是在图像处理中被去除了，并提供了一个参考链接以支持讨论。
• [kohbo] 对讨论中的哲学性观点表示赞赏，认为美不仅存在于观察者的眼中，还与观察者的位置有关。
• [throwawaymaths] 认为这种图像可以用于测试暗物质理论，指出了其在科学研究中的潜在价值。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了爱因斯坦环和引力透镜效应的技术性问题，如去扭曲技术和太阳作为透镜的设想。
• 对图像处理技术，如衍射尖峰的处理，也引起了参与者的兴趣和讨论。
• 对天体距离和实际位置的疑问反映出对具体天文数据的需求。
• 哲学性评论为讨论增添了美学和相对性的视角。
• 暗物质理论测试的提及展示了天文图像在科学研究中的广泛应用。

A dramatic Einstein ring seen by Webb
by Brian Koberlein,
Universe Today
A spiral galaxy lensed around a closer elliptical galaxy. Credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, G. Mahler
One of the first verified predictions of general relativity is the gravitational deflection of starlight. The effect was
first observed in 1919
during a total solar eclipse. Since stars appear as points of light, the effect is seen as an apparent shift in the position of stars near the eclipse. But the effect happens more generally.
If a distant galaxy is obscured by a closer one, some of the distant light is gravitationally lensed around the closer galaxy, giving us a warped and distorted view of the faraway stars. This effect can also magnify the distant galaxy, making its light appear brighter, and we have used this effect to observe some of the most distant stars in the universe.
But perhaps the most beautiful effect of gravitational lensing is what's known as an Einstein Ring. This is where the
distant galaxy
is so perfectly centered behind the closer galaxy that its light is distorted into a circle of light. Einstein was aware of the effect but said in 1936 that "there is no hope of observing this phenomenon directly." But as brilliant as Einstein was, he couldn't imagine the power of modern telescopes.
We have now found dozens of Einstein rings, and one of the more beautiful examples was recently found by JWST, as seen in the image above. The close galaxy in the foreground is an
elliptical galaxy
that's part of a large cluster known as SMACS J0028.2-7537. The more colorful galaxy warped around it is a
spiral galaxy
similar to the Milky Way. It is billions of years more distant, but perfectly aligned to create the almost perfect ring.
Of course, this image is only possible because of our vantage point. Astronomers in other galaxies wouldn't catch such a wondrous image. Yet another astronomical example of how beauty is not only in the eye of the beholder, but also where that beholder is.

43557139.article_summary: 文章介绍了詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）观测到的一个显著的爱因斯坦环。爱因斯坦环是由于引力透镜效应造成的，当一个遥远的星系正好被一个较近的星系遮挡时，其光线会被引力弯曲成一个圆形。这种现象验证了广义相对论的预测。尽管爱因斯坦曾认为无法直接观测到这种现象，但现代望远镜已经发现了数十个爱因斯坦环。文章提到的图像显示了一个螺旋星系的光被前方椭圆星系引力透镜化，形成了几乎完美的环状。这种景象依赖于观测者的独特视角，展现了宇宙的美妙。

data.title: Coffea stenophylla: A forgotten bean that could save coffee from extinction
data.author: derbOac
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了植物学家如何寻找稀有咖啡物种以防止咖啡灭绝。重点提到了一种被遗忘的咖啡豆——**Coffea stenophylla**，其在1896年被记录具有“优越的风味”和市场潜力。如今，科学家正深入偏远地区寻找这种及其他新咖啡物种，以应对气候变化和病害对现有咖啡种植的威胁，确保未来咖啡供应的可持续性。这种努力可能拯救咖啡行业，并让人们继续享受优质的咖啡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕咖啡替代品、咖啡因增强及气候变化对咖啡种植的影响展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持使用野生植物如 yaupon 作为咖啡替代品**：doodlebugging 提到 yaupon  holly 茶含有天然咖啡因，且具有适应多种气候条件的优势（耐旱、耐涝），并指出其含有可减轻咖啡因崩溃的成分（如可可碱）。同时提到该植物历史上的命名可能带有政治或商业动机，旨在避免与英国茶竞争。

• **质疑干旱气候下增强咖啡因生产的难度**：djha-skin 认为在干燥气候下，植物专注于生产作为农药的咖啡因会更加困难，因为昆虫在潮湿气候中更为猖獗，而干燥气候中植物和害虫对水的依赖都会减少。

• **提到其他咖啡豆品种的潜力**：
  - sgt 提到曾尝试过一种叫 Racemosa 的咖啡豆，体验独特但与传统咖啡不同。
  - vmwareuser-020 提到 Liberica 咖啡豆，已在马来西亚流行，并具有抗热和抗旱的特性，适合在极端气候条件下种植。

• **对气候变化导致咖啡灭绝的观点持怀疑态度**：briandear 认为关于咖啡因气候变化而灭绝的说法过于夸张，指出历史上咖啡作物失败是常见现象，且气候变化对作物种植区域的影响可以随时间调整。

• **对全球依赖刺激品的批评**：Henchman21 批评社会对刺激品的依赖，并暗示这种现象令人沮丧。

• **从科学角度讨论植物水分利用效率**：chris_va 提到植物水分利用的低效问题，并建议未来通过基因工程（如C4/CAM咖啡）改善这一问题。

补充讨论：
• **提到与咖啡相关的历史和文化**：saunved_42 和 jessekv 提到咖啡品种的历史和地域文化差异，如 stenophylla 咖啡的历史价值以及台湾和澳大利亚的优质咖啡文化。

• **视频资源分享**：dbetteridge 分享了 James Hoffman 的一个视频，探讨了咖啡豆的研究工作。

争议焦点：
• **气候变化对咖啡种植的实际影响**：部分评论者（如 briandear）认为气候变化对咖啡种植的威胁被夸大，而其他评论者（如 djha-skin）则强调气候变化对作物的影响复杂且多方面。

data.title: Matrix.org Will Migrate to MAS
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary:
2025年4月7日，Matrix.org将把其 homeserver 的身份验证系统迁移到 Matrix 认证服务（MAS），以实现基于 OAuth 2.0/OIDC 的下一代认证。此次迁移将导致最多一小时的停机时间。多项 MSC（包括 MSC3861 等）已经进入最后评论期并即将合并，新的认证系统将带来新的账户管理界面、更高的安全性及更好的注册体验。

**主要变化包括：**
1. **账户管理界面**：用户可在 account.matrix.org 上管理设备、联系信息、密码及账户注销。
2. **安全性提升**：服务器将独有账户凭证访问权，限制敏感操作，并清晰展示使用账户的客户端。
3. **注册体验改进**：新系统明确账户存储位置，支持下一代客户端。

现有会话在迁移后保持活跃，兼容旧版客户端。MAS 开启了 Matrix 身份验证的新时代，未来还将支持如二维码登录等新功能。

如有任何疑问，可加入 #matrix-auth:matrix.org 讨论。

主要讨论点：Matrix平台的功能、安全性、用户体验改进以及技术实现细节

不同观点：
• jckahn认为Matrix（通过Element）由于采用端到端加密（E2EE），比Google Chat和WhatsApp更安全，并推荐其他人也使用Matrix。他还提到Signal没有网页界面，因此不适合他。
• jokoon提到在使用Firefox严格管理cookies时，连接到Mozilla的Matrix实例时遇到困难，并对MAS（Matrix Authentication Service）能否解决此问题表示期待。
• apetresc回忆起一个旧的MSC或TWIM，提到了一种新的认证机制，允许使用自己的域而无需自建服务器处理实际流量，并对MAS是否包含此功能表示疑问。
• neilv关注matrix.org的服务器端代码是否开源以及能否自托管，并询问新的认证方法是否需要修改所有Matrix客户端。

• kibwen认为Matrix有可能在Discord逐渐恶化的情况下获得市场机会，但需要打磨用户体验以抓住机会。
• oofbey将Matrix比作新的XMPP，暗示其可能成为替代通讯工具。
• xyst查看了MSCs后发现MAS启用了OIDC/OAUTH认证流程，并希望Matrix homeserver能作为身份提供者，提供替代大科技公司身份验证的方案。
• frankzander询问是否存在用于warez的Matrix服务器。
• sanatgersappa提到Simplex聊天，询问其他人是否尝试过。

补充讨论：
• 用户对Matrix的安全性、隐私性以及自托管能力表示关注。
• 改进用户体验，特别是对非技术用户的入门体验，是一个重要的讨论点。
• 新的认证机制及其对不同类型服务器的潜在影响引发讨论，包括技术实现细节和用户体验的平衡。

43558464.article_content:
On Monday 7th of April 2025 at 7am UTC, we will migrate the Matrix.org homeserver's authentication system over to MAS (Matrix Authentication Service) in order to benefit from Next-generation authentication.
The migration will involve up to one hour of downtime.
MSC3861
(Next-generation auth for Matrix, based on OAuth 2.0/OIDC) and its dependent MSCs have progressed sufficiently that the Foundation is confident in MAS and the new next-generation auth APIs.Specifically, all the MSCs are now in or have passed Final Comment Period (FCP) with disposition to merge! 🎉
We expect the MSCs to finish FCP and get merged into the next spec release.The full list of core Next-gen Auth MSCs is:
MSC3861: Next-generation auth for Matrix, based on OAuth 2.0/OIDC
MSC2964: Usage of OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant and refresh token grant
MSC2965: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata
MSC2966: Usage of OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration in Matrix
MSC2967: API scopes
MSC4254: Usage of RFC7009 Token Revocation for Matrix client logout
This is incredibly exciting, reflecting 4 years of work on next-generation auth, and brings with it a new account management interface, additional security, and a better registration experience.
🔗
The account management interface
You will be able to manage you account on a
dedicated interface at account.matrix.org
(accessible through your client or browser), where you can:
See and delete your devices.
Update your contact information, like your email address.
Change your password and deactivate your account.
🔗
Improved security
MAS comes with a significant refactoring of how authentication works on Matrix. Without breaking compatibility with the former authentication API, it brings several benefits
Now, only your server will be able to see your account credentials! No more typing your password in every client you’d like to log in to.
Restricted access to sensitive operations, like deactivating your account.
Clearer view of which clients are using your account.
🔗
Improved registration experience
Regardless of the client you use, the new registration and login experience makes it clear where your account lives, and it supports next-generation clients like Element X.
🔗
Impact
Your current sessions will remain active after the migration has taken effect. In other words, you will not be logged out of your clients.
We’re providing backwards compatibility for existing Matrix clients - this does not remove the stable Matrix 1.0 APIs. You can read more about the impact on clients in our previously published blog article -
Authentication changes on Matrix.org
.
🔗
This is only the beginning!
Matrix Authentication Service is Matrix's next-generation authentication stack. Together with the next-generation authentication APIs, it is the base of a new exciting era for authentication in Matrix!
This has been one of the most ambitious projects within the Matrix project, the result of a multi-year investment by Element, funded in turn by Element’s customers, including BWI.
It will enable new forms of authentication flows, like QR-code login (coming soon to matrix.org with
MSC4108
), and new categories of applications building on Matrix, thanks to fine-grained control over client access to the account.
You can find all the technical details in Quentin's Matrix Conference talk,
Harder Better Faster Stronger Authentication with OpenID Connec
t.
Finally, if you have any concerns, please come talk to us in
#matrix-auth:matrix.org
The Foundation needs you
The Matrix.org Foundation is a non-profit and only relies
on donations to operate. Its core mission is to maintain
the Matrix Specification, but it does much more than that.
It maintains the matrix.org homeserver and hosts several
bridges for free. It fights for our collective rights to
digital privacy and dignity.
Support us

data.title: How Google built its Gemini robotics models
data.author: simonpure
data.article_summary: 谷歌DeepMind发布了新一代Gemini Robotics模型，这些模型专为机器人设计，能够执行复杂任务，如准备沙拉、玩井字棋，甚至折纸。新模型基于Gemini 2.0，通过机器人特定数据进行微调，增加了物理动作能力。Gemini Robotics-ER模型专注于“具身推理”，能够识别物体、确定位置并生成执行代码。而Gemini Robotics模型则能够理解场景、与用户互动并采取行动，尤其在灵活性方面取得显著进展。这些模型可以适应多种机器人形态，完成不同任务，如打包午餐盒或擦白板，展示了广泛的应用潜力。谷歌希望通过这些模型，实现能够帮助人们完成日常任务的机器人，最终成为物理世界中的智能代理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Gemini Assistant的可靠性、AI与机器人技术的未来发展及其潜在应用和影响

不同观点：
• [lima] 认为Gemini Assistant在Pixel手机上的基本功能（如设置计时器、添加购物清单）不如之前的Google Assistant可靠，尽管AI技术在其他方面有进步。
• [abidhusain] 对AI和机器人技术的进步感到兴奋，认为外包特定角色（如AI研究或机器人工程师）可以帮助公司引入顶尖人才，推动创新，并讨论了外包对研发和市场速度的影响。
• [dachworker] 指出Gemini的具体实现细节不足，但认为如果该技术能够半可靠地工作，将产生比ChatGPT大100倍的影响。
• [barbazoo] 怀疑Gemini Assistant的民用目的，暗示其技术可能主要用于军事，尽管公司试图让公众相信它会用于日常生活。
• [hansmayer] 以幽默的方式指出一些不切实际的期待，如让机器人完成篮球扣篮，质疑其实际应用价值。
• [harmmonica] 认为Google在将研究转化为产品方面存在困难，提到Google在transformers技术上的先发优势被ChatGPT抢占，担心Google的机器人技术可能也会面临类似问题。
• [otherayden] 担心机器人技术可能被用于国防工业，提出如果机器人能够理解如“把橡皮擦收起来”的指令，也可能被用于军事指令如“杀死所有敌人”。
• [cozyman] 以幽默方式提问机器人是否遵循机器人法则，如果让它杀人会怎样。
• [free652] 以愚人节为由，对消息的真实性表示怀疑。

补充讨论：
- 评论中对Google Gemini Assistant的实际应用和可靠性存在争议，部分用户质疑其相对于之前技术的退步。
- 对AI和机器人技术的未来发展方向及其潜在军事应用存在担忧，特别是技术在国防领域的可能滥用。
- 对Google在将前沿技术转化为市场产品方面的能力存在怀疑，历史上的一些失败案例被提及。

43557310.article_content:
How we built the new family of Gemini Robotics models
Apr 01, 2025
·
[[read-time]] min read
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
Powered by Gemini Robotics models, robots can learn complex actions like preparing salads, playing games like Tic-Tac-Toe and even folding an origami fox.
Joel Meares
Contributor, The Keyword
Share
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Mail
Copy link
As Google DeepMind prepared for
its recent announcement
of a new family of Gemini 2.0 models designed specifically for robots, its head of robotics, Carolina Parada, gathered her team for another check of the tech’s capabilities.
They asked a bi-arm ALOHA robot — a duo of limber metal appendages with multiple joints and pincer-like hands used widely in research — to perform tasks it hadn’t done before, using objects it hadn’t seen. “We did random things like put my shoe on the table and ask it to put some pens inside,” Carolina says. “The robot took a moment to understand the task, then did it.”
For the next request, they found a toy basketball hoop and ball and asked the robot to do a “slam dunk.” Carolina watched, proud and delighted, as it did just that.
Carolina says witnessing the slam dunk was a “wow” moment.
“We’d trained models to help robots with specific tasks and to understand natural language before, but this was a step change,” Carolina says. “The robot had never seen anything related to basketball, or this specific toy. Yet it understood something complex — ‘slam dunk the ball’ — and performed the action smoothly.
On its first try.
”
This all-rounder robot was powered by a
Gemini Robotics
model that is part of a new family of multimodal models for robotics. The models build upon
Gemini 2.0
through fine-tuning with robot-specific data, adding physical action to Gemini’s multimodal outputs like text, video and audio. "This milestone lays the foundation for the next generation of robotics that can be helpful across a range of applications," said Google CEO Sundar Pichai when
announcing the new models on X
.
The Gemini Robotics models are highly dextrous, interactive and general, meaning they can drive robots to react to new objects, environments and instructions without further training. Helpful, given the team’s ambitions.
“Our mission is to build embodied AI to power robots that help you with everyday tasks in the real world,” says Carolina, whose fascination with robotics began with childhood sci-fi cartoons, fueled by dreams of automated chores. “Eventually, robots will be just another surface on which we interact with AI, like our phones or computers — agents in the physical world.”
Like people, robots need two main functions to perform tasks effectively and safely: the ability to understand and make decisions, and the ability to take action. Gemini Robotics-ER, an "embodied reasoning” model built on Gemini 2.0 Flash, focuses on the former, recognizing elements in front of it, defining their size and location, and predicting the trajectory and grip required to move them. It then can generate code to execute the action. We’re now making this model available to trusted testers and partners.
Google DeepMind is also introducing Gemini Robotics, its most advanced vision-language-action model, which allows robots to reason about a scene, interact with the user and take action. Crucially, it makes significant advances in an area that has proved tricky for roboticists: dexterity. “What comes naturally to humans is difficult for robots,” Carolina explains. “Dexterity requires both spatial reasoning, and complex physical manipulation. Across testing, Gemini Robotics has set a new state-of-the-art for dexterity, solving complex multi-step tasks with smooth motions and great completion times.”
Gemini Robotics-ER excels at embodied reasoning capabilities, including detecting objects and pointing at object parts, finding corresponding points and detecting objects in 3D.
Powered by Gemini Robotics, machines have prepared salads, packed kids’ lunches, played games like Tic-Tac-Toe and even folded an origami fox.
Preparing models that could do many different kinds of tasks was a challenge — largely because it went against the general industry practice of training models for a
single
task over and over until it can be solved. “Instead, we chose broad task learning, training models on a huge number of tasks,” Carolina says. “We expected to see generalization emerge after a certain amount of time, and we were right.”
Both models can adapt to multiple embodiments, including academic-focused robots, like the bi-arm ALOHA machine, or humanoid robots like Apollo developed by our partner Apptronik.
The models adapt to different embodiments, able to perform tasks like packing a lunchbox or wiping a whiteboard in different forms.
This ability to adapt is key to a future where robots could take on a number of very different roles.

data.title: Sailing from Berkeley to Hawaii in a 19ft Sailboat
data.author: protonbob
data.article_summary: 《Chubby Commutes to Hawaii: 技术讨论》由Bill Teplow撰写，文章讲述了作者作为地质顾问，利用休假时间准备了一次从加州伯克利到夏威夷的航行。他的船是West Wight Potter 19 "Chubby"。在出发前，他进行了大量准备工作，包括增加两个额外的排水口以防浪淹，并在舱口安装防水门以提高安全性。作者还安装了jack lines以便在甲板工作时保持安全。航行距离为2142海里，历时24天，整个过程顺利无重大事故。作者强调，尽管Chubby顺利完成了跨洋航行，但它设计上是沿海巡航艇，不建议作为远洋巡航船使用。此次航行体验愉快，船体和设备均无损坏，抵达夏威夷时状态良好。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于单人航行冒险及其准备工作的讨论

不同观点：
• LeifCarrotson认为该网站非常有趣，尤其是关于其妻子的信件以及航行中的电力管理。他指出，现代技术如太阳能板可以更有效地解决电力问题，而174瓦时的日常电力需求在今天可以通过简单的太阳能方案满足。
• _cormorant指出可能有一个与故事中描述的船只相同的船正在出售，并提供了一个出售链接。
• smithclay推荐了一本相关的书《Sailing Alone: A Surprising History of Isolation and Survival at Sea》，供对单人航行历史感兴趣的人阅读。
• medion分享了个人类似的航行经历，从Berkeley出发到Honolulu，虽然时间比预期长且遇到了一些危险，但总体顺利。
• _whiteCaps_推荐了Paul Lutus的航行书和Vic Maui比赛，为有兴趣参与航行比赛的人提供了参考。
• goleary对原文中不使用SSB接收机获取天气报告的做法表示惊讶。
• rkhassen9对原文中提到的罐头防锈措施提出疑问，不确定是否过于谨慎。
• for1nner推荐了一个YouTube频道，其中包含关于单人航行旅程的视频，认为这些视频对航行准备有帮助。
• BXLE_1-1-BitIs1分享了自己在Lake Superior和一些河流系统中的独木舟航行经验，使用了不同的食物和装备。
• protonbob喜欢该网站的复古设计和探索体验。
• zbowling感叹现代网站设计中失去了一些旧技术，如iso-8859-1编码。
• TuringNYC担心原文中缺乏备用电源，建议至少使用太阳能板作为备用，并引用了科幻电影《星球大战》中的冗余设计作对比。
• frainfreeze提到了Evi Nemeth，一位从IT领域退休后开始航海冒险的女性，推荐了她的书和航行经历。
• code_kate08对故事中的勇气和创造力表示钦佩，认为这是人类冒险精神的体现。
• nataz推荐了Robin Lee Graham的故事，一个16岁开始单人环球航行的年轻人，写了书并被拍成电影。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于原文中对罐头防锈措施的必要性，rkhassen9认为可能过于谨慎，但尚未有明确结论。
- 不同用户分享了各自的航行经验和推荐资源，提供了丰富的视角和实用建议。
- 对现代技术如太阳能板的讨论显示出技术进步对传统航行方式的影响和改进可能性。

43558077.article_content:
Chubby Commutes to Hawaii:
A Technical Discussion
By Bill Teplow
From Dream to Plan
As a consulting exploration geologist, my work life tends to consist of periods
of intense work punctuated by periods of intense unemployment. True to form,
I completed my last work assignment on July 8th and I found myself with a month
and a half of enforced leisure before my next gig. Since the coming job was
located on the Big Island of Hawaii, an old fantasy of mine started to materialize
as an actual plan. In early July, while looking at my West Wight Potter 19 "Chubby"
sitting jauntily at her berth at the Berkeley Marina, tugging at her dock lines
and proudly showing off her new bottom paint, it dawned on me that I could use
her to commute to my next job. On July 9th I started serious preparations for
the trip.
Just as I was getting heavily into the outfitting, my client on the Big Island
called and asked me to show up on July 16th at a coordinating meeting for the
project startup. I flew over to Hilo a day early and went straight to Radio
Bay, the small boat harbor located in the far eastern corner of Hilo Bay, tucked
in behind the big commercial docks. I chatted with the very friendly and accommodating
Harbor Master's staff and got all the information needed for proper check-in
and for renting a space at the harbor. I also got a chance to see the particular
style of anchoring and stern tie that is used at the 10' high cement sea wall.
The daily fee for keeping Chubby at Radio Bay is $8.50. There is a 30 day limit
that can be extended if there is room. When I arrived four weeks later in Chubby,
there were two boats tied up, leaving room for perhaps 15 more, so space was
not an issue. There is a locked restroom with shower at the dock for the exclusive
use of cruisers, and a market and laundromat one block away. The friendly atmosphere
and secure tie-up for my destination port gave me the final push to commit to
the voyage.
Upon return home to Oakland I found myself with four days to make the final
preparations for the trip. I had committed myself to a July 21 departure which
was the latest possible date that would assure my arrival in Hilo prior to start
of work. Also that date had a mild afternoon ebb to aid my escape. With such
a short period of time to prepare the boat, things got pretty hectic. But when
it came time to push back from the dock, Chubby was pretty well prepared and
upon arriving in Hilo, I was still of the same opinion.
To Reality
The following is a discussion of the technical aspects of preparing Chubby
and sailing her from Berkeley, California to Hilo, Hawaii. The actual distance
sailed was 2142 nautical miles and the voyage took 24 days, almost to the minute,
to complete. The voyage in general went very smoothly with no major mishaps.
I arrived in Hilo feeling fit, rested and happy. For those who enjoy reading
about ordeals at sea, I am sorry to disappoint. Nothing that was supplied by
International Marine, the Potter manufacturer, broke during the voyage. Chubby
generally behaved quite well in the open ocean and the trade winds even though
she is designed to be a trailer sailer and coastal pocket cruiser. I want to
stress that I do not want this article or my generally pleasant experience in
sailing Chubby to Hawaii to be construed as an endorsement for using the Potter
19 as a blue water cruiser. It was designed to be a safe and competent trailerable
coastal pocket cruiser and it fulfills its stated goals admirably.
Safety
Of the modifications I made to the otherwise stock Potter 19, most were aimed
at increasing the margin of safety for this already safe and stable design.
In order to increase the rate of drainage of the cockpit in case Chubby was
pooped, I added two additional 1-1/4" diameter cockpit drains located just
above the cockpit floor at the base of the transom. I also raised the overall
freeboard of the cabin by installing a hinged and latched lower companionway
door. Weather stripping for the door made a water-tight seal. This increased
the cabin freeboard by about 8" and raised it above the height of the transom.
Theoretically this would allow the clearing of water from the cockpit while
preventing significant volumes of water from spilling into the cabin.
I installed two types of jack lines. I ran a conventional nylon webbing jackline
around the perimeter of boat and anchored them through the fore and aft pairs
of deck cleats. The jackline was used as an anchor for my tether and harness.
The perimeter arrangement allowed me to clip into the jackline in the cockpit
and then go to the foredeck for headsail changes in my usual manner which was
to swing outboard of the shrouds. If I got bucked off the foredeck, I would
theoretically slide along the jackline to the stern and would be able to climb
aboard the boat using the swim ladder. A critical extra bit of safety equipment
for this jackline system was the tiller pilot trip line. It appeared to me that

• [notepad0x90] 认为代码签名证书的成本应该降低，并批评CA/B论坛（证书颁发机构/浏览器论坛）过于专注于TLS证书。他希望PKI在Linux社区中得到更广泛的应用，类似于Let's Encrypt为S/MIME和Authenticode等提供的服务。
• [infogulch] 关注自动颁发的中间CA（ICA）的可能性，并建议允许通过DNS-01挑战验证、短寿命且具有名称约束的ICA。他提出了三个反对意见并进行了反驳，强调这种机制能为私有服务提供更高的安全性和实用性。
• [tptacek] 指出Let's Encrypt已经多用途（MPIC），表明Let's Encrypt已经部分实现了多用途证书颁发的需求。
• [Y-bar] 关心本地自签名证书的有效期问题，尤其是在新的浏览器要求下（证书有效期需小于398天），是否会影响自签名证书的使用。
• [amiga386] 质疑内部企业DNS的证书颁发问题，担心企业可能需要向CA公开其内部DNS信息以获取有效证书。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是是否应允许自动颁发短寿命的中间CA，以提高安全性和灵活性。
• 另一个争议点是代码签名和非TLS证书的PKI应用场景是否应得到更多关注和支持。
• 讨论中还提到了自签名证书的有效期限制以及内部企业DNS的隐私问题，这涉及到证书颁发流程中的透明度和安全性之间的平衡。
• 最后，Let's Encrypt的多用途性和现有PKI基础设施的改进需求也是讨论的重要内容。

data.author: msfi
data.article_summary: The Mermaid Chart VS Code Plugin is a tool that allows developers to create and edit Mermaid.js diagrams directly within Visual Studio Code. It supports automatic file recognition, syntax highlighting, and real-time diagram rendering with pan and zoom features. The plugin seamlessly integrates with Markdown, enabling embedded diagrams in documentation. Advanced features include cloud integration, team collaboration, and AI-assisted diagram generation using GitHub Copilot. It supports offline editing and Git-based version control, making it ideal for developers working on software architecture, API flows, and microservice documentation. The plugin can be easily installed from the VS Code Marketplace, offering a frictionless workflow for both individual and team-based projects.

data.title: What, exactly, is an 'AI Agent'? Here's a litmus test
data.author: 1as
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了“AI代理”的定义和区分标准。尽管AI代理通常被认为是具备自主性和工具使用能力的AI驱动系统，但具体定义尚不明确。文章提出了一种精准的判断标准，即通过“身份”来界定AI代理。在法律概念中，代理可以代表 principal 行动，但也具有独立身份。在企业软件中，身份由审计日志中的行动者定义。因此，文章提出AI代理应能在审计日志中以其自身身份记录行动，具备自主性、工具使用能力和决策能力。与AI助理不同，AI代理能够独立行动，而不仅仅是作为人类的延伸。文章还指出，像ChatGPT这样的系统不被普遍视为代理，因为它们缺乏独立身份。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理的定义及其在不同情境下的应用

不同观点：
• andy99的观点: 认为代理（agent）和工作流（workflow）的区别在于代理有执行图中的循环，可以自主选择是否继续执行，而工作流则是链式的LLM调用，LLM没有选择权。引用Anthropic的定义来支持其观点。
• ajcp的观点: 认为AI代理的定义是能够根据广泛定义的外部刺激和动机/目标做出反应的系统，强调代理具有自主性，而非确定性的工作流。举例说明代理和非代理系统的区别。
• janalsncm的观点: 认为关于AI代理定义的讨论没有实际意义，重要的是软件能否可靠地完成任务，而不是它是否被称为AI或代理。
• bhouston的观点: 不认同ajcp的定义，认为代理应该有能力影响世界，并通过反馈循环感知和反应，而不需要人类干预。以ChatGPT为例说明何时算作代理。
• TeMPOraL的观点: 不认同以"AI系统是否以自己的身份执行操作"作为代理的定义，认为只有代表用户执行操作的系统才是代理，且这种定义不应被推广。
• asdev的观点: 认为自主的AI代理是一个包含LLM调用的循环，能够根据之前的输出做出反应。
• antonkar的观点: 提出一种物理学视角的定义，认为代理是时间性、能量性、选择性的，而智能是空间性、静态性的。
• simonw的观点: 指出在这个话题的讨论中已经有六种不同的代理定义，每种定义都有其自信的支持者。
• tedk-42的观点: 认为目前没有真正的AI代理，只是市场炒作，目前的代理只是将一系列交互通过代码粘合在一起，依赖LLM解释输入或生成输出。
• destedexplan的观点: 认为定义不重要，"who cares"。
• tiffanyh的观点: 质疑"代表服务的代理是否算作代理"。
• Feathercrown的观点: 认为AI代理具有选择何时行动的能力。
• whiddershins的观点: 认为"AI代理"是一个没有明确意义的术语，争论其定义没有意义，它可以是任何有助于设计或解释事物的定义。

补充讨论：
• DonHopkins分享了一个关于Cursor AI系统频繁出现幻觉（hallucination）的实际案例，展示了AI代理在实际应用中可能出现的问题，强调了AI系统在操作过程中可能带来的困扰和挑战。

争议焦点：
• AI代理的定义：不同参与者对AI代理的定义有不同理解，主要争议在于代理是否需要自主性、是否需要以自己的身份执行操作，以及代理与工作流之间的区别。
• 实际应用中的问题：DonHopkins分享的案例展示了AI系统在实际应用中可能出现的问题，如幻觉现象，这引发了对AI代理在实际应用中的可靠性和可用性的讨论。

总结：
讨论围绕AI代理的定义展开，参与者从不同角度提出了各自的看法，包括技术实现、哲学思考和实际应用中的问题。争议的焦点在于如何定义AI代理，特别是在自主性和执行身份方面的理解差异。同时，实际应用中AI系统出现的问题也被提出，显示出理论定义与实际应用之间的差距。

43560849.article_content:
What is an ”AI agent”?
Confusion abounds
.
There is also some consensus: agents must of course be
AI-driven systems
. They should have some degree of
autonomy
, and they should be able to
use tools
in addition to understanding and
reasoning
.
But why isn't, say, ChatGPT an agent? According to most definitions out there, it actually is. Yet most (including OpenAI themselves) don’t describe it that way. In general, we seem to have a sense of “we’ll know it when we see it” with AI agents.
To guide our building efforts at
Tines
, we wanted a more precise definition. So we came up with our own objective criteria – a litmus test – for agents. It boils down to
identity
.
Learning from the law
Agency is a longstanding
concept in common law
, where principals give authority to agents to act on their behalf. For example, a company could appoint a real estate broker to find an office. Or an individual could hire a travel agent to organize a vacation.
What happens when such an agent breaks the law? Are they, or the principal, to blame?
Principals can be held accountable (e.g. if they instruct the agent to do something illegal), but the agent makes its own decisions, too. So an agent may be the one prosecuted, when acting under their own
identity
.
In law, agents can act as their principal, but also independently as themselves.
Audit logs contain identity
In enterprise software systems, we have a clear definition of identity: the actor who is named in the audit log, for any action taken.
Our litmus test for AI agents:
Does the AI system perform actions under its own identity?
If it does, it’s an agent, and the audit logs will name the agent itself. And if it doesn’t – like most copilots or in-product assistants – it’s not.
Other properties of agents are revealed by passing this test. Identity implies
autonomy
, because the AI must
use tools
and perform actions independently. Identity requires capability and
reasoning
, because the AI must be capable of making good decisions to be entitled to bear such responsibility – an organization won’t trust it otherwise. And identity doesn't preclude an agent occasionally deferring to a human for input or supervision – agents in the real world do this, as do human employees with their colleagues and managers.
AI assistants are always supervised by a human. An AI agent can act independently on behalf of an organization. Audit logs are the litmus test.
Applying the litmus test
An AI agent is a system that can take independent actions under its own identity, rather than acting as an extension of a human user. This distinction – who or what is named in the audit log – defines whether a system is truly an agent, or simply an assistant.
By this definition, many great pieces of AI software are not agents, including our
Workbench
product, which is designed to operate within human control. And that's OK: we believe there will always be an important role for software that helps humans carry out their work more effectively.
But the promise of AI agents is something beyond this, and we're excited for that, too.
43560849.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了“AI代理”的定义和区分标准。尽管AI代理通常被认为是具备自主性和工具使用能力的AI驱动系统，但具体定义尚不明确。文章提出了一种精准的判断标准，即通过“身份”来界定AI代理。在法律概念中，代理可以代表 principal 行动，但也具有独立身份。在企业软件中，身份由审计日志中的行动者定义。因此，文章提出AI代理应能在审计日志中以其自身身份记录行动，具备自主性、工具使用能力和决策能力。与AI助理不同，AI代理能够独立行动，而不仅仅是作为人类的延伸。文章还指出，像ChatGPT这样的系统不被普遍视为代理，因为它们缺乏独立身份。
43560849.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理的定义及其在不同情境下的应用

不同观点：
• andy99的观点: 认为代理（agent）和工作流（workflow）的区别在于代理有执行图中的循环，可以自主选择是否继续执行，而工作流则是链式的LLM调用，LLM没有选择权。引用Anthropic的定义来支持其观点。
• ajcp的观点: 认为AI代理的定义是能够根据广泛定义的外部刺激和动机/目标做出反应的系统，强调代理具有自主性，而非确定性的工作流。举例说明代理和非代理系统的区别。
• janalsncm的观点: 认为关于AI代理定义的讨论没有实际意义，重要的是软件能否可靠地完成任务，而不是它是否被称为AI或代理。
• bhouston的观点: 不认同ajcp的定义，认为代理应该有能力影响世界，并通过反馈循环感知和反应，而不需要人类干预。以ChatGPT为例说明何时算作代理。
• TeMPOraL的观点: 不认同以"AI系统是否以自己的身份执行操作"作为代理的定义，认为只有代表用户执行操作的系统才是代理，且这种定义不应被推广。
• asdev的观点: 认为自主的AI代理是一个包含LLM调用的循环，能够根据之前的输出做出反应。
• antonkar的观点: 提出一种物理学视角的定义，认为代理是时间性、能量性、选择性的，而智能是空间性、静态性的。
• simonw的观点: 指出在这个话题的讨论中已经有六种不同的代理定义，每种定义都有其自信的支持者。
• tedk-42的观点: 认为目前没有真正的AI代理，只是市场炒作，目前的代理只是将一系列交互通过代码粘合在一起，依赖LLM解释输入或生成输出。
• destedexplan的观点: 认为定义不重要，"who cares"。
• tiffanyh的观点: 质疑"代表服务的代理是否算作代理"。
• Feathercrown的观点: 认为AI代理具有选择何时行动的能力。
• whiddershins的观点: 认为"AI代理"是一个没有明确意义的术语，争论其定义没有意义，它可以是任何有助于设计或解释事物的定义。

补充讨论：
• DonHopkins分享了一个关于Cursor AI系统频繁出现幻觉（hallucination）的实际案例，展示了AI代理在实际应用中可能出现的问题，强调了AI系统在操作过程中可能带来的困扰和挑战。

争议焦点：
• AI代理的定义：不同参与者对AI代理的定义有不同理解，主要争议在于代理是否需要自主性、是否需要以自己的身份执行操作，以及代理与工作流之间的区别。
• 实际应用中的问题：DonHopkins分享的案例展示了AI系统在实际应用中可能出现的问题，如幻觉现象，这引发了对AI代理在实际应用中的可靠性和可用性的讨论。

总结：
讨论围绕AI代理的定义展开，参与者从不同角度提出了各自的看法，包括技术实现、哲学思考和实际应用中的问题。争议的焦点在于如何定义AI代理，特别是在自主性和执行身份方面的理解差异。同时，实际应用中AI系统出现的问题也被提出，显示出理论定义与实际应用之间的差距。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕博尔赫斯的作品及其与人工智能（LLM）关系的讨论

不同观点：
• [viccis] 推荐博尔赫斯的作品，尤其是《特隆、乌克巴尔、奥尔比斯·特蒂乌斯》和《迷宫》，并提到目前英语最佳版本是《企鹅现代作家全集》。他还讨论了博尔赫斯与LLM（大型语言模型）的关系，认为即使拥有博尔赫斯的全部阅读和感官数据，也无法创造出博尔赫斯式的先验知识，因为这涉及到康德的认识论问题。

• [karaterobot] 对LLM能否通过深入理解博尔赫斯的生活来重现其作品表示好奇，并认为这是一个有趣的创意故事，或许未来LLM可以实现这一点。

• [101008] 推荐博尔赫斯，但认为其英文翻译缺乏原作的诗意和音乐性，庆幸自己的母语是西班牙语。

• [kouru225] 推荐博尔赫斯的短篇小说《博闻强记的富内斯》，并分享了链接。

• [jhbadger] 对网站使用的图片实际上是克劳德·香农表示困惑，并提供了相关链接。

• [tekacs] 推荐了一篇关于博尔赫斯与人工智能的论文，并提供了链接。

• [jl6] 提到霍夫斯塔特应该写一本关于博尔赫斯的书，并分享了自己关于博尔赫斯与AI等主题的写作链接。

• [david_shi] 引用了博尔赫斯的《阿莱夫》中的一段文字，展示了博尔赫斯作品中的深邃意象。

• [netsharc] 认为博尔赫斯的故事有时像是在报告某种假设情境，如果这篇讨论是对博尔赫斯的致敬，那将非常有趣。

• [6stringmerc] 提到在狱中阅读萨特的《存在与虚无》，认为LLM若经过萨特作品的训练，可能会产生令人不安的逻辑推论，反映人类思想和行为的不完美状态。

• [integralof5y] 认为博尔赫斯和赫伯特·西蒙都是伟大的思想家，但他们关于人类与机器智能的对话并不深入，LLM为我们提供了探索智能与语言关系的新工具。

补充讨论：
• [mentalgear] 询问是否有该访谈的音频文件，表示更喜欢听原版内容。

争议焦点：
• 博尔赫斯作品能否通过LLM重现：[viccis]和[karaterobot]对此持不同意见，前者认为即使拥有数据也无法重现博尔赫斯的先验知识，而后者则认为这是一个有趣的潜在发展。

• 翻译问题：[101008] 认为博尔赫斯的英文翻译缺乏原作的诗意和音乐性，这引发了对翻译质量的讨论。

• 博尔赫斯与人工智能的关系：[tekacs]和[jl6]提供了相关论文和链接，扩展了博尔赫斯作品与现代AI技术的联系。

• 访谈图片错误：[jhbadger] 指出了网站图片的错误，并提供了相关链接，这涉及到对历史人物的正确识别问题。

这些讨论展示了博尔赫斯作品的多重维度和其在现代技术背景下的新意义。

data.title: Vets Who Code
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: VetsWhoCode是一个由退伍军人和军属创立的非营利组织，致力于通过高质量、AI驱动的软件工程培训项目，帮助退伍军人和军属顺利转型进入科技行业。该组织提供免费的远程学习课程，着重培养实战技能，并由导师指导解决实际问题。其课程紧跟行业趋势，提供个性化辅导和终身社区支持。该项目已帮助超过300名退伍军人和军属实现职业转型，累计创造超过2000万美元的收入。多位学员反馈该项目对其职业发展产生了重大积极影响，如成功转型到微软和GitHub等科技公司。VetsWhoCode注重实际就业成果，旨在为退伍军人打开通向科技行业的大门。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于"vet"一词的多重含义以及相关项目和网站的反馈和建议

不同观点：
• [ash_091] 指出在其国家中，"vet"通常专指"veterinarian"（兽医），因此网站上的用法让他感到困惑。
• [freedomben] 是一位有20年编程经验的退伍军人（vet），对成为导师感兴趣，但网站未明确导师的职责和时间承诺，如1对1会议的频率和时长。
• [torstenvl] 和 [oerdier] 都提到网站的用户体验问题，特别是移动端导航栏过大以及动画导致页面跳动，影响阅读。
• [awslattery] 作为一位积极参与退伍军人编程活动的导师，指出网站在时间承诺、活动注册和支持等方面缺乏信息，并提到个人时间管理的困难。
• [the__alchemist] 认为美国政府和军队应更重视内部编程工作，而不是过度依赖外包。
• [pyjarrett] 推荐American Corporate Partners作为退伍军人进入软件开发等领域的资源。
• [beAbU] 简单指出"vet"在这里指的是退伍军人，而非兽医。
• [redeux] 对网站内容中大量依赖AI生成表示担忧，认为这可能影响教育质量，并指出AI内容需要人工评估和改进。
• [kwertyoowiyop] 提到网站的邮件地址缺少城市、州或邮编信息。
• [the_real_cher] 认为兽医和技术的结合可能是有益的，暗示兽医背景的人参与技术工作有潜力。

补充讨论：
• 网站的用户体验问题，特别是移动端导航和动画效果，是多个评论者关注的焦点。
• 关于"vet"一词的多重含义（退伍军人 vs 兽医）引起了困惑，需要澄清。
• 网站对导师的职责和时间承诺缺乏详细信息，影响了潜在导师的参与意愿。
• 对AI生成内容的担忧反映了对教育质量的关注，强调了人工评估和改进的必要性。
• 提供了一些额外的资源和支持渠道，如Vets Who Code和American Corporate Partners。

• 关于"vet"一词的多重含义（退伍军人 vs 兽医）引起了困惑，需要澄清。

data.title: Dipping my toes in OpenBSD, in Amsterdam
data.author: DJHenk
data.article_summary:
本文讲述了作者尝试在古董笔记本电脑（Toshiba 300 CDT）上安装各种操作系统，最终只有OpenBSD成功运行。这台1998年发布的笔记本内存仅32MB，运行现代系统非常困难。作者最初尝试了多种Linux发行版和其它操作系统，均失败。最终，OpenBSD成功启动并运行，尽管由于硬件限制和安全性设置，使用过程缓慢且具有挑战性。

作者提到，OpenBSD因其简约和安全性备受推崇，但学习曲线陡峭。在尝试配置和使用过程中遇到了许多困难，例如权限问题和配置文件错误。作者还对比了现代公司繁琐的客户验证流程，赞赏OpenBSD.Amsterdam提供的虚拟机服务，支持OpenBSD开发且操作直接、无繁琐手续。

最终，作者再次尝试OpenBSD，感受到其文档和专注于创建可靠系统的优点，尽管使用过程中仍遇到配置问题。

Dipping my toes in OpenBSD, in Amsterdam
March 31, 2025
Sometimes the water is cold at first.
$

A couple of years ago, I was playing with an ancient laptop, a
Toshiba 300 CDT
. I can't remember exactly, but I believe it had an internal memory of 32 MB. Sources on the internet differ on the exact specification, perhaps there were different models, but we are definitely talking about megabytes, not gigabytes. I was wondering whether it would be possible to get such an old device connected to the internet securely and do "something real" with it. Could it still be useful in some way, however limited? It was released in 1998. Back then, people had to-do lists. They were using word processors, and they went online to visit websites. Why wouldn't that still be possible?
I started by looking into several small Linux distributions, like
Damn Small Linux
and
Puppy Linux
. Unfortunately, those proved to be too much for this old machine. I started a half-hearted attempt to do
Linux From Scratch
, figuring that that would be the most basic and minimal Linux possible. But that turned into a whole project in itself, and I got distracted by other kinds of OSes. I tried
Haiku
,
Minix
and many, many more. This list is just what pops up in my head now, years later. Naturally, I got to
the BSDs
as well, but all to no avail. Nothing would work on this ancient laptop, the limited memory being the culprit most of the time.
Well, nothing except
OpenBSD
. Installing and seeing it boot was a puzzling moment. After all the failures, this one simply... just worked? Funny. I just wanted something to play with, but because I was going to connect it to the internet, I wanted something secure and supported. And then the only OS that worked was the one people keep bringing up as the most secure OS available. That probably says something about the virtues of simplicity and minimalism.
I did not use it very long, though. It took 15 minutes to boot, thanks to
one of the security features
. I could likely have disabled that, but learning OpenBSD turned out to be a challenge. For a Linux user, it all looks so familiar. Yet, it is different enough that I just kept stumbling around and got nowhere.
$
pkg_add helix
pkg_add:
pkg_add must be run as root
$
doas pkg_add helix
doas:
doas is not enabled, /etc/doas.conf: No such file or directory
Learning can be difficult. Learning is taking in something new and giving that a place in the model of the world that you already have. To connect the new thing to the things you already know. If it is truly new, that might prove to be difficult. There is no obvious place in your mental model to put the new thing.
You may think you are open-minded, that you are flexible enough to learn new things, but often that only means that you are ready for square pegs of various new sizes. What happens if you encounter a round one? It may take several failed attempts before the concept of roundness even emerges in your head.
$
doas rcctl restart relayd
(
failed
)
Sometimes you are the round peg. Take the term KYC. It stands for Know Your Customer, and it means that organizations must take steps to make sure you, a potential customer, are not a fraudster. They are required by law to learn who you are, so they can determine if it is okay to start a business relationship with you.
For me, getting to know someone simply means talking to them. Preferably over some beer or coffee. For many companies, "getting to know you" nowadays means asking you to stare into your webcam so that an AI can take a good look at you. Or to submit a scan of your passport, that they promise to process securely because your privacy is very, very important to them. Somehow, I never believe it when they say that.
When I started looking for a new way to host this site because I was done playing around at
the previous hoster
, and now wanted something simple and stable, I encountered many of those companies that wanted to get to know me in the most awkward way possible. These days, buying European is all the rage, but European companies are just the same. Soulless websites with forms that require intimate information. They really, really value my pri...  yeah, right.
But then I stumbled upon
OpenBSD.Amsterdam
. A local offering of OpenBSD VMs. The organization pledges to use part of the money they charge for sponsoring the development of OpenBSD, which is cool. It felt no-nonsense and rock solid, like the OS itself. I have never met the people behind it, but I bet they like coffee, or beer.
$
doas relayd
-n
/etc/relayd.conf:37:
cannot load keypair ewintr.nl for relay www4tls
/etc/relayd.conf:45:
cannot load keypair ewintr.nl for relay www6tls
no
actions, nothing to do
OpenBSD, there it is again. Remembering my earlier experience with the old laptop, I figured I needed to give it another try. After all, besides security, enthusiasts always keep raving about the documentation and the focus on creating a

data.title: PaperBench
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对LLM（大型语言模型）评估和PaperBench基准测试的讨论

不同观点：
• **[no_multitudes]** 对测试结果的质量提出质疑。认为论文或代码中缺乏具体的输出示例，仅仅给出LLM对其他模型代码的评分（如21%）并不具有定性意义。
  
• **[smusamashah]** 提供了具体的测试结果，指出表现最好的模型Claude 3.5 Sonnet在PaperBench上的平均复制得分为21.0%，支持了该基准测试工具的有效性。

• **[tetris11]** 对该项目的归属权表示担忧，认为由营利性公司主导可能存在利益冲突，尤其在AI竞赛中拥有巨大利益的公司。

• **[amelius]** 对AI辅助阅读论文的用户界面（UI）表示兴趣，认为这是一个值得发展的方向，而不是仅仅关注代码复现。

• **[timabdulla]** 对人类专家的表现提出疑问，认为如果是顶尖的博士生，应该能在超过48小时的努力后接近100%地复制论文结果。

• **[DrillShopper]** 误解了PaperBench的用途，认为它类似于GPU基准测试软件，表明对该工具的定位存在不同认知。

• **[riku_iki]** 质疑基准测试的目标，不明白为什么在已有GitHub代码的情况下，还需要重新生成代码来复制论文结果。

• **[antonkar]** 提出了一个全球性的AI安全解决方案，建议将所有GPU集中到由国际科学家控制的云端，以防止AI被不法分子利用。这一观点虽然与主讨论点不完全相关，但涉及到了AI安全和风险管理。

补充讨论：
• **关于结果的透明性和质量**：no_multitudes和smusamashah的观点形成了对比，前者质疑结果的定性意义，后者提供了具体数据支持测试有效性。
  
• **关于项目主导权和利益冲突**：tetris11的观点提出了对营利性公司主导科研项目的担忧，引发了对科研公正性和独立性的讨论。

• **关于人类专家能力的假设**：timabdulla对人类专家的高期望与实际测试结果可能存在的差距，值得进一步探讨。

• **关于AI安全和全球治理**：antonkar的观点虽然偏离主讨论点，但引出了一个重要话题，即AI安全在全球范围内的风险和解决方案。

以上观点涵盖了对LLM评估方法的质疑、对项目主导权的担忧、对人类专家能力的讨论以及对AI安全的全球性建议。

data.title: Hacking the call records of millions of Americans
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary:
文章揭示了Verizon Call Filter iOS应用中的一个安全漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者获取Verizon无线用户的通话记录，包括来电号码和时间戳，而无需设备入侵或密码猜测。漏洞的关键在于，应用在请求通话记录时，服务器未验证请求的电话号码是否与登录用户匹配。攻击者只需修改请求中的电话号码，即可获取其他用户的通话历史。

此漏洞不仅侵犯隐私，还可能对特定人群如家暴幸存者、执法人员和公众人物构成安全威胁。通话元数据可用于重建个人日常活动、识别频繁联系人，并推断私人关系。时间戳与其他信息结合，可能暴露个人行踪和私密联系方式。

技术上，问题出在应用使用的一个未适当验证用户身份的API端点。该漏洞可能影响所有或绝大多数Verizon用户，因其Call Filter服务可能默认开启。这一漏洞不仅导致大量用户信息泄露，还可能被用作实时监控工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Verizon电话号码及通话记录数据泄露的安全漏洞及其影响

不同观点：
• [twalkz] 指出Verizon的服务器未能验证请求的电话号码是否与登录用户绑定，导致用户可以修改请求的电话号码，获取与其他Verizon用户相关的数据。他认为这是Verizon的一个重大疏忽，并希望公司在披露漏洞时能告知此前是否有其他人利用过该漏洞。

• [dotty-] 提到Verizon Call Filter应用使用了一个看起来非常内部化的域名来查询用户通话记录，暗示这种命名方式可能反映出安全措施不到位。

• [devmtk] 对Verizon这样的大公司出现这种低级错误感到震惊，质疑公司的渗透测试和安全责任人，并担心是否有其他数据泄露的风险。

• [adxl] 提出疑问，如何才能像发现此类漏洞的人一样找到新的安全漏洞，并建议通过逆向工程应用或监控请求来寻找漏洞，以参与漏洞赏金计划。

• [vivzkestrel] 好奇如何能发现这些漏洞，询问是否需要全职从事这种工作，或者是否可以通过系统化的方式找到未被发现的漏洞。

• [chatmasta] 指出通话记录通常会打印在每月的账单上，并可能包含短信记录，认为这些数据可能已经广泛泄露到公司内外部的多个系统中，暗示该漏洞只是冰山一角。

• [grg0] 质疑为什么这一事件没有成为新闻头条，认为政府通常夸大外国势力对公民的干扰，但对公司漏洞却视而不见，暗示大公司对媒体和国会的控制。

43558550.article_content:
Hacking the Call Records of Millions of Americans
Imagine if anyone could punch in a phone number from the largest U.S. cell carrier and instantly retrieve a list of its recent incoming calls—complete with timestamps—without compromising the device, guessing a password, or alerting the user.
Now imagine that number belongs to a journalist, a police officer, a politician, or someone fleeing an abuser.
This capability wasn’t a hypothetical.
I recently identified a security vulnerability in the
Verizon Call Filter iOS app
which made it possible for an attacker to leak call history logs of Verizon Wireless customers.
Call logs can be quite valuable, especially for nation states, as recently noted in coverage of the Salt Typhoon breach of telecom networks:
https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/25/us/politics/trump-vance-hack.html
Given that this data is of such value, you’d expect that both how it’s accessed, and who is given access would be closely guarded. However, as I found, this may not be the case.
High level overview:
In order to display your recent history of received calls in the Verizon Call Filter app, a network request is made to a server. That request contains various details such as your phone number and the requested time period for call records. The server then responds with a list of calls and timestamps for each.
So surely the server validated that the phone number being requested was tied to the signed in user? Right? Right?? Well…no. It was possible to modify the phone number being sent, and then receive data back for Verizon numbers not associated with the signed in user.
In short, anyone could lookup data for anyone.
This is of course a privacy concern for all. But for some this could also represent a safety concern.
Consider scenarios involving survivors of domestic abuse, law enforcement officers, or public figures—individuals who rely on the confidentiality of their communication patterns. Having their incoming call logs exposed is not just invasive; it’s dangerous.
Call metadata might seem harmless, but in the wrong hands, it becomes a powerful surveillance tool. With unrestricted access to another user’s call history, an attacker could reconstruct daily routines, identify frequent contacts, and infer personal relationships.
Timestamps can be cross-referenced with social media or public sightings to map physical movements. Repeated numbers expose private or burner lines, compromising whistleblowers, journalists, or abuse survivors.
This wasn’t just a data leak. It was a real-time surveillance mechanism waiting to be abused.
Technical details:
The Verizon Call Filter app uses the endpoint
https://clr-aqx.cequintvzwecid.com/clr/callLogRetrieval
to lookup call history for the authenticated user and display it in the app.
This endpoint requires a JWT (JSON Web Token) in the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme and uses an
X-Ceq-MDN
header to specify a cell phone number to retrieve call history logs for.
A JWT has three parts: header, payload, and signature. It’s often used for authentication and authorization in web apps.
The payload in this case looked like:
{
"sub"
:
"SIGNED_IN_USER_PHONE_NUMBER_HERE"
,
"iat"
:
"1740253712"
,
"iss"
:
"df88f1ed1dfd9a903e4c8dca7f00089e134c6c4e0a566cd565147ba1dadf78a6"
,
"secret"
:
"REDACTED"
,
"alg"
:
"ECDSA-256"
,
"exp"
:
"1740255512"
}
sub
stands for subject — it identifies who the token is about (usually the user ID). In this case that is a phone number of the signed in user.
What should have been happening, and did seem to take place on other endpoints for additional app functionality, is that the server would compare the phone number specified in the request to the user identifier (sub) in the JWT, to ensure that the user requesting the information should have access to it.
However, the
/clr/callLogRetrieval
endpoint was not validating that the phone number specified in the
X-Ceq-MDN
header matches the
sub
in the JWT payload, meaning it was possible to lookup call history logs for any phone number within the application by passing the desired phone number in the value of that header.
Example Vulnerable Request:
The issue I discovered impacted at least those who have the Verizon Call Filter service enabled (I did not test a number which had it disabled; I can’t rule out whether or not all Verizon numbers could have been impacted).
Based on
https://www.verizon.com/support/call-filter-faqs/
and
https://www.verizon.com/about/news/verizon-helps-customers-avoid-15-billion-robocalls
I believe this service may be on by default for many/all Verizon Wireless customers, so in either case, it does seem this issue impacted either nearly all, or all customers.
While this endpoint
only
returned received calls for the specified phone number, I don’t believe that to be a major limitation on impact. For one, that’s still an immense amount of information. But also, for a targeted individual, this could stretch into a partial picture of outgoing calls as well, provided
43558550.article_summary:
文章揭示了Verizon Call Filter iOS应用中的一个安全漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者获取Verizon无线用户的通话记录，包括来电号码和时间戳，而无需设备入侵或密码猜测。漏洞的关键在于，应用在请求通话记录时，服务器未验证请求的电话号码是否与登录用户匹配。攻击者只需修改请求中的电话号码，即可获取其他用户的通话历史。

此漏洞不仅侵犯隐私，还可能对特定人群如家暴幸存者、执法人员和公众人物构成安全威胁。通话元数据可用于重建个人日常活动、识别频繁联系人，并推断私人关系。时间戳与其他信息结合，可能暴露个人行踪和私密联系方式。

技术上，问题出在应用使用的一个未适当验证用户身份的API端点。该漏洞可能影响所有或绝大多数Verizon用户，因其Call Filter服务可能默认开启。这一漏洞不仅导致大量用户信息泄露，还可能被用作实时监控工具。

data.title: Ace: Realtime Computer Autopilot
data.author: huerne
data.article_summary: Ace是一个计算机自动驾驶仪，能够使用鼠标和键盘执行桌面任务。它在计算机任务上表现优于其他模型，相关模型和任务套件已开源。Ace通过屏幕和提示执行操作，由专家团队训练，已完成超过一百万次任务。尽管Ace速度极快，但仍可能出错，随着训练资源的增加，其智能和能力将不断提升。目前，Ace的早期研究预览版已发布，邀请用户参与试用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLM）在处理复杂任务（如预订旅行）时的能力和局限性，以及用户对LLM应用的期望与现实之间的差距。

不同观点：
• joshstrange：对LLM在处理复杂任务（如自动预订旅行）时的能力持怀疑态度。他认为当前的LLM无法处理所有必要的情况，特别是在需要综合考虑多个因素（如费用、位置、价格和设施）时。他批评了LLM社区中常见的“随着时间推移，模型会变得更好”的乐观态度，指出LLM问题的解决并不像传统软件问题那样简单，且训练和调整模型的过程耗时且昂贵。他还提到自己不愿意依赖此类系统，因为担心出错的风险。
• vivzkestrel：分享了一篇题为“反对对话界面的案例”的文章链接，暗示对对话式界面的质疑。
• iamleppert：对招聘用例表示幽默回应，表明对某些应用场景的娱乐性。
• the__alchemist：表示对帖子内容与标题预期不符的惊讶。
• sherjilozair：作为General Agents的创始人兼CEO，表示愿意回答问题，展示了对讨论的开放态度。
• lilyhills03 和 cbiscuit：对帖子内容表示兴奋和支持。
• misbah143：对LLM和计算机代理的未来持乐观态度，认为其发展迅速且前景广阔。

补充讨论：
• joshstrange详细描述了LLM在处理实际任务（如预订旅行）时的不足，包括无法处理所有必要的情况、输出结果看似合理但不准确或完整，以及训练和调整模型的困难。
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在处理复杂任务时的实际能力和用户的期望之间的差距。joshstrange对当前LLM的能力持怀疑态度，而misbah143则对LLM的未来持乐观态度。
• vivzkestrel分享的文章链接可能提供了对对话式界面的进一步批评，值得进一步阅读和讨论。

总体而言，讨论涉及了对LLM当前能力的质疑、对未来发展的不同预期以及对具体应用场景的幽默和支持。

data.title: Item Flow, Part 1: A new unified concept for layout
data.author: ulrischa
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种新的统一布局概念——"Item Flow"，旨在合并CSS中的Flexbox和Grid布局系统，同时解决“瀑布”（masonry）布局问题。当前，Flexbox和Grid无法完全实现一些设计师期望的布局效果，比如瀑布布局，仍需借助JavaScript库。文章提出了一种新的属性系统，名为"item-flow"，包含四个子属性："item-direction"（内容流向）、"item-wrap"（换行控制）、"item-pack"（密集排列）和"item-slack"（布局松弛控制）。这种新系统旨在统一和扩展布局能力，使Flexbox和Grid具备更多功能，如Flexbox的密集排列和Grid的关闭换行功能。文章邀请开发者社区对这一新概念提出意见，并表示将在后续文章中进一步探讨其对未来布局的影响。

• **CSS已经功能完备**：用户[ericyd]认为CSS已经功能完备，对目前CSS的能力感到满意，并表示不对难以实现的功能感到困扰，反映了一部分开发者对CSS现状的满足感。

• **CSS Grid的能力争议**：用户[mediumsmart]指出CSS Grid已经可以实现类似masonry布局的功能，所谓的不足实际上是想要一种“shuffle feature”（洗牌功能），表明对CSS Grid的能力有不同的理解和期望。

• **对过去CSS语法的不满**：用户[gedy]对过去CSS语法的不一致性感到不满，但对新的改进感到满意，表明对CSS语法一致性和易用性的关注。

• 争议焦点之一是CSS的功能是否足够完备以及是否需要进一步扩展。例如，[ericyd]和[mediumsmart]对CSS Grid能力的看法不同。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对CSS语法简化和标准化的不同看法，部分用户如[andrewstuart]希望减少简写和别名，而[codeflo]则期待更简化的工具如Tailwind。

43559986.article_content:
Item Flow, Part 1:
A new unified concept for layout
Mar 28, 2025
by
Jen Simmons, Saron Yitbarek, Elika Etemad, Brandon Stewart
Contents
Combining Flexbox and Grid
Item Direction
Item Wrap
Item Pack
Item slack
The Overall Plan
What do you think?
CSS Grid and Flexbox brought incredible layout tools to the web, but they don’t yet do everything a designer might want. One of those things is a popular layout pattern called “masonry” or “waterfall,” which currently still requires
a Javascript library
to accomplish.
Masonry layouts in CSS feature was first proposed by Mozilla and implemented in Firefox behind a flag
in 2020
. From the beginning, there’s been a hot debate about this mechanism. The WebKit team at Apple picked up where Mozilla left off, implemented the drafted spec, and landed it in
Safari Technology Preview 163
. This reinvigorated the conversation. By October 2024, there were two competing ideas being debated — to “Just Use Grid” or to create a whole “New Masonry Layout”.
We wrote extensively about these ideas
in a previous article on this website.
A lot has happened since October. Now, a third path forward is emerging — a path that would mean the CSS Working Group doesn’t choose either “Just Use Grid” or “New Masonry Layout”. It merges ideas from both with a completely-new idea to create a unified system of Item Flow properties. This article explains what Item Flow is, and its impact on both Flexbox and Grid. In Part 2, another article will more fully explain the implications for the future of masonry-style layouts.
But first, why is a third possibility called Item Flow emerging at all? Why not just pick between the “Just Use Grid” and “New Masonry Layout” options? Well, back in October, the folks working on masonry
asked the W3C Technical Architecture Group (TAG) to weigh in
on the debate. The TAG had
a lengthy response
, but one of the most interesting parts was this:
Overall, we think masonry, grid, and wrapping-flexbox should be incorporated into a unified set of properties. Chrome’s [New Masonry Layout] proposal splits apart property sets too eagerly, but even the WebKit [originally Mozilla | Just Use Grid] proposal seems to miss a chance to develop more-general properties.
Wow. Incorporate Flexbox, Grid and Masonry into a unified set of properties? What would that even look like?
The suggestion isn’t to combine all of Flexbox with all of Grid — but rather to create a new set of properties and values to “replace” specifically the
flex-flow
and
grid-auto-flow
properties. (You will always be able to use the older syntax if you prefer.) Think how originally the
Alignment properties
and the
gap
property were defined to work only in one layout system, and then later got modified and extended to work in multiple layout contexts.
Several of us here at Apple got together and started figuring out how a such unified system for layout
*-flow
could work. We decided to tentatively name the shorthand
item-flow
. It’d be the main property from which the longhands and values follow. Together, the new rules would all control the direction of flow, how items wrap, how items pack, whether or not there’s “slack” in the layout, and more.
As we worked through the details, we started to get excited. Suddenly new features for Flexbox and Grid that people have wanted for years had an obvious home. Things seemed to click together elegantly. New capabilities emerged:
Flexbox could gain a way to do dense packing
Grid could gain the ability to turn off wrapping
Masonry layouts could now be triggered with a value for
item-flow
and more…
In this article, we want to describe Item Flow to you, the people who make websites and web apps, to see what you think. So, let’s go on a journey to imagine what this future would be like…
Combining Flexbox and Grid
Flexbox has
flex-flow
. It’s a
shorthand
for these two longhands:
flex-direction: row | row-reverse | column | column-reverse;
flex-wrap: nowrap | wrap | wrap-reverse;
Flex-direction determines which direction the content flows, while flex-wrap determines whether or not to wrap content.
CSS Grid has
grid-auto-flow
.
grid-auto-flow: row | column | dense;
It determines the direction in which the content flows, and whether or not dense packing is used, all in one property. It has no longhands.
So how shall we unify these capabilities? We proposed calling the new shorthand
item-flow
, with four new longhands:
item-direction
item-wrap
item-pack
item-slack
(It’s important to note all of these are brand new, baby fresh ideas. They will get discussed at length and changed before they become reality in browsers. To make this article readable, we are glossing over the current debates and presenting just one name for each property/value, not listing the all the variations proposed at the CSSWG.)
Item Direction
The
item-direction
property would determine how content flows. Should content flow in rows or columns? In the normal direction or reversed? This would work just like
flex-direction

data.title: Windows on ARM on a Smart Watch
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Google Pixel Watch 3上运行Windows on ARM的项目。作者详细描述了硬件配置，包括Snapdragon W5 Gen 1芯片、2GB RAM、32GB存储以及高分辨率OLED屏幕。通过解锁引导加载程序并利用UEFI，作者成功将Windows和Linux引导到这款智能手表上。文章还提到，该项目利用了Qualcomm的开源代码和固件，并经历了繁琐的补丁和调整过程。最终，作者实现了在智能手表上运行Windows的实验性成果，展示了智能手表作为一种潜力巨大的设备，可以替代部分手机功能。项目详情和代码可参考WOA-Project的Github页面。

TL;DR:
Pixel Watch Guides on WOA-Project Github organisation
Also there is a section at the bottom outlining other things I am releasing at the end of this week. Scroll down if you do not care about the time 😉
Many years of spending, sorry, losing time making Windows on ARM run on anything not a computer, I started getting bored
What could be the next project really? Years of wondering about, diverging into
foldables out of all things
, I still couldnt let go of my head that something else could be done, something more, evident, something more stupid, sorry, something more useful. Something I had not figured out yet. Thousands of hours rambling online, including with
old people
, I still couldnt work it out...
...and then it came to me
The answer was ALWAYS under my eyes. Yes! Making windows run
on an ARM
! To be more exact, on a
smartwatch
How did I never think of this before!
And so can you! Yes, for real, see
Pixel Watch Guides on WOA-Project Github organisation

Quad core sixty four bits ARM Cortex A53 cluster
2 whole GBs of DDR4X RAM
32GB of eMMC storage
Adreno 702 Graphics (this thing even has raytracing!) clocked at a whoping 1Ghz (perfect for gaming on the go!)
456x456 OLED Coated Curved (fancy! not even phones do that anymore) and ✨ Rounded ✨ display (wow!)
More rounded than your iPhone
Ultra high speed LTE modem onboard (on some models only)
USB. Yes, your charger does USB
Audio

Calling support
it texts
Ultra advanced Sensor Hub (good for your health) (the writer of this post def needs to get help in that area)

can touch this, world first circular touch screen
it smol
cute
its a freaking watch
has all the functionality you have on your phone. So why wasting your time on phones, get watch, watch is the superior technology, not fish
Getting Windows to run on your ARM
Now that the story line is laid out (see above), let's get a victim, sorry, test subject (we will pretend for the sake of the writer sanity this whole thing did not start just because of the Windows on ARM pun)
Chosen was the
Google Pixel Watch 3 (Large LTE Model)
that came out late last year, notably because thats what I had, and also because it featured everything my 2 grand USD phone had, for only a quarter of the price (I did tell you why are we bothering with expensive phones)
The watch runs on Android 15 (originally Android 14 but more on that later), has an unlockable bootloader, and unfortunately features Google conception of reinventing how to boot linux yearly (more on that later too)
My newly obtained watch on the very first day of ownership, doing what every single normal user would do, mess with it
The watch uses a Snapdragon W5 Gen 1 (Part number SW5100) combined with 2GB of DDR4X ram on 32GB of eMMC storage
This is more than enough for a smartwatch, let's face it, but also enough for us. It using a Qualcomm chipset means i could reuse all my experience messing with previous hardware using Qualcomm chipsets easily and tap onto easily accessible opensource code repos (including, Google own)
As a modern Qualcomm platform, roughly based on Kona era firmware (Kona is the Snapdragon 865), it also is familiar territory for the firmware side of things.
Image Credit: Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
The SoC is also making use of
old but proven
Cortex-A53 cores, 4 of them to be exact. This is a bit on the older side (Cortex A53 was designed back in 2011) and wont run modern OSes needing atomics, but this is enough for our fun experiments here.
Modern Qualcomm firmware, means we are already dealing with an UEFI here, in XBL (Qualcomm own eXtensible Boot Loader). So armed with the watch of all of this knowledge the very first step has been to backup the watch using a rooted boot image, and inspect.
This is not fun
Then doing the very same steps of, painfully taking back all EFI files from the stock uefi, and adapting them to run in my own UEFI environment. We suddenly, are in UEFI land.
After hours of patching and figuring out correct load order (apriori was all wrong somehow) we are at a shell!

data.title: MIT 6.5950 Secure Hardware Design – An open-source course on hardware attacks
data.author: imakwana
data.article_summary: MIT的“安全硬件设计”课程（6.5950/6.5951）是一门开源课程，旨在教授学生如何攻击现代CPU以及设计抵御这些攻击的架构。课程包括动手实验，学生可以实际操作真实处理器，学习各种先进的硬件攻击和防御方法。课程围绕“思考、游戏、实践”三大理念设计，通过讲座、复习课和实验三个环节实现。讲座侧重于关键思考和研究文献的探讨，内容涵盖微架构攻击、侧信道攻击、瞬态执行攻击（如Spectre、Meltdown）、物理安全等。复习课采用互动游戏形式，如Capture-the-Flag（CTF）竞赛。实验课则让学生在真实硬件上实现攻击，如缓存侧信道攻击、Rowhammer攻击等。所有课程材料均为开源，供其他教师使用，但需事先联系获取指导方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕硬件安全、在线课程及其相关趋势的讨论

不同观点：

• **oytis** 的观点：提出一个与主话题不太相关的观察，认为现在很多知名大学在网上发布的课程材料，其授课教师似乎越来越年轻。他质疑这是否反映了教师年龄结构的变化，还是年轻教师更倾向于将课程放到网上，或者只是他随着年龄增长感知发生了变化。

• **klop1** 的观点：回应oytis，表示自己曾经学习过这些在线课程，并从中获益匪浅，对课程团队表示感谢。klop1支持将课程公开化的做法，认为这对学习者非常有帮助。

43562109.article_content:
Secure Hardware Design
MIT’s Secure Hardware Design Class (6.5950/6.5951) is an open-source course that teaches students both how to attack modern CPUs and design architectures resilient to those attacks. Students gain hands-on experience hacking real processors and are taught various state-of-the-art hardware attacks and defenses.
This course is the culmination of multiple years of work.
Browse our story here
.
Meet the Team
Secure Hardware Design is the culmination of years of effort by a team of students. Say “hello” to the people behind it!
Think, Play, Do.
Our course philosophy involves three pillars- Think, Play, Do.‍
Think
In Lecture, we encourage students to think critically about hardware security as a part of greater systems. Our lectures are designed to guide critical thinking and engagement with the research literature.
Topic
Lecture Materials
Microarchitectural Attacks
Side channels introduction 🔨
Cache side channel deep dive 🔨
Transient execution attacks (Spectre, Meltdown)
Side channel defenses
Physical security
Hardware Security Modules (HSM)
Physical Attacks (Power analysis, EM, fault injection) 🔨
Rowhammer
Hardware support for software security
Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)
Memory safety mechanisms 🔨
Tools for security assurance
Fuzzing, formal verification 🔨
The 🔨 icon means this lecture features an in-class demo.
Please send requests for powerpoint files to
Mengjia
.
Play
In Recitation, we encourage students to play with the course materials through interactive hands-on games. Our recitations consist of interactive learning sessions, leveraging the Capture-the-Flag (CTF) format for friendly competitions amongst students. Students team up and work with their peers to conquer various challenges together.‍
Topic
Content
Format
C/C++ Recitation
A brief refresher on C/ C++ syntax and useful features.
CTF
Cache Attack Recitation
A visual overview of prime+probe on a custom RISC-V CPU.
Group Learning
Physical Attacks Recitation
Students work together to implement a timing side channel against real microcontrollers.
CTF
RISC-V System Programming Recitation
Overview of the privileged ISA specification for RISC-V with emphasis on exception handling and interrupt conditions.
CTF
Formal Verification Recitation
Students learn the basics of formal verification techniques.
Group Learning
Do
In Labs, students have a chance to actually put the concepts from class to work. The attack labs involve implementing attacks taught in class on real hardware. No simulators, no trickery, no nonsense. Real implementations on real hardware.‍
“How can I use your materials in my class?”
Every year, we update our course to reflect the ever-changing landscape of research in the hardware security world. All of these labs are open-source and free to use. Just shoot us an email at
hw-sec-lab-dev
at mit dot edu before doing so, so we can give you the instructor’s solutions and starter gradebook. If you do use our materials in your class, make sure to attribute us on your class webpage.
Lab
Difficulty
Setup
Cache Side Channels
Hard
x86_64 Linux server. Some tuning required. We use Cascade Lake.
Spectre
Medium
x86_64 Linux server.
Website Fingerprinting
Easy
Any modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari).
Rowhammer
Hard
x86_64 Linux server. Some tuning to match your hardware required.
ASLR Bypasses
Easy
x86_64 Linux server.
CPU Fuzzing
Medium
x86_64 Linux server.
Cache Side Channels (Dead Drop)
Students start with building primitives to measure cache access latencies and examine microarchitecture details. Next, they will implement Prime+Probe on a modern cache hierarchy, requiring a thorough understanding of cache geometry. Finally, they implement a covert channel chat client, demonstrating mastery over creating contention on set associative structures.
Spectre
Students implement a Flush+Reload attack against shared memory between userspace and kernelspace. Then, they extend their attack to work under speculation in increasingly difficult exploitation scenarios to leak kernel memory back to userspace.
Website Fingerprinting
We start with teaching students to implement a cache occupancy attack using Javascript to profile different websites. Next, the students are guided to use machine learning to distinguish these websites based on their traces collected using JavaScripts. Finally, we ask the students to slightly change the attack and think about the root causes of the attack.
Rowhammer
Students learn the essential steps towards implementing Rowhammer in the wild. We guide the students to go through the two level address translation: virtual address -> physical address -> DRAM location. The students are first given the physical address of vulnerable rows and hammer rows and they will quickly see bit flips in the wild. Then the students are asked to reverse engineering some missing pieces of DRAM banking functions to search for unknown vulnerable rows.
ASLR Bypasses

data.title: Multi-Token Attention
data.author: fzliu
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种新的注意力机制——多 token 注意力（Multi-Token Attention, MTA），以解决传统注意力机制仅依赖单个查询和键 token 向量相似性的局限性。MTA 通过在查询、键和头之间应用卷积操作，使相邻的查询和键能够相互影响注意力权重，从而利用更丰富、更细致的信息来提升模型性能。实验表明，MTA 在多种基准测试中表现优异，尤其在需要处理长文本信息的任务中，优于传统的 Transformer 模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Transformer架构的改进及其在处理大上下文大小音频数据分类问题中的应用

不同观点：
• rakejake：尝试将MultiHeadAttention层引入到CNN中以替代GRU层，获得了比CNN-GRU混合模型更好的结果。虽然训练速度更快，但内存消耗较大。
• bionhoward：将该方法与Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) 进行比较，指出BLT在嵌入时使用注意力机制，而本文方法在嵌入后使用卷积。
• kouteiheika：指出该方法在实际应用中存在问题，尤其是对注意力机制的修改使其无法与Flash Attention等优化库兼容，且FlexAttention目前也存在较多bug。
• bigdict：质疑通过增加计算资源是否能真正提高性能，尤其是在每单位计算性能上的提升。
• bob1029：提出对注意力机制中查询和键的乘法增加可能会导致内存带宽瓶颈的问题。
• cgearhart：对引入局部窗口的必要性提出质疑，认为注意力机制原本就是为了解决长距离依赖问题，重新引入局部窗口似乎是倒退。
• curiousfiddler：质疑卷积方法是否能比多头注意力提取更多语义信息，并将其与CNN使用多种滤波器类比。
• fabmilo：认为应超越tokenization，认为当前在RL优化中的工作只是局部优化，呼吁更大突破。
• jwilber：支持卷积操作在LLM中的 comeback，提到最近使用conv-based hyena operator的striped hyena2架构的成功。
• antonkar：提出一种全球安全的AI解决方案，建议将GPU集中在云端由国际科学家控制，以防止AI被不当使用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论焦点之一是新方法是否能真正提高性能，尤其是在计算资源增加的情况下。
• 另一个焦点是新方法在实际应用中的可行性，尤其是与现有优化库的兼容性问题。
• 对局部窗口和长距离依赖的处理也是讨论的重要方面，部分评论者认为局部窗口可能会削弱注意力机制的优势。
• 有评论者提出应从更高层次上改进AI架构，而不仅仅是在现有框架上进行局部优化。

Title:
Multi-Token Attention
Authors:
Olga Golovneva
,
Tianlu Wang
,
Jason Weston
,
Sainbayar Sukhbaatar
View a PDF of the paper titled Multi-Token Attention, by Olga Golovneva and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Soft attention is a critical mechanism powering LLMs to locate relevant parts within a given context. However, individual attention weights are determined by the similarity of only a single query and key token vector. This "single token attention" bottlenecks the amount of information used in distinguishing a relevant part from the rest of the context. To address this issue, we propose a new attention method, Multi-Token Attention (MTA), which allows LLMs to condition their attention weights on multiple query and key vectors simultaneously. This is achieved by applying convolution operations over queries, keys and heads, allowing nearby queries and keys to affect each other's attention weights for more precise attention. As a result, our method can locate relevant context using richer, more nuanced information that can exceed a single vector's capacity. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that MTA achieves enhanced performance on a range of popular benchmarks. Notably, it outperforms Transformer baseline models on standard language modeling tasks, and on tasks that require searching for information within long contexts, where our method's ability to leverage richer information proves particularly beneficial.

data.title: Web Server for AoE 1, 2 and 3 DE supporting LAN multiplayer 100% offline
data.author: apitman
data.article_summary:
Age LAN Server 是一个支持《帝国时代》1、2、3决定版进行局域网（LAN）多人游戏的离线 web 服务器。它允许玩家在没有互联网连接的情况下进行游戏，即使官方服务器维护或关闭，LAN 功能仍可使用。该项目目前处于维护状态，仅修复错误和更新依赖项。要完全离线游玩，玩家需要自定义启动器来绕过游戏的联网限制，并可能使用 Steam 模拟器。

支持功能包括场景模式、地图传输、游戏恢复、模组支持、大厅聊天和跨平台联机（Steam 和 Xbox）。但也存在一些限制，如无法进行排名比赛、无法观战、好友列表显示所有在线用户等。此外，成就、排行榜、玩家数据等功能在离线模式下无法使用。

服务器最低系统要求包括 Windows 10、Linux kernel 2.6.32 及以上、macOS Big Sur 等，客户端则需对应游戏的特定版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：经典即时战略游戏《Age of Empires》（AoE）及其相关技术话题，包括游戏保存、网络对战方式、开源许可问题以及技术实现细节。

不同观点：
• Rendello推荐了一个免费的、类似于AoE的游戏0 A.D.，并附上了链接，认为该游戏对战略游戏爱好者具有吸引力。
• recycledmatt对游戏功能因服务器关闭而丢失表示遗憾，强调了游戏未来验证的重要性。
• apitman寻找通过互联网进行LAN游戏的最佳方案，提到了Hamachi和ZeroTier，倾向于开源解决方案，并对Tailscale不支持多播表示失望。
• red_admiral对AoE2在1999年发布并持续更新至2025年表示赞赏，认为其具有长久生命力。
• Seanambers回忆了2000年代LAN游戏的经历，提到游戏崩溃反而避免了失败，增加了乐趣。
• o1o1o1对Steam的便利性表示认可，但对其锁定效应表示担忧，并赞赏开源项目带来的自主权。
• abigail95质疑在AGPL许可下附加使用条款的合法性，认为这可能违反了许可证的规定。
• ziofill不确定是否需要拥有游戏副本才能玩0 A.D.，还是该游戏是独立的。
• LPisGood对AoE3的API文档是否公开表示好奇，并提到有人曾试图逆向工程。
• cheeseomlit讨论了AoE2 DE的多人游戏是否主要依赖于P2P，并提到了一些技术细节和社区争议。
• brink希望AoE2能像国际象棋一样长久存在，认为它是“完美”的游戏。
• typh00n分享了在LAN Party上尝试运行某游戏失败的经历，但表示愿意再次尝试。
• hoten对游戏的web服务器功能感到困惑，特别是其在匹配和广播方面的作用。
• CursedSilicon询问是否存在类似于《Diablo 2》和《Warcraft 3》的AoE游戏服务器项目。
• pjmlp对使用编译管理语言在游戏开发中的应用表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 玩家对经典游戏的持久性和技术细节有浓厚兴趣，特别是如何在现代环境下运行和保存这些游戏。
• 关于开源和许可证问题的讨论显示了社区对软件自由和自主权的关注。
• 技术实现细节，如P2P、服务器架构和API文档，是玩家和开发者之间的重要讨论点。
• 对LAN Party和网络对战的技术挑战和解决方案也是讨论的重点。

game modes without having an internet
connection

ensuring the game LAN functionality is still available even if the official
server

data.title: An open source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale control server
data.author: quyleanh
data.article_summary: Headscale 是一个开源、自托管的 Tailscale 控制服务器实现，专为自托管爱好者和小型开源组织设计。Tailscale 是一个基于 Wireguard 的现代 VPN，其控制服务器负责交换节点间的 Wireguard 公钥、分配 IP 地址、管理用户边界、共享机器以及暴露节点路由。Headscale 旨在提供一个单一的 Tailscale 网络（tailnet），适合个人或小型组织使用。项目文档提供了功能、客户端支持和运行指南等详细信息。开发者需使用 Go 和 Buf 工具，并遵循特定的代码风格和格式要求。项目与 Tailscale 公司无关，但有维护者在 Tailscale 工作并贡献代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Headscale与Tailscale的安全性、功能性、开源性及其实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **SuperShibe的观点**：对Headscale的安全性表示担忧，特别是Tailnet lock和安全审计的进展缓慢。他认为Headscale虽然成功绕过了防火墙，但在提供足够的安全措施上有所不足。同时，对Tailscale的控制服务器无法让用户了解或否决其指令表示担忧。

• **infogulch的观点**：建议Headscale允许实例间的对等/联合，并提出具体的IPv6和ULA范围的方案以解决地址冲突问题。不过，该建议之前被项目维护者认为超出了当前范围。

• **Happily2020的观点**：推荐自我托管的Netbird作为Tailscale的替代方案，强调Netbird的控制服务器是开源的，并提供与付费版本相同的功能和GUI。

• **1vuio0pswjnm7的观点**：指出Headscale允许用户通过阅读、编辑和编译源代码来理解或否决控制服务器的指令，而Tailscale则不允许。他认为不是所有用户都需要或想要编辑第三方软件的能力，有些用户可能更信任由风投资助的公司。

• **pilif的观点**：提醒大家注意Tailscale官方客户端维持设置控制服务器能力的重要性，担心如果Tailscale公司出现问题（如资金不足或被收购），该功能可能会消失。

• **3abiton的观点**：质疑Headscale相对于Wireguard + OpenWrt设置的附加价值，要求明确其优势。

补充讨论：
• **aborsy的风险担忧**：询问如果Tailscale协调服务器被攻破并启用了Tailnet lock的情况下，设备被 compromised 的风险有多大。

• **mountainriver的积极反馈**：表示Headscale在生产环境中表现出色，非常满意。

• **snvzz的长期使用体验**：认为Headscale在半年的使用中非常出色，已经离不开它。

• **udev4096的实际应用问题**：关心Headscale在通过Jellyfin/Plex流媒体传输视频时的表现。

• **pluto_modadic的疑问**：关心自我管理Headscale时的一些bug是否已经解决。

争议焦点：
• Headscale与Tailscale在安全性、开源性和控制权上的对比，特别是用户是否需要编辑、理解和否决控制服务器指令的能力。
• Headscale的功能扩展（如实例对等/联合）是否应纳入项目范围。

An open source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale control server.
Join our
Discord server
for a chat.
Note:
Always select the same GitHub tag as the released version you use
to ensure you have the correct example configuration and documentation.
The
main
branch might contain unreleased changes.
What is Tailscale
Tailscale is
a modern VPN
built on top of
Wireguard
.
It
works like an overlay network
between the computers of your networks - using
NAT traversal
.
Everything in Tailscale is Open Source, except the GUI clients for proprietary OS
(Windows and macOS/iOS), and the control server.
The control server works as an exchange point of Wireguard public keys for the
nodes in the Tailscale network. It assigns the IP addresses of the clients,
creates the boundaries between each user, enables sharing machines between users,
and exposes the advertised routes of your nodes.
A
Tailscale network (tailnet)
is private
network which Tailscale assigns to a user in terms of private users or an
organisation.
Design goal
Headscale aims to implement a self-hosted, open source alternative to the
Tailscale
control server. Headscale's goal is to
provide self-hosters and hobbyists with an open-source server they can use for
their projects and labs. It implements a narrow scope, a
single
Tailscale
network (tailnet), suitable for a personal use, or a small open-source
organisation.
Supporting Headscale
If you like
headscale
and find it useful, there is a sponsorship and donation
buttons available in the repo.
Features
Please see
"Features" in the documentation
.
Client OS support
Please see
"Client and operating system support" in the documentation
.
Running headscale
Please note that we do not support nor encourage the use of reverse proxies
and container to run Headscale.
Please have a look at the
documentation
.
Talks
Fosdem 2023 (video):
Headscale: How we are using integration testing to reimplement Tailscale
presented by Juan Font Alonso and Kristoffer Dalby
Disclaimer
This project is not associated with Tailscale Inc.
However, one of the active maintainers for Headscale
is employed by Tailscale
and he is allowed to spend work hours contributing to the project. Contributions from this maintainer are reviewed by other maintainers.
The maintainers work together on setting the direction for the project. The underlying principle is to serve the community of self-hosters, enthusiasts and hobbyists - while having a sustainable project.
Contributing
Please read the
CONTRIBUTING.md
file.
Requirements
To contribute to headscale you would need the latest version of
Go
and
Buf
(Protobuf generator).
We recommend using
Nix
to setup a development environment. This can
be done with
nix develop
, which will install the tools and give you a shell.
This guarantees that you will have the same dev env as
headscale
maintainers.
Code style
To ensure we have some consistency with a growing number of contributions,
this project has adopted linting and style/formatting rules:
The
Go
code is linted with
golangci-lint
and
formatted with
golines
(width 88) and
gofumpt
.
Please configure your editor to run the tools while developing and make sure to
run
make lint
and
make fmt
before committing any code.
The
Proto
code is linted with
buf
and
formatted with
clang-format
.
The
rest
(Markdown, YAML, etc) is formatted with
prettier
.
Check out the
.golangci.yaml
and
Makefile
to see the specific configuration.
Install development tools
Go
Buf
Protobuf tools
Install and activate:
nix develop
Testing and building
Some parts of the project require the generation of Go code from Protobuf
(if changes are made in
proto/
) and it must be (re-)generated with:
make g

data.title: Apple's Cubify Anything: Scaling Indoor 3D Object Detection
data.author: Tycho87
data.article_summary: 该仓库提供了Cubify Transformer的公开实现和相关的CA-1M数据集，用于室内3D物体检测。CA-1M数据集包含每个场景的类别无关3D框注释，并以激光扫描仪的坐标系发布。每个帧还包含独立于任何姿态的3D框地面真实数据、GT姿态和深度图像。数据以WebDataset格式发布，并提供基本代码以运行Cubify Transformer模型。CA-1M数据集仅包括成功注册到激光扫描仪的捕获，所有数据在CC-by-NC-ND许可证下发布，可通过`data/train.txt`和`data/val.txt`中的链接下载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕扫描房间并导出到Blender等3D工具的应用，及其相关技术实现、许可证问题和实际效果的讨论。

不同观点：
• Carrok认为，现有的扫描应用（如Scaniverse）已经接近实现他的需求，但存在问题：扫描结果是一个整体网格，无法单独操作家具（如沙发），他希望能够自由移动家具。
• pablogancharov提供了一个渲染USDZ文件的Three.js演示链接，可能对其他开发者有帮助。
• pzo批评了项目中使用的多重许可证组合，认为这使得第三方开发者难以使用，建议使用单一的严格许可证（如AGPL或CC-by-NC-ND）。
• desertmonad也指出许可证（Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives）非常限制，不利于广泛使用。
• callumprentice提到自己正在开发的equirectangular图像查看器，并分享了相关链接和示例，认为这些工具可以在现实和虚拟世界中都有很好的表现。
• syntaxing对该技术未被集成到CoreML中表示惊讶，认为这对Vision Pro等设备很有用。
• fidotron对扫描结果的精度提出质疑，认为图片中的细节（如墙上的画和天花板的梁）处理得不够好，可能无法满足大多数AR开发者的需求。
• totetsu以讽刺的口吻质疑该应用是否是为了让智能音箱更好地汇报用户家中的情况给Apple。
• Svip则以幽默的方式提到Power Mac G4 Cube，与Apple相关的"cube"概念产生联想。

补充讨论：
• 许可证问题是一个重要讨论点，多个评论提到多重许可证组合让使用变得复杂且限制较多。
• 扫描结果的精度和可操作性是另一个讨论焦点，Carrok和fidotron都提到扫描结果的细节和可编辑性问题。
• 技术实现方面，syntaxing和pablogancharov提到CoreML和Three.js等技术工具的潜在应用。

争议焦点：
• 许可证的多重性和限制性是主要争议点，开发者们对如何简化和放宽使用限制有不同看法。
• 扫描结果的精度和可操作性也是争议的焦点，部分用户对当前技术的实现效果表示不满。
