Benchi
Benchi is a minimal benchmarking framework designed to help you measure the
performance of your applications and infrastructure. It leverages Docker to
create isolated environments for running benchmarks and collecting metrics.
It was developed to simplify the process of setting up and running benchmarks
for
Conduit
.
Features
Docker Integration
: Define and manage your benchmarking environments using
Docker Compose.
Metrics Collection
: Collect and export metrics in CSV format for further
analysis.
Custom Hooks
: Define custom hooks to run commands at various stages of the
benchmark.
Progress Monitoring
: Real-time monitoring of container statuses and
metrics during the benchmark run.
Installation
To install Benchi, download
the
latest release
or
install it using Go:
go install github.com/conduitio/benchi/cmd/benchi@latest
Alternatively, you can install just the Benchi binary on a Linux OS with:
curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ConduitIO/benchi/main/install.sh
|
sh
Usage
Running Benchmarks
Run benchi and point
-config
to a benchmark
configuration file
.
The repository includes an
example benchmark
, which can be run
using the following command:
benchi -config ./example/bench-kafka-kafka/bench.yml
Results
Running the benchmark will store the results in a folder named after the current
date and time inside of
results
(e.g.
results/20060102_150405
). You can
adjust the output folder using the
-out
flag.
The output folder will contain two files:
benchi.log
: Log file containing the full output of benchi.
aggregated-results.csv
: Aggregated metric results from all collectors and
all tests. The results are aggregated using a
trimmed mean
, where the top
and bottom 5% of the results are removed. Benchi also disregards any 0 values
from the start and end of the test, to accomodate for warm-up and cool-down
periods.
The output folder will also contain one folder per benchmark run (i.e. per test
and tool combination). Each benchmark run folder will contain:
infra_NAME.log
: Log file containing the output of the infrastructure docker
containers, split per infra service.
tool_NAME.log
: Log file containing the output of the tool docker containers.
COLLECTOR.csv
: Raw metrics collected using the corresponding
metrics collector
.
Command-Line Flags
-config
: Path to the benchmark config file (required).
-out
: Path to the output folder (default:
./results/${now}
*).
-tool
: Filter tool to be tested (can be provided multiple times).
-tests
: Filter test to run (can be provided multiple times).
*
${now}
is replaced with the current time formatted as
YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS
.
Docker network
Benchi creates a Docker network named
benchi
to connect the infrastructure
services and tools. This network is created automatically and removed after the
benchmark run. Please make sure to connect your services to this network to
ensure they can communicate with each other.
Example Docker Compose configuration:
services
:
my-service
:
networks
:
-
benchi
networks
:
benchi
:
external
:
true
Environment variables
Benchi runs all Docker Compose commands using the same environment variables as
the current shell. This means that you can use environment variables to pass
values to your services.
For instance, having the following Docker Compose configuration:
services
:
my-service
:
environment
:
-
MY_ENV_VAR=${MY_ENV_VAR}
You can inject the environment variable by running Benchi as follows:
MY_ENV_VAR=my-value benchi -config ./my-benchmark.yml
Configuration
Benchi uses a YAML configuration file to define the benchmark in combination
with Docker Compose configurations.
Below is an example configuration:
infrastructure
:
database
:
compose
:
"
./compose-database.yml
"
cache
:
compose
:
"
./compose-cache.yml
"
tools
:
my-app
:
compose
:
"
./compose-my-app.yml
"
metrics
:
prometheus
:
collector
:
"
prometheus
"

:
url
:
"
http://localhost:9090/metrics
"

-
name
:
"
http_requests_rate
"

rate(request_count{endpoint=hello}[2s])
"

"

-

Endpoint Load

2m

:

:

data.article_summary: Anime.js 是一个快速、多功能的 JavaScript 动画库，能够突破浏览器限制，通过单一API实现网页上的各种动画效果。它具有直观的API，支持逐属性参数设置、灵活的关键帧系统、内置缓动效果和增强的CSS变换。此外，它还支持SVG图形变形、线条绘制和路径跟随，并可以通过Scroll Observer API实现滚动同步动画。Anime.js 提供高级交错效果和拖拽功能，并支持响应式动画和模块化导入，以保持较小的包体积。该库还包括详细的文档和示例代码，帮助开发者快速上手。Anime.js 是免费的，并依赖赞助商的支持。

• [跨平台兼容性] 有用户提到该页面在非传统安卓浏览器上运行良好，表明其底层库具有良好的兼容性（[monetus]）。
• [响应式布局问题] 部分用户指出了页面在响应式布局中存在的一些问题，如调整窗口大小时滚动条会重置（[XCSme]）。

data.title: Show HN: Novanode, Global load balancing with Caddy, no vendor lock-in
data.author: martianE
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于技术方案及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• Snawoot分享了一个与供应商无关的技术方案，提供了具体操作指南的链接。这个方案被描述为“粗略但真正独立于供应商”的解决方案，但未详细解释具体操作细节。

• quicksilver03对Snawoot的方案提出了实际操作中的问题，特别是如何在区域A宕机时将流量重定向到区域B，以及在一个区域内一个节点宕机时的处理方法。这表明quicksilver03关注方案在实际故障情况下的有效性与可操作性。

• mlhpdx讨论了在构建类似系统时，每个区域的固定成本对实验者和大团队来说都是一个障碍。他指出，尽管成本在整体预算中不算高，但足以阻止个人或团队随意搭建和维护非生产环境。他还提到，现有的负载均衡方案虽然部署快速，但在按使用量计费方面有所欠缺，这使得长期运行半闲置堆栈的成本较高。

• codegeek对Caddy（一种开源的Web服务器和反向代理工具）表示兴趣，并询问该方案是否支持SSL终止和一般反向代理功能。codegeek希望有一个托管的Caddy集群，以便无需直接配置Caddyfiles或API就能使用所有Caddy功能。

• metadat则对项目名称的读音和来源表示好奇，属于对项目细节的轻松提问，没有涉及技术深度。

• trevorhinesley对多区域部署的具体技术实现表示疑问，特别是是否涉及Anycast技术。这表明他关注多区域部署的技术细节和实现方式。

• revskill表达了对整体方案的不理解，仅拥有VPS（虚拟专用服务器）后该如何操作并不明确，显示出对项目入门指导的需求。

补充讨论：
• 该讨论中涉及了多个技术细节，包括流量重定向、节点故障处理、固定成本对实验的影响、按使用量计费的需求、SSL终止及反向代理功能，以及Anycast技术的应用。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在方案的可操作性和成本问题上，尤其是对于个人实验者和小团队而言，如何在保持方案有效性的同时降低成本是一个关键问题。
• 不同参与者对技术细节的关注点各异，有的关注实际操作中的故障处理，有的则关注方案的成本和易用性。

主要讨论点：用户对一个具有赛博朋克风格的应用程序的反馈和看法

不同观点：
• Layogtima：对该应用表示喜爱，并询问是否为开源，表达了将其用于模拟Vogon Constructor Fleet飞船界面的兴趣。
• b0bben：分享开发该应用程序的背景和动机，强调追求个人兴趣（受《神经漫游者》启发），并寻求社区反馈以决定是否将其发展为正式产品。同时提供早期alpha版本下载链接，提醒用户注意安全。
• egypturnash：对演示视频中缺乏实际内容（如图片）表示失望，但对外观风格表示认可。
• jamauro：简单直接地表示赞赏，并鼓励继续开发。
• indigoabstract：将应用界面比作黑客游戏的用户界面，认可其视觉风格。
• cyberpunk：以幽默方式表达个人品牌与该应用的关联，提到一些具体元素（如T恤、牛仔裤、字体、耳机），强调个性化风格。

补充讨论：
• b0bben在其评论中提到开发该应用的个人经历和对赛博朋克风格的追求，反映出一种从个人兴趣出发进行创作的热情。
• 不同用户对应用外观的评价多为正面，但对实际功能和内容的展示存在一定期待和质疑（如egypturnash对缺乏实际图片的评论）。
• b0bben积极回应反馈，提供下载链接并提醒用户注意安全，显示出对社区反馈的重视和开放态度。
• cyberpunk的评论带有幽默和个人色彩，强调了赛博朋克风格中的个性化元素，为讨论增添了一些轻松的氛围。

争议焦点：
• 目前讨论中没有明显争议，但用户对应用实际功能和内容的期望与当前展示效果之间存在一定差距，可能成为未来开发中的讨论点。

主要讨论点：欢迎Tom成为Hacker News（HN）的新任公开 moderator，以及对HN社区和现有moderator团队的评价与期望。

不同观点：
• 感谢与欢迎：多数评论对Tom的加入表示欢迎和感谢，赞扬了他多年对社区的支持。例如，rurp、raphman和noleary都表达了对HN社区和moderator团队的赞赏，强调了社区长久以来的高质量和稳定性。
• 幽默与调侃：部分评论以幽默方式回应Tom的加入，例如codetrotter对Tom名字发音的调侃，以及koolba建议给Tom一个新用户名“darn”来制造混淆。
• 对社区运营的建议：keepamovin提出了一个功能建议，希望可以私密地“收藏”用户，以便跟踪他们发表的言论。这一建议引出了对HN现有功能和用户体验的讨论。

补充讨论：
• 对moderator工作的认可：GVRV回顾了Tom在大学期间对CS和创业俱乐部的贡献，强调了他作为moderator的合适性。hakaneskici和isoprophlex则强调了moderator团队在维护社区质量方面的不懈努力和重要性。
• 对HN独特氛围的赞扬：ddingus和scrapcode都提到了HN独特的社区氛围，认为这是一个充满智力刺激和健康讨论的地方，并对此表示感激。
• 对moderator团队透明度的关注：palmotea提出了对是否存在其他秘密moderator的疑问，这涉及到社区对moderator团队透明度的关注。

争议焦点：
• 目前评论中未见明显争议，主要以正面评价和建议为主。不过，keepamovin的功能建议可能引发对HN现有功能体系和用户体验的进一步讨论。

总体来看，评论主要集中在对Tom加入moderator团队的欢迎和感谢，以及对HN社区长期以来高质量讨论环境的认可和期望。同时，也有一些幽默调侃和功能建议，为讨论增添了多样性。

data.title: The Steam Deck is software-freedom friendly
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Steam Deck的成功不仅在于其硬件性能或电池寿命，而在于其基于Linux系统的开放性和兼容性哲学。Steam Deck通过Proton软件层实现了对大量PC游戏的兼容，推动了Linux游戏支持的显著提升。与许多限制用户自由的设备不同，Steam Deck允许用户自由安装各种软件和游戏启动器，甚至可以作为桌面电脑使用，体现了对用户自由和设备所有权的高度尊重。文章还赞扬了Valve对设备维修和开放市场的支持，认为Steam Deck展示了商业利益与用户公民权益可以共存的可能性。不过，文章也提及Valve的企业文化曾受到批评。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Valve及其产品（尤其是Steam和Steam Deck）的消费者友好性、技术实现、市场定位以及对游戏行业的长期影响。

不同观点：
• **Valve的消费者友好性**：
  - [TehCorwiz] 认为Valve非常注重消费者体验，Steam提供了一个低压力的销售环境，功能设计以用户体验为中心，例如允许家长控制、不随意更改用户设置等。相比之下，其他平台如Epic的体验较差。
  - [whytevuhuni] 认为Valve并非圣徒，尤其是在游戏分发平台的垄断地位上，但他们确实比其他公司更注重用户体验，继承了“不作恶”的理念。

• **Steam Deck的技术与市场定位**：
  - [glenstein] 强调Steam Deck是Valve长期技术发展的成果，源自早期的Steam Machines项目，并成功推动了Linux生态系统的发展。虽然Steam Machines在初期未被广泛接受，但它们为Steam Deck的成功奠定了基础。
  - [craftkiller] 支持Steam Deck，特别是它对Linux系统的支持，但也表达了对独占游戏（如任天堂游戏）无法在Steam上获取的不满，认为这导致了不必要的硬件浪费。
  - [danso] 指出Switch 2可能在硬件上更强大且价格相近，但Steam的杀手锏是其更便宜且更广泛的游戏库。

• **软件自由与技术细节**：
  - [seba_dos1] 认为Steam Deck并非特别注重软件自由，只是没有特意限制它，这与Valve的无为而治态度有关。
  - [accurrent] 赞赏Steam Deck利用开源软件进行商业产品开发，并希望其他制造商能效仿，而不是捆绑Windows系统。
  - [dezzadk] 对Steam Deck依赖Wine技术实现游戏兼容性表示不满，认为这忽视了原生Linux端口的重要性，并指出Valve的商业化行为与其他公司无异。

补充讨论：
• **Steam Deck的实用性与用户体验**：
  - [GardenLetter27] 分享了Steam Deck的多功能用途，从游戏到控制机器人等，表明它不仅限于游戏设备。
  - [Fwirt] 强调Steam Deck作为PC游戏的“主机化”设备，解决了PC游戏兼容性问题，并提供了类似主机的无缝体验。
  - [thih9] 关心游戏控制器的兼容性问题，询问是否需要手动映射控制。

• **对未来和公司发展的担忧**：
  - [jerf] 提到Steam Deck甚至比被破解的Switch更好用，无需进行复杂的破解操作。

争议焦点：
• **Steam Deck对开源和原生Linux的支持**：一方认为Valve通过Steam Deck推动了Linux生态系统的发展，另一方则批评其过度依赖Wine技术，忽视了原生Linux端口的维护。
• **Valve的商业行为**：虽然许多人赞赏Valve的消费者友好态度，但也有人指出其在平台垄断和商业化方面的潜在问题。

43567923.article_content:
The
Steam Deck
is a great gaming system. This isn’t because of it’s great battery life. A Nintendo Switch would probably have better battery life. It’s not because of its great performance. I don’t usually play AAA games, so I wouldn’t know. The Steam Deck is great because of the philosophy on which it is built.
The popularity of Steam Decks is directly tied to the betterment of support for games on Linux. This is because the Steam Deck really is a linux computer in a handheld form-factor with a gamepad, among other things, attached to it. According to
ProtonDB
, over 5000 PC games are certified Verified on the Steam Deck, and over 15,000 games are considered playable. This means that there are tens of thousands of games that can be run on Linux in some way.
Thanks to Steam’s efforts, the state of compatibility of games on Linux systems have heavily improved. Not all these thousands of games running on the Deck have binaries that run natively on Linux. Pivotal to the success of the Deck is Proton, a middle-layer compatibility software, that makes this (mostly) seamless emulation possible. Nonetheless, the greater the adoption of Decks, the likelier we are to normalize prioritizing game-builds for Linux.
We run software because it serves us some purpose. In this, running software is no different from utilizing everyday objects, and playing games are no different from running software. Yet, this teleological view of computing would miss a lot of context. When picking an operating system, we may want to make a choice that aligns with the goals of transparency or software freedom. But this would not be realistic if the programs we would like to run on top are not supported in such an ecosystem. Since large parts of Proton is open-source, and are released under permissive licenses, gaming on a Deck takes us closer to using a principled software stack for daily use.
Purchasing everyday objects give us ownership over them. With media, software and computing equipment, this is less so. When you buy a book, you may lend it to others, sell it, earmark the pages and even rip it in two if you like. This is very different from the experience of buying a smartphone. You can’t run arbitrary programs of your choice on an Android phone without rooting, or on an iPad or an iPhone without jailbreaking. In most scenarios, you’d be forced to sign away your legal ability to root or jailbreak before you can engage with the device in any meaningful way.
The Steam Deck does not engage in this practice. It runs a heavily customized version of Arch Linux. This means that you can plug in a keyboard and mouse into it, and pretend that it is your desktop computer. If you like, you can install the LibreOffice suite on it, and prepare presentations.
The matter of using your computers the way you like is more than just a symbolic debate about the nature of ownership. It is a political matter of freedom of expression. When they control the apps that you run on your device, they are in charge of deciding which content is Kosher, and which content is obscene. It is also an economic matter of having efficient markets. The mythological power of the free market works only when the consumers can switch between different producers at will. When the operators of the market themselves try to capitalize on chokepoints and direct the consumers to buy products from their allies, this is no longer the case.
Switch owners buy games from the Switch Store not because that is the best market, but because that is the only marketplace from which they can install games. This is thankfully, less of a case with the Steam Deck. The Steam Deck encourages you to buy and play Steam games, of course. Nonetheless, I had
no issues
installing
Epic Games
,
GoG
or even
itch.io
launchers on my Deck and playing games from them. The Deck also includes a “non-steam game” tab in its UI to let users conveniently access them.
When your shoe tears up, you are welcome to visit the cobbler of your choice. They all understand the internals of a shoe. And when they need to fix them, they all can gather the nails, glue and the pieces of fabric that they might need. This is less so for many computing products. Many manufacturers try to discourage third party vendors from repairing them. Worse, they sometimes purposely use proprietary parts in their products, replacements of which would be hard to find. Thankfully, Valve has been different. Valve has released
a video
explaining the internal organization of the Steam Deck and how one should approach replacing parts, should they wish to do so.
This post is not really necessarily about the Steam Deck (or Valve Corporation) itself. That said, the Steam Deck is an excellent demonstration that the commercial interest of making profit does not necessarily have to overpower the civic interests of the people.
Valve’s libertarian ideology has not always been an unquestionable force for good.
Some
people
have criticized that their company culture

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个PowerShell脚本（RemoveDefaultApps.ps1），用于卸载Windows系统中预装的某些默认应用程序。这些应用包括如Microsoft.BingFinance、Microsoft.BingNews、Microsoft.Solitaire等。脚本通过调用`Get-AppxPackage`和`Remove-AppxPackage`等PowerShell命令来移除用户和系统中的指定应用，并参考了多个微软文档和社区资源。此脚本旨在帮助用户清理不必要的预装软件，以优化系统性能和减少干扰。

data.title: AI 2027
data.author: Tenoke
data.article_summary: 本文预测超人类AI在未来十年将产生巨大影响，可能超过工业革命。作者们基于趋势推断、兵棋推演、专家反馈等编写了具体场景，以预测2027年AI的可能发展，包括“减速”和“竞赛”两种结局。尽管预测未来非常困难，但这样的尝试有助于引发关于AI未来影响的讨论，并识别潜在风险和重要问题。本文并非建议或号召，而是为了提高预测准确性，并鼓励他人参与讨论和提出不同看法。作者团队包括多位有AI研究和预测成功经验的专家，如Daniel Kokotajlo和Eli Lifland。文章详细描述了2025年中期AI代理的初步应用，虽然这些代理比以往技术更先进，但仍面临普及挑战，而在专业领域，AI正逐渐改变编码和研究工作。

不同观点：

• porphyra批评文章有“中国恐惧症”倾向，指出中国在人工智能创新方面的成就被忽视，文章错误地暗示中国只会通过窃取技术来发展。
• infecto认为文章大部分内容是幻想，实际有价值的讨论点很少，特别是右侧的指标完全是虚构的，不值得关注。
• amarcheschi分享了使用Claude和Gemini等AI工具进行数据分析的实际体验，表示难以通过简单的互动完成复杂任务，质疑其他人如何通过“感觉编程”完成任务。

• Joshuatanderson支持文章的观点，提到Scott Alexander之前的预测在图像进展方面表现良好。
• Willingham对文章中提到的2027年自动化大多数白领工作的预测表示好奇，质疑哪些工作不会被自动化，如治疗师或HR。

• Q6T46nT668w6i3m将文章与“Annie Hall”中的“mansplaining”场景相比，暗示文章内容自大且无意义。

• ikerino认为文章开头合理，但很快变得像科幻小说，希望看到关于技术发展最慢合理速度的讨论。

• 文章对AI发展时间线的预测是否过于乐观。

• 对AGI实现时间和影响的预测是否可信。

has said
OpenAI is setting its sights on “superintelligence in the true sense of the word” and the “glorious future.”
3
What might that look like? We wrote AI 2027 to answer that question. Claims about the future are often frustratingly vague, so we tried to be as concrete and quantitative as possible, even though this means depicting one of many possible futures.
We wrote two endings: a “slowdown” and a “race” ending. However, AI 2027 is not a recommendation or exhortation. Our goal is predictive accuracy.
4
We encourage you to debate and counter this scenario.
5
We hope to spark a broad conversation about where we’re headed and how to steer toward positive futures. We’re
planning to give out thousands in prizes
to the best alternative scenarios.
Our research on key questions (e.g. what goals will future AI agents have?) can be found
here
.
The scenario itself was written iteratively: we wrote the first period (up to mid-2025), then the following period, etc. until we reached the ending. We then scrapped this and did it again.
We weren’t trying to reach any particular ending. After we finished the first ending—which is now colored red—we wrote a new alternative branch because we wanted to also depict a more hopeful way things could end, starting from roughly the same premises. This went through several iterations.
6
Our scenario was informed by approximately 25
tabletop exercises
and feedback from over 100 people, including dozens of experts in each of AI governance and AI technical work.
“I highly recommend reading this scenario-type prediction on how AI could transform the world in just a few years. Nobody has a crystal ball, but this type of content can help notice important questions and illustrate the potential impact of emerging risks.”
—
Yoshua Bengio
7
We have set ourselves an impossible task. Trying to predict how superhuman AI in 2027 would go is like trying to predict how World War 3 in 2027 would go, except that it’s an even larger departure from past case studies. Yet it is still valuable to attempt, just as it is valuable for the US military to game out Taiwan scenarios.
Painting the whole picture makes us notice important questions or connections we hadn’t considered or appreciated before, or realize that a possibility is more or less likely. Moreover, by sticking our necks out with concrete predictions, and encouraging others to publicly state their disagreements, we make it possible to evaluate years later who was right.
Also, one author wrote a lower-effort AI scenario
before, in August 2021
. While it got many things wrong, overall it was surprisingly successful: he predicted the rise of chain-of-thought, inference scaling, sweeping AI chip export controls, and $100 million training runs—all more than a year before ChatGPT.
Daniel Kokotajlo
(
TIME100
,
NYT piece
) is a former OpenAI researcher whose previous
AI predictions
have
held up well
.
Eli Lifland
co-founded
AI Digest
, did
AI robustness research
, and ranks #1 on the
RAND Forecasting Initiative
all-time leaderboard.
Thomas Larsen
founded the
Center for AI Policy
and did AI safety research at the
Machine Intelligence Research Institute
.
Romeo Dean
is completing a computer science concurrent bachelor’s and master’s degree at Harvard and previously was an
AI Policy Fellow
at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy.
Scott Alexander, blogger extraordinaire
, volunteered to rewrite our content in an engaging style; the fun parts of the story are his and the boring parts are ours.
For more about our team and acknowledgements, see the
About page
.

The world sees its first glimpse of AI agents.
Advertisements for computer-using agents emphasize the term “personal assistant”: you can prompt them with tasks like “order me a burrito on DoorDash” or “open my budget spreadsheet and sum this month’s expenses.” They will check in with you as needed: for example, to ask you to confirm purchases.

Though more advanced than previous iterations like
Operator
, they struggle to get widespread usage.

data.author: trevin
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了当今世界色彩逐渐消失的现象，特别是在汽车颜色、消费品设计和影视色彩运用等方面。数据显示，超过80%的新车是黑、白、灰或银色，消费品颜色也趋于中性化。影视作品的色调也越来越单调，充满灰暗的蓝灰色。这种现象不仅源于工业材料和市场需求，还深植于西方哲学对色彩的长期怀疑。从柏拉图到康德，许多哲学家认为色彩是感官上的干扰，不具备理性价值。现代极简主义和市场趋势进一步推动了这种“惧色症”（Chromophobia）。文章呼吁重新思考色彩在现代生活中的重要性，并努力恢复其运用。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• crazygringo：认为现代设计更注重中性色，色彩应作为点缀而非主元素。过度使用色彩会造成视觉疲劳，现代品味倾向于用色彩突出重点，而非让所有东西都五颜六色。
• JKCalhoun：热衷于色彩，反对目前市场上的单调颜色选择，特别是在汽车和电影色调上。他认为色彩的减少是市场和设计上的一种损失。
• fguerraz：指出色彩使用减少的原因是市场和经济因素，色彩多样性会导致库存和转售价值问题。制造商为了避免销售困难，选择生产更易销售的颜色。
• colmmacc：分享个人经验，穿着鲜艳颜色让他更容易与人接触，并且在欧洲时尚中较为常见。他主张使用色彩来增加个人风格和亲和力。
• rahkiin：认为汽车颜色选择受价格影响，定制颜色成本高导致消费者选择便宜的基本颜色。如果厂商不收费，可能会有更多颜色选择。

Walk around in the average parking lot, and you’ll find yourself in a sea of black, white, and silver vehicles. Watch Netflix at home or catch a film in the theaters, and you’ll get the same washed-out color grade on either screen. Glance at the logos of the world’s largest companies, and you’ll notice a shrinking palette.
It all points to one thing: color is vanishing from our world.
This isn’t just a hunch. Studies of everything from car paint to consumer objects show that we’re in the midst of a vast aesthetic shift. What used to be vibrant has become sterile. What used to pop out and catch our attention now fades into the background.
The question is — why?
The answer isn’t just about fashion or materials, but is rooted in a much older understanding of the relationship between color and truth.
Here’s why color is disappearing from our world, and what we can do to bring it back…

A Monochrome World
The colors around us aren’t just changing. They’re disappearing.
According to major auto paint suppliers, more than 80% of new cars are now grayscale. Black, white, gray, and silver dominate the roads. Reds, blues, and greens in auto production are increasingly rare.
It’s not just cars — a study of over 7,000 objects in the UK’s Science Museum found that the colors of consumer goods have been steadily neutralized since 1800. Bright, saturated tones have been giving way to gray, beige, and taupe for centuries.
Graphic design has followed a similar trend. Streaming platforms, fashion brands, and e-commerce hubs are consistently rebranding in black-and-white. Most recently, HBO’s move to rename its service “Max” was accompanied by a logo redesign that stripped away its original blue — replacing it, of course, with stark white text on a black background.
Even cinema has gone gray. Although Ridley Scott’s
Napoleon
was shot on vivid, richly colored sets, its final color-grade — like that of many historical dramas — washes out all the colors in a somber, blueish-gray tint. It’s a visual style that has become so ubiquitous that directors like Wes Anderson are often considered “unorthodox” for their use of vibrant color in film.
On the surface, there are some straightforward reasons for this. Industrial materials like steel and plastic, for example, are produced in neutral shades. Grayscale branding for logos is easier to reproduce and scale. Muted palettes are less likely to alienate customers.
But this isn't the whole story. To fully understand why color is disappearing from our world, we have to go further back…
The Philosophers’ Suspicion of Color
Color has always had a strange status in Western philosophy — and more often than not, that status is second-class.
In
Chromophobia
, art theorist David Batchelor argues that the devaluation of color can be traced to the very birth of Western thought. From Plato onward, color was treated as a distraction: sensory noise that got in the way of rational understanding.
Plato described the world of appearances as a deceptive “prison-house,” i.e., a realm of illusion where truth could only be grasped by looking beyond the senses. Color, tied directly to sensation, was thus something to overcome — not to embrace.
Aristotle echoed the sentiment. In
Poetics
, he argued that the power of artwork lay in its structure, not its palette:
“A random distribution of the most attractive colors would never yield as much pleasure as a definite image without color.”
For Aristotle, it’s form that holds meaning — not hue.
This view persisted through the Enlightenment, with German philosopher Immanuel Kant arguing that while color may add charm to art, it has no bearing on true aesthetic judgment. In his view, color neither touches reason nor elevates the mind.
The underlying theory in all of these cases is that while color is sensory, unstable, and chaotic, form is rational, stable, and pure. Once you see this bias, you begin to notice how deeply it has shaped the modern world — and how it helps explain our current retreat into colorlessness.
Minimalism, Mass Markets, and Beige Beats

data.title: A 6-Hour Time-Stretched Version of Brian Eno's Music for Airports
data.author: vinhnx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了布莱恩·伊诺（Brian Eno）的标志性环境音乐专辑《Music for Airports》（机场音乐）及其影响。该专辑创作于1978年，通过秒级长度的磁带循环创造出缓慢、冥想性的音乐，放弃了传统的大小调音阶，旨在为听众提供一种背景音，让人放松甚至思考死亡。文章提到一个由YouTube用户创建的长达6小时的延展版专辑，并回顾了该专辑在现实机场中的应用，如1980年代在纽约拉瓜迪亚机场的短暂播放以及2018年伦敦城市机场为庆祝专辑40周年而进行的全天循环播放。此外，文章还讨论了该专辑在多媒体艺术中的地位，并设想未来在更多公共空间中使用环境音乐而非经典摇滚或流行音乐。读者评论则进一步探讨了类似音乐在其他场景（如医生办公室）的应用潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Brian Eno的《Ambient 1: Music for Airports》及其相关的 ambient 音乐

不同观点：
• okeuro49 引用Brian Eno的采访，强调机场背景音乐应避免让乘客感到焦虑，特别是对于像他这样容易紧张的飞行者。Eno认为机场音乐不应试图掩饰飞行可能带来的危险感，而是应提供一种更合适的氛围。
• jquaint 提到使用软件（如paulstretch）来制作类似 ambient 音乐，并分享了相关工具链接，提供了一种技术上的视角。
• morsch 更喜欢The Black Dog的《Music for Real Airports》，并将之与Eno的作品进行对比，展示了不同音乐人的类似作品之间的偏好差异。

A 6‑Hour Time-Stretched Version of Brian Eno’s
Music For Airports
: Meditate, Relax, Study
in
Music
|   	March 17th, 2025
3 Comments
Writ­ing in his 1995 diary about his sem­i­nal ambi­ent album
Music for Air­ports
, Eno remem­bered his ini­tial thoughts going into it: “I want to make a kind of music that pre­pares you for dying–that doesn’t get all bright and cheer­ful and pre­tend you’re not a lit­tle appre­hen­sive, but which makes you say to your­self, ‘Actu­al­ly, it’s not that big a deal if I die.’”
Cre­at­ed in 1978 from sec­onds-long tape loops from a much longer improv ses­sion with musi­cians includ­ing Robert Wyatt,
Music for Air­ports
start­ed the idea of slow, med­i­ta­tive music that aban­doned typ­i­cal major and minor scales, brought in melod­ic ambi­gu­i­ty, and began the explo­ration of sounds that were designed to exist some­where in the back­ground, beyond the scope of full atten­tion.
For those who think 50 min­utes is too short and those piano notes too rec­og­niz­able, may we sug­gest this 6‑hour, time-stretched ver­sion of the album, cre­at­ed by YouTube user “Slow Motion TV.” The tonal field is the same, but now the notes are no attack, all decay. It’s gran­u­lar as hell, but you could imag­ine the whole piece unspool­ing unno­ticed in a ter­mi­nal while a flight is delayed for the third time. (Maybe that’s when the accep­tance of death hap­pens, when you’ve giv­en up on ever get­ting home?)
Unlike
Music for Films
, which fea­tured sev­er­al tracks Eno had giv­en to film­mak­ers like Derek Jar­man, it took some time for
Music for Air­ports
to be real­ized in its intend­ed loca­tion: being piped in at a ter­mi­nal at La Guardia, New York, some­time in the 1980s. And that was just a one-time thing.
?si=6VMY_yEfZdFDZbp6
The album seemed des­tined for per­son­al use only, but then in 1997 the mod­ern ensem­ble Bang on a Can played it live, trans­lat­ing the ran­dom­ness of out-of-sync tape loops into music nota­tion. Over the years they’ve per­formed it at air­ports in Brus­sels, the Nether­lands and Liv­er­pool, and in 2015 the group brought it to Ter­mi­nal 2 of San Diego Inter­na­tion­al.
Writ­ing for KCET, Alex Zaragoza report­ed
that “cry­ing babies, echoes of rolling suit­cas­es and board­ing pass­es serv­ing as tick­ets to the con­cert failed to remind any­one that they were, indeed, at one of the busiest air­ports in the coun­try. Even the tell­tale announce­ments were there:
Air­port secu­ri­ty is every­one’s respon­si­bil­i­ty. Do not leave bags unat­tend­ed
.”
And then in 2018,
Lon­don City Air­port played the orig­i­nal album
in a day-long loop for the album’s 40th anniver­sary.
As site-spe­cif­ic mul­ti-media art builds pop­u­lar­i­ty in the 21st cen­tu­ry with increas­ing­ly cheap­er and small­er tech­nol­o­gy, we might hope to hear ambi­ent drones, and not clas­sic rock or pop, in more and more land­scapes.
Note: An ear­li­er ver­sion of this post appeared on our site in 2019.

43520122.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了布莱恩·伊诺（Brian Eno）的标志性环境音乐专辑《Music for Airports》（机场音乐）及其影响。该专辑创作于1978年，通过秒级长度的磁带循环创造出缓慢、冥想性的音乐，放弃了传统的大小调音阶，旨在为听众提供一种背景音，让人放松甚至思考死亡。文章提到一个由YouTube用户创建的长达6小时的延展版专辑，并回顾了该专辑在现实机场中的应用，如1980年代在纽约拉瓜迪亚机场的短暂播放以及2018年伦敦城市机场为庆祝专辑40周年而进行的全天循环播放。此外，文章还讨论了该专辑在多媒体艺术中的地位，并设想未来在更多公共空间中使用环境音乐而非经典摇滚或流行音乐。读者评论则进一步探讨了类似音乐在其他场景（如医生办公室）的应用潜力。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对开源项目贡献的激励机制及其实际效果

不同观点：
• **nikcub** 认为当前的开源项目贡献机制存在问题，尤其是在激励贡献者方面。他指出，很多贡献者在没有获得足够认可或回报的情况下，容易感到倦怠并退出项目。他提到，即便是大规模的公司支持项目，也没有很好地解决这一问题。nikcub 强调，需要重新设计激励机制，让贡献者能获得更长久的动力。

• **支持现有机制的观点** 认为，开源项目的贡献本身是自愿的，贡献者在参与时就应了解并接受这一性质。有人指出，现有的荣誉激励（如在项目中被提及、获得社区尊重等）已经足够，且开源项目的文化和精神就在于无偿贡献。这种观点认为，过度的物质激励可能会扭曲开源精神，导致项目变得商业化。

• **混合激励机制的观点** 提出，可以结合荣誉激励和物质激励。例如，通过奖金、资助计划或提供职业发展机会等方式，让贡献者不仅获得精神上的满足，还能在物质上有所回报。这种观点的支持者认为，这不仅能激励更多人参与，还能提高贡献的质量和持续性。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点** 在于如何在保持开源精神的同时，有效地激励贡献者。一些人担心物质激励会改变开源社区的本质，使其变得功利化；而另一些人则认为，开源社区需要与时俱进，找到适应现代社会的方式来吸引和留住优秀贡献者。

• **具体例子** 被提到，诸如 Google Summer of Code (GSoC) 和其他类似的资助项目，是目前一些大公司支持开源贡献的有效方式。这些项目通过提供资金支持，吸引学生和新人参与开源，但 nikcub 认为这些措施还远远不够，且覆盖面有限。

• **社区建设** 被认为是另一种激励方式，通过建立更紧密的社区关系和提供更多学习和成长机会，来增强贡献者的归属感和成就感。这种观点强调软性激励，如指导计划、知识分享和团队合作等。

通过这些观点的讨论，可以看出开源贡献激励机制是一个复杂且多维度的问题，涉及文化、经济和社区动态等多个方面。

How Silica Gel Took Over the World
Spencer Wright
I find them stuffed into the toes of a new pair of sneakers. I find them wedged into a sheaf of seaweed snacks. I find them in the over-inflated bag that contains my new inhaler, and in the vacuum-sealed one puckered around my kids’ 3D printing filament. “DO NOT EAT,” they all admonish me, and I find myself slipping them under the top layer of the garbage already in the trash can, as if my kids wouldn’t be able to control their urge to taste whatever is inside these tiny white pouches. Silica gel packets are
everywhere
, their presence seemingly the only thing keeping our packaged food crispy and our belongings free of mildew. How on earth did they all get here?
Is silica gel taking over the world?
Tear its little Tyvek wrapping, and spill a packet of glassy silica gel beads into the palm of your hand; they won’t hurt you. They are made of the same stuff as sand: “Silica” means “silicon dioxide,” which is the primary component of most drinkware, windshields, and the screen of whatever electronic device you’re reading this on. But glass has a density of around 2500 kilograms per cubic meter, and crystalline silicon dioxide (quartz) is around 2650. Silica gel, on the other hand, is more like 700 kilograms per cubic meter. It may look fully dense, but in fact it’s shot through with countless tiny pores. If your windowpane is like a thin sheet of solid ice, then a silica gel bead is like a tiny snowball.
Silica gel beads, as seen by a scanning electron microscope. Image credit: Dusan Berek, via
Structural inhomogeneities in wide-pore silica gels
.
Zoom in on a silica gel bead with a scanning electron microscope, and its smooth surface turns discontinuous, riddled with voids about 2.5 nanometers across (roughly the diameter of a strand of DNA). This microstructure gives silica gel radical properties. The silica gel packets in my kids’ seaweed snacks are just a little bit bigger than postage stamps, and have a total mass of about a gram. That single gram of silica gel could have an internal surface area of eight hundred square meters—the size of
almost two basketball courts
.
These factors allow silica gel to adsorb up to 40% of its own weight in water vapor, through a process called
capillary condensation
. When humid air migrates into the pores of a silica gel bead, its vapor pressure increases, causing water to condense onto the silica gel’s internal surfaces. At the risk of anthropomorphizing water, it’s as if it prefers to be a liquid, stuck within the silica gel’s tiny capillaries, than a vapor, carried along with whatever else is in the air.
If you find a packet of silica gel in an imported snack or the pocket of a new jacket, it’s probably there to filter water vapor out of air. Like most filters, there is a limit to how much water a piece of silica gel can hold; its internal surfaces are finite in size, and as a result there is a finite amount of humidity that a given packet of silica gel can adsorb. Luckily, silica gel vendors offer nifty calculators so that their customers can size their silica gel packets to the volumes of air they wish to dry out—and how dry they want the air to be. If you wanted to desiccate the air inside of a child’s balloon, you’d calculate its volume (let’s call it 14 liters), then make some assumptions about its temperature and humidity (around 35°C, 75% RH), then decide what you want its final relative humidity to be (let’s bring it down to 20% RH). Run these numbers and you’d find you needed to pull about 0.3 grams of water out of the air in your balloon. This can be done, pretty reliably, with a one- or two-gram packet of silica gel, slipped into the balloon just before you blow it up.
Of course, different applications will entail different goals. The bag that holds your potato chips is not
completely
impermeable to moisture, and if you’re going to ship it across an ocean and then let it sit on a shelf for a few months, you should expect some additional water vapor to find its way in. There are also applications in which silica gel is used not so much to dry something out but to maintain a particular equilibrium humidity. In the art world, silica gel packets are slipped into exhibit cases and
used for their “buffering capacity,”
helping maintain a stable (and relatively high) humidity inside the case while conditions in the rest of the gallery might vary.
Silica gel is commonly placed inside museum display cases, in hidden compartments that ventilate to the display chamber. Image via the National Park Service's *very* thorough
Exhibit Conservation Guidelines, Second Edition
.
While glass and glassy substances have been used by humans for many thousands of years, it wasn’t until the early twentieth century that Walter Patrick, a researcher at Johns Hopkins, developed
and patented
an efficient way to create silica gel. He did this by mixing a substance called “water glass” with an acid.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程训练营（bootcamps）的现状及其与就业市场的关系，特别是与大学毕业生的竞争。

不同观点：
• [对ISAs（收入分享协议）的看法分歧]  
  ◦ 一部分人曾经对Lambda School采用ISAs表示赞扬，认为这是一种帮助学生在没有前期成本的情况下完成学业的好方法。  
  ◦ 然而，随着Lambda School被曝出存在一些掠夺性行为，公众对ISAs的看法变得负面。

• [编程训练营的就业市场状况]  
  ◦ 有人质疑编程训练营是否仍然表现良好，尤其在当前就业市场似乎无法为传统大学毕业生提供足够的岗位。这暗示训练营毕业生的就业前景可能更加严峻。

补充讨论：
• [ISAs的潜在问题]  
  ◦ ISAs虽然初期被认为是减轻学生经济负担的创新方式，但由于某些机构的掠夺性行为，这种模式的实际效果和道德性受到质疑。

• [就业市场竞争]  
  ◦ 讨论中提到大学毕业生和编程训练营毕业生之间的就业竞争，反映了科技行业就业市场可能供过于求的担忧。这表明不仅训练营的学生，即使是大学毕业生也在面临就业挑战。

争议焦点：ISAs是否是帮助学生负担教育的好方法，以及编程训练营毕业生在当前就业市场中的竞争力。

主要讨论点：科学实验中的精确性、科学教育中的评分标准、科研工作中的现实问题以及科学历史的背景。

不同观点：
• [jerf的观点] 科学实验中的精确性难以保证，尤其是在使用不精确的工具（如老式手表）时。jerf指出，在高中物理实验中使用这种工具测量重力加速度，结果非常不准确，且这种不准确在科学教育中往往得不到宽容。他进一步批评科学教育和科研中对“正确”结果的追求，认为科学家经常在数据不理想的情况下“捏造”结果。

• [roadbuster的观点] 支持jerf的经历，认为其揭示了大学本科生活中的现实，并提到jerf后来转向了计算机科学领域，最终取得了博士学位，这表明在面对科学实验和教育中的挫折时，职业生涯的转向可能是解决办法。

• [sevensor的观点] 分享了在教授半导体制造实验课时的类似经历，强调了实验安全的重要性，同时也对学生在实验中遇到的困难和实验结果的不准确表示理解，认为这种情况很常见。

• [cosmic_quanta的观点] 提到在其研究的超快凝聚态物理领域中，存在通过曲线拟合来合理化不准确数据的现象，且往往不呈现残差或其他拟合优度测试，暗示这种做法在科研中可能广泛存在。

• [HiPHInch的观点] 提到在量子化学计算研究中遇到的困难，特别是许多研究工作是闭源的，难以复现。此外，使用非自由许可的软件（如Origin和MS Word）也增加了协作和复现的难度。

• [aylmao的观点] 提供了jerf的教育和职业背景信息，强调他最终在计算机科学领域取得了成功，并在知名公司工作，这与他在物理实验中的挫折形成对比。

• [janandonly的观点] 认为jerf的帖子揭示了物理科学中的现实问题，并对其进行了讽刺，表明对物理科学的选择和其带来的挫折感。

• [joquarky的观点] 提供了对jerf实验失败的总结，并提到其对物理学研究的失望，最终选择了计算机科学，这与原文内容一致。

• [jpmattia的观点] 强调了固体物理学中的能带结构理论的美丽和重要性，认为其对社会的改变是显著的，暗示对科学研究应有更深的理解和欣赏。

• [shadowgovt的观点] 通过讲述华氏温标的历史背景，说明了早期科学测量中的实际问题和解决方案，提供了对科学实验中工具和方法的历史视角。

• [smaddox的观点] 提供了关于如何正确测量半导体材料电阻率的技术细节，强调了使用专业设备（如四探针法）的重要性，指出了在科学实验中使用正确方法和工具的必要性。

• [jpm_sd的观点] 认为本科实验中的挫折如果能放在历史背景中理解，可能会更容易接受，并建议在教学中更好地解释历史上的科学发现过程，以帮助学生理解和应对实验中的困难。

补充讨论：

data.title: Parrots and humans share a brain mechanism for speech
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 一项发表于2025年3月19日《Nature》的研究显示，小型鹦鹉（虎皮鹦鹉，*Melopsittacus undulatus*）的大脑具有类似于人类语言产生的机制。纽约大学Langone Health的神经科学家Michael Long及其同事发现，虎皮鹦鹉大脑中的前弓状体区域存在与发声相关的神经细胞，其组织方式类似于“声音键盘”，可以产生各种声音，类似于人类语言的灵活性。这种相似性可能是趋同进化的结果，即人类和鹦鹉分别演化出相似的语言机制。研究人员正试图利用机器学习解析鹦鹉的“语言”，以进一步理解其交流内容及其与人类语言的相似性。这项研究可能挑战“人类独特性”的观念。

By

When it comes to speech, parrots have the gift of gab. And the way the brains of small parrots known as budgerigars bestow this gift is
remarkably similar to human speech
, researchers report March 19 in
Nature
.
So far, budgerigars are the only animals known to have language-producing centers akin to those in humans, says Michael Long, a neuroscientist at New York University Langone Health. This “is really the first nonhuman animal in which that has been shown.” Understanding how speech gets created in budgies’ brains could help clarify what goes wrong in certain communication disorders in people.
Sign up for our newsletter
We summarize the week's science breakthroughs every Thursday.
Budgerigars (
Melopsittacus undulatus
) are tropical-colored,
smart
cutie pies. Beyond their looks, these parrots are particularly social and chatty, making them interesting research subjects for language studies.
Budgerigars have complex conversations, perhaps enabled by the “vocal keyboard” in their brains.
Long and his Langone Health colleague Zetian Yang tracked the behavior of individual nerve cells in four of these birds’ brains as they produced their chirrups. The activity of these cells, nestled in a part of the brain called the anterior arcopallium, is tied to the sounds the birds make, the duo found.
The organization of these neurons’ activity, it turns out, is pretty simple, Long says. He compares this neural organization to a keyboard that can produce a range of sounds — consonants, vowels, high pitches and low pitches. A budgie “is able to generate arbitrary sounds in its universe by just playing this vocal keyboard,” Long says. Overall, this flexible system has a humanlike organization.
The similarities
between human and parrot brains
may reflect two species solving a problem in a similar way, neurally speaking. These parallels could be “a very tidy example of convergent evolution, where you have humans that have developed this kind of neural mechanism for speech, and these parrots have developed a kind of similar mechanism,” Long says.
Now that scientists know more about how budgie brains help the birds talk, another question dogs Long: What are these parrots talking about?
“We are trying now to translate budgie,” he says, using advanced machine learning to determine what each warble and chirp means. Perhaps their language itself — not just the way their brain creates it — is similar to that of people. With these kinds of experiments, Long says, “maybe we can start to reexamine the notions of human exceptionalism.”

data.title: Train and Weather Tracker with Raspberry Pi and E-Ink
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个使用Raspberry Pi和电子墨水屏构建的火车与天气追踪器项目。作者为了方便自己和妻子每天早上快速查看即将到来的地铁F线和G线的到站时间以及天气情况，开发了这个设备。该设备使用9.7英寸电子墨水屏和Raspberry Pi 4b，显示内容包括日期、时间、实时秒针、未来30分钟的火车到站时间、通勤天气以及未来12小时的天气预报。设备通过MTA API获取火车到站信息，并能以较为精准的时间显示即将到来的列车。软件部分包括显示引擎、布局系统、数据服务和应用控制器，采用了模块化架构。由于电子墨水屏的刷新率限制，作者采用了混合更新策略以减少鬼影现象并确保显示正常工作。整个项目代码和说明可以在GitHub上找到。

43517439.article_content:
Train & Weather Tracker with Raspberry Pi & E-Ink
March 2, 2025
Art
,
Physical
,
Software
I finally built a Raspberry Pi project my wife loves: an e-ink train and weather tracker! If you want to build one yourself,
the Github & instructions are here.
Kira will be jogging to the night shift!
Over the past few years, I've been on something of an e-ink journey.  I started with a
weather and news display
(still the only post on my website that regularly gets organic traffic.) While I loved it and it looked great, a phone is a better way to check the news, and the weather only gets checked once a day. Then in 2022 while at MIT I built
Jarvis, the e-ink voice-to-image display
. Jarvis was a great party trick — say, "Hey Jarvis, paint me an elephant on a bowling ball in Times Square" and watch as the image gradually appeared. Notably, this was before ChatGPT, when people were still impressed by AI!
Jarvis live demo is better!
Then over Thanksgiving, I had some free time, a basket of spare parts, and the itch to code and build something physical. So here we are with the e-ink train and weather tracker.
The idea is simple: Every morning, my wife and I take the inbound F or G subway lines to work from a stop that's a 2-minute jog or a 6-minute walk from our house. I love the NYC subway and it works incredibly well, but the trains come
often
and
predictably
, not
on-a-schedule
. So every morning we're calling out, when's the next G, when's the next F — and one of us pulls out a phone for the MTA app or Google Maps and yells back the upcoming train times. Then we time our morning routines to either stretch for a train in three minutes or slow down for a train in ten.
The subway and weather tracker makes checking train times much faster and calmer than pulling out a phone. Since it's centrally located in our home, someone is always close enough to glance at it.
The subway times reported by the
MTA API
are reliable once the train is within a few stops or 15 minutes away, with precision increasing as the trains get closer. Having the train times on the wall lets you check how your morning routine is developing against the train schedule as the departure time gets closer.
Best of all, Kira loves it! This goes on my DIY pantheon along with adding legs to her dresser to make it a better height and fixing a towel rack right before she hosted her colleagues for a book club.
If you want to build one yourself or better understand the project, I'll dive into some editorial and gotchas below. The practical instructions, parts, and code live in this
GitHub Repo
.
Description & Features
The train & weather tracker is built on a
9.7" 1200x825 E-Ink display
attached to a
Raspberry Pi 4b
. The display is split into four parts: a header, with date, time, and a live second hand to indicate liveness; a train tracker; the commute weather; and a "weather bar" displaying the next 12 hours of weather. The main focus of the layout is the train tracker, which shows the upcoming 30 minutes of inbound F & G trains.
The display sits in a laser cut mat board with black ridges sized to hide the black border of the e-ink display. The mat board sits in a 8.5" x 11" cherry frame that is 1.5" deep to allow the raspberry pi to be backmounted while the frame is still flush to the wall. We hang the display next to the door above a key holder, which is generally the right place for it, but also helps hide the power cord.
Not pretty, but it works
Project Details
The software portion of the project is manageable although there are some gotchas when programming against the Waveshare e-ink hat in particular. We have a modular architecture with a clear separation of concerns:
Display Engine: Renders the layout to the display, supporting communication with the physical e-ink display or rendering a png for non-raspberry pi development
Layout System: A pretty hacky visual arrangement of the elements. It'd be fun to do something more sophisticated here (e.g. a html renderer), but 🤷‍♂️. This will likely require the most work if you want to modify the project
Data Services: Fetch & process (this is important!) train arrival from NYC Transit GTFS feeds + get the weather forecasts
Application Controller: Orchestrate the event loop and subscription model to drive updates to the display
The biggest technical constraint is the update rate to the e-ink display. The display supports multiple update modes with different tradeoffs and
can
manage sub 500 ms updates, especially for partial updates, but a faster refresh results in fuzzy characters and substantial ghosting that looks pretty bad. The bigger issue is that overloading the display causes it to crash, which requires a full reset.
After some testing, I chose a hybrid display update strategy.
Every second, the pixels around the seconds & minutes digits of the time are rerendered with the display's fastest partial update mode to make it clear that the display is functioning as expected.

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Android系统逐渐变得与iOS相似，失去了曾经的开放性和高度自定义特性。过去，Android以其开放源代码、可轻松解锁和刷机（root）、支持侧载应用和自定义ROM等特点，与苹果的封闭系统形成鲜明对比。用户和开发者社区围绕这些特性形成了活跃的生态，但如今，大多数Android手机厂商已锁定硬件，禁止解锁bootloader，刷机可能导致银行和流媒体应用失效。Google也在限制侧载应用。文章以OnePlus为例，说明其从鼓励刷机和自定义，到被Oppo合并后转向类似苹果的封闭生态。过去，自定义ROM如CyanogenMod让老旧设备获得新功能，但现在这种文化和工具（如Xposed）已逐渐消失，Android的“西部狂野”时代已结束。

主要讨论点：用户对现代智能手机及其功能变化的看法

不同观点：
• [对手机操作系统归属感的丧失]  
   - eadmund认为现代智能手机已经不再属于用户自己，而是被大公司如Google、Microsoft和Apple控制。  
   - 他提到只有Linux电脑还能算作用户自己的，但也调侃称部分归属给了一个叫Lennart的人（可能是指系统开发者）。

• [华为被禁对Android生态的影响]  
   - MaxPock认为华为被禁止使用Google Play商店后，Android失去了创新动力。  
   - 华为曾是Android生态创新的主要推动力，MaxPock以自己的2019年P30 Pro为例，认为其性能至今仍能媲美最新的旗舰手机。

• [手机功能得失的个人体验]  
   - don-code详细描述了自己多年来更换手机的经历，认为手机在某些方面失去了功能，却没有得到足够的补偿。  
   - 例如从Treo 650换到HTC Sensation时，失去了物理键盘和易用的操作系统，虽然获得了Wi-Fi和更好的网络连接，但后续更换手机时，感觉功能提升有限，且失去了可更换电池和更好的相机。  
   - 他担心未来的手机将失去更多实用功能（如耳机插孔、可更换电池、SD卡槽等），且无法满足个人需求。

补充讨论：
• [对IR blaster消失的遗憾]  
   - tootie提到红外发射器（IR blaster）曾是非常实用的功能，但现在几乎没有手机配备这一功能。  
   - don-code也提到自己从未使用过HTC M9上的IR blaster，表明这一功能对部分用户可能并不常用，但对需要的人仍有价值。

争议焦点：
• 华为被禁对Android生态的影响程度  
   - MaxPock认为华为被禁对Android生态的创新造成了重大打击，而其他评论未直接回应这一观点，显示出对该问题可能存在不同看法。  
  
• 手机功能的变化是否为进步  
   - don-code认为手机在功能上有得有失，但整体上失去的功能更为重要，而其他用户可能认为技术的自然迭代带来了足够的补偿。

43572824.article_content:
Quick Links
Android’s Wild West Days Are Long Over
The End Of Hyper-Customization and Tinkering
Hardware On Android Has Gone the Way of the iPhone
Copy-Paste Designs
Google Is Making It Harder To Sideload Apps
Android and iOS used to be fierce rivals, but these days, they feel more and more like twins. Locked hardware, walled software gardens, uniformity in design, and lacking customization were once Apple's distinctive traits, but over the years, Android adopted them, too. Let's take a look at the iPhone-ification of Android.
Android’s Wild West Days Are Long Over
When it first came out, Android stood in perfect contrast to the iPhone's iOS. Apple was closed-source, but Android was open-source. You couldn’t unlock or jailbreak an iPhone that easily, but you could root an Android in seconds. Back when rearranging icons was the extent of customization on iOS, Android handed us the keys to the kingdom.
Sideloading apps,
modding culture
, easy access to the Play Store for indie developers, apps like that could link with other apps to build sophisticated automations, and the bold, experimental hardware concepts that made Android the Linux of phones (whose kernel it’s built on).
Thriving communities grew around Android’s openness and empowerment that iOS couldn't hope for with its walled garden. Tinkerers and enthusiasts shared resources and helped each other on online forums. It was rebellious and exciting.
Close
That’s all long gone now, though. Almost every manufacturer has locked down their hardware.
You can’t
unlock bootloaders
on most phones, and even if you manage to somehow root your phone, it’s (almost) certainly going to break banking apps and DRM-protected apps like Netflix.
Android phones ship with something called the “Play Integrity API” that tells apps “don’t trust this user,” if they’ve rooted or unlocked the phone.
The community around Android modding has mostly fizzled out. There are fewer and fewer custom ROMs floating around that once kept your phone going long after official manufacturer support ended. Google is also trying to take away sideloading now (more on that later).
OnePlus is the poster child for this shift. The original OnePlus phone was a “flagship killer” that shipped with Cyanogen OS (built on the beloved custom ROM CyanogenMod). It delivered on the promise because it really did have killer features for its wallet-friendly price. OnePlus encouraged modding and tinkering, which earned it a lot of power users. Forums always buzzed with OnePlus discussions and resources.
Close
OnePlus phones had almost no bloat; it was easy to unlock them, and they supported
custom recovery options
. Eventually, OnePlus merged with the Chinese smartphone brand Oppo, and Oppo’s custom Android skin (ColorOS) cannibalized OxygenOS. Then came the bootloader lockdown, more bloat, missed software updates, and an Apple-style ecosystem lock-in. Unlocking and rooting these phones is almost impossible now.
The End Of Hyper-Customization and Tinkering
With complete control over your phone’s hardware, you can push customization and modding to the extreme. Back then, you could replace the default firmware of your phone with a custom version of the Android operating system. These custom ROMs would have features that mainstream Android didn’t. You could create snapshot backups of your entire phone that restore everything, down to the layout of your home screen apps.
Take CyanogenMod, for example. I had a Samsung Galaxy Europa back in the day that ran Android 2.2 (codename Android Froyo) with Samsung’s TouchWiz skin on top. Officially, you couldn’t upgrade that phone past Android Froyo.
By the time Android Ice-cream Sandwich (Android 4.4) rolled around, Samsung had long dropped support for my phone. I desperately wanted to get my hands on it, but being a broke middle-schooler, I couldn’t afford a brand-new phone. So I did what anyone in my situation would in those days: I rooted my phone and installed CyanogenMod (custom ROM based on Android ICS 4.4).
Close
I remember feeling giddy the first time I saw the CyanogenMod boot screen on my old phone. And just like that, my phone had Android ICS, plus tons of features that even the official Android 4.4 didn’t. CyanogenMod introduced customized app permissions well before mainstream Android. It gave you granular control over the data and hardware that apps can access, just like you get on modern Android phones. It even had a kill switch that revoked any app’s internet access.
You could customize everything about the UI natively—fonts, icons, status bar, notification shade, lock screen, animations, widgets, remapping hardware keys, you name it. Best of all, it made my old phone run faster than it ever did on Samsung’s version of Android.
Even if you didn’t swap the entire OS, you could customize the native firmware using tools like
Xposed
in a modular fashion. You could overclock or underclock the CPU, freeze apps to save battery life, cut bloatware, and keep your phone

data.title: An image of an archeologist adventurer who wears a hat and uses a bullwhip
data.author: participant3
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容的合法性、创造性以及对社会的影响

不同观点：
• **AI生成内容是“盗窃机器”**：一些用户（如jauntywundrkind、MgB2、mcv）认为AI生成内容只是对训练数据的重复和模仿，缺乏创造性，且有可能侵犯知识产权。他们指出，AI生成与原作品几乎一致的内容，类似于剽窃行为。

• **知识产权法的批判与废除呼声**：psychoslave和burnished对知识产权法本身提出质疑，认为现行的知识产权法并不公平，且多为大公司控制和牟利的工具。他们主张废除或缩减知识产权法，认为解决人类基本需求更为重要。

• **AI的“默认模式”与创造性局限**：fidotron和TrackerFF提到AI生成器往往依赖于某种“默认模式”，产生过于通用的结果，缺乏独特性。这种现象限制了AI的实际应用，使得生成的内容缺乏真正的创新。

• **AI生成工具的合法使用与版权问题**：alkonaut和SLHamlet认为，使用AI生成内容并不能规避版权问题，用户仍可能面临法律风险。SLHamlet还指出，尽管AI可以生成原创故事，但需要极其详细的长提示，这使得直接由人类创作更为实际。

• **AI生成内容的未来与数据质量问题**：willvarfar预测，未来的编程语言和数据质量会受到当前LLM生成内容的影响，未来互联网可能充斥更多低质量和虚假信息。traverseda则提出，可以通过向量相似性搜索解决部分版权问题。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的“防护栏”问题**：一些用户（如flenserboy、htrp）担心AI工具中的“防护栏”设置过于严格，可能导致合法使用受限。burnished和fidotron则批评这些防护措施是自利和虚伪的。

• **AI在历史与媒体中的影响**：TrackerFF提出，随着AI对旧照片和媒体的修改，未来历史学家可能面临辨别真实性的困难，这引发了对历史保存和真实的担忧。

• **不同AI生成器的对比**：xnx指出，不同AI生成器（如ChatGPT与Google's Gemini/Imagen 3）在生成知识产权内容上的表现不同，表明技术实现和训练数据对生成结果的影响。

争议焦点：
• **AI生成内容的合法性与道德问题**：主要围绕AI生成内容是否构成知识产权侵犯，以及现行法律和防护措施是否足够和合理。
• **AI的创造性与人类创作的对比**：讨论了AI是否能够真正实现创造性，还是仅仅是对已有内容的模仿和重组。

data.title: AI cheats: Why you didn't notice your teammate was cheating
data.author: duckling23
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了游戏作弊技术的发展，特别是从内存读取的 aimbots 到基于颜色的 colorbots，再到如今的AI辅助瞄准。作者 vike256 分享了自己在游戏作弊领域的经验，包括早期使用 Android 手机制作作弊程序，以及后来开发了开源 colorbot "Unibot"。Colorbots 通过分析屏幕上的颜色来识别敌人，但并不适用于所有游戏。AI 作弊则是 colorbots 的进化版，利用训练过的AI模型在不同游戏中实现作弊功能。由于这些作弊手段需要额外硬件和复杂的设置，成本高且难以检测，普通玩家和反作弊系统很难发现。最终，作者指出，如今的作弊者面临高成本和被封禁的风险，而普通玩家很难察觉到轻微的作弊行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何有效检测和应对在线游戏中的作弊问题，以及作弊对游戏环境和社会的影响。

不同观点：
• **fracus**：认为应该采用统计方法或陷阱账号（honeypot method）来检测作弊者，并建议在竞技场景中要求玩家提供身份证明以确保 accountability。
• **ineedasername**：指出一些作弊者为了绕过反作弊系统需要进行繁琐的操作，如重刷BIOS和重装系统，质疑这种行为是否值得。同时，对作弊者通过作弊获取胜利的心态表示不理解。
• **RALaBarge**：认为匿名性是作弊问题的根源，提出需要引入某种中心化的身份识别机制和对现实生活中的惩罚措施来遏制作弊行为。
• **ultimafan**：通过观察发现队友作弊时，其他队友往往选择无视，因为他们可以享受胜利而不必亲自使用作弊手段，从而避免内疚感。
• **nkrisc**：感叹有些人为了破坏他人的游戏乐趣而不惜一切代价。
• **nathants**：认为单人游戏模式更好，因为无法责怪队友，同时讨论了硬件摄像头反作弊和内核级反作弊的必要性。
• **thesuitonym**：不理解为什么有人会频繁使用作弊软件，认为这种行为不如观看别人玩游戏。
• **kibwen**：希望无法阻挡的作弊手段能够摧毁依赖随机队友的竞争性在线游戏市场。
• **twic**：提出一种自我调侃的应对方法，即玩得非常差以避免遇到作弊者。

niila.fi
<- Posts
Posted: 2025-04-03
AI cheats: why you didn’t notice your teammate was cheating
For the past few years, cheats have evolved rapidly. First came memory reading aimbots, then colorbots, and now AI aim assist. Cheats have escaped the host PC. How does it affect the players and anti-cheats?
vike256
That's me, or the handle that I use online. I've been in the video game hacking scene on and off for what seems like forever. I don't know the exact point when I stumbled upon it, but I was making my first cheats on my Android phone when I was 12.
I didn't have a PC at the time, so I sat on my bed with a rooted phone in my hands that had GameGuardian installed. I remember writing a trainer with Lua for a game called Growtopia. I've since gotten a PC and programmed a few more cheats. Most notably Unibot, an open-source colorbot.
[1]
Image of Unibot debug screen while detecting an enemy. Green box is the detection area. Red box is the target.
Read more
Colorbots, why they work... or don’t
Colorbots read the enemy positions from the screen. They scan every pixel and filter based on enemy colors. It works for games that have colored enemy highlights or outlines.
Their flaw is that they don't work in every game, and they can merge multiple enemies into a single target if they are too close together. This can lock the cheater’s aim between enemies, unable to shoot either.
Image of someone having issues with multiple enemies merging into a single target. The user seems to be using Unibot.
The post
Colorbots became popular as the first cheats to achieve aimbot without memory reading. Colorbots are quite hard to detect. You can essentially just plug in a capture card to your PC and pass the images to another PC that the cheat runs on.
The aimbot input can be sent along with your normal mouse input through an Arduino or a KMBox. Just plug the KMBox to your PC and connect both the cheat PC and your mouse to it.
Diagram of how a 2PC cheat could function. This would work for both AI and colorbot cheats.
AI cheats are essentially advanced colorbots
Colorbots don't work on all games, because not all games have distinct enemy colors. This is where AI comes in. Developers train AI models to detect enemies, then distribute these models to users. This makes a single cheat work on every game imaginable.
So, the host PC only has a capture card and a "mouse" plugged into it, and the second PC runs the cheat. The anti-cheat has no idea, and...
You have no idea
You probably won’t notice the cheat while spectating, because cheat developers are intentionally nerfing their cheats to evade detection. Anti-cheats have made cheats more expensive, time-consuming, and less effective.
Today's cheats cost more but do less. Now a typical cheater needs an extra PC, external hardware, and $5-500 monthly payments just to bypass a decent anti-cheat.
After all that, they are still at a risk of getting banned. Cheaters must reflash their BIOS, wipe their PCs, reinstall Windows, and create a new account to play again. That's not something I'd like to do once a few weeks.
Cats seems to be the most helpful bunch among cheater forums.
So you being unable to spot a slight aim assist while spectating is normal. Of course you'll notice the aim assist if the player is insanely bad and has the aimbot configured wrong, but that's just plain stupidity being witnessed.
[1] Unibot is an open-source colorbot I made late 2023. It was not the first of its kind but it made waves within the cheating community. It was the first user-friendly, modifiable colorbot compatible with games like Valorant, Overwatch, and Roblox.
...yes Roblox. It has many FPS games that people play. Bad Business and Rivals are my favorites, but most people seemed to use Unibot for Arsenal. Unibot had a config file that you could use to change the important values. It was the first time users would not have to touch code to make the cheat work on their favourite game.
Unibot is still available on my GitHub. If you’re interested, check out the
GitHub Wiki
. The documentation is quite good for a game cheat.
43574929.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了游戏作弊技术的发展，特别是从内存读取的 aimbots 到基于颜色的 colorbots，再到如今的AI辅助瞄准。作者 vike256 分享了自己在游戏作弊领域的经验，包括早期使用 Android 手机制作作弊程序，以及后来开发了开源 colorbot "Unibot"。Colorbots 通过分析屏幕上的颜色来识别敌人，但并不适用于所有游戏。AI 作弊则是 colorbots 的进化版，利用训练过的AI模型在不同游戏中实现作弊功能。由于这些作弊手段需要额外硬件和复杂的设置，成本高且难以检测，普通玩家和反作弊系统很难发现。最终，作者指出，如今的作弊者面临高成本和被封禁的风险，而普通玩家很难察觉到轻微的作弊行为。

data.title: Tenstorrent Launches Blackhole Developer Products at Tenstorrent Dev Day
data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: Tenstorrent在旧金山Dev Day活动中发布了新一代Blackhole™芯片系列，专为高效处理大规模AI工作负载设计，具备无限扩展能力。新产品包括：Blackhole™ p100（999美元）、Blackhole™ p150（1,299美元）以及TT-Quietbox液冷工作站（11,999美元）。这些产品采用6nm制程，具备更快的片上网络（NoC）和更高的内存密度，并增加了RiscV核心。Tenstorrent还推出了Developer Hub，为开发者提供模型支持、教程和资源。所有Blackhole™产品均支持开源软件栈，可在Tenstorrent官网和GitHub上获取。此外，Tenstorrent还宣布与ECOBLOX和UnsungFields达成战略合作，推动中东、非洲及AI云平台的扩展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tenstorrent硬件平台的技术规格、应用场景及其市场竞争力

不同观点：
• [rasengan0] 认为Tenstorrent开发者支持的模型过滤功能不错，但建议增加对Blackhole RISCV p100a p150型号的支持，并根据内存规格推测其性能可与n300型号媲美。
• [wincy] 对Tenstorrent的技术感到困惑，不确定是否值得关注，并询问是否可以运行Deepseek R1模型，显示出对实际应用场景的关注。
• [jauntywundrkind] 用幽默的方式将数据处理比喻为AI发出霍金辐射，虽未深入技术讨论，但表现出对AI处理能力的抽象理解。
• [mika6996] 质疑Tenstorrent Blackhole卡的竞争力，表明对市场定位的疑虑。
• [littlestymaar] 强调Tenstorrent需要在卡上增加更多VRAM，并对比中国公司对Nvidia GPU的改装，提出价格与性能的期望，认为现有产品内存不足且兼容性问题会限制其成功。
• [mixmastamyk] 对RISC-V作为AI加速器的角色表示疑问，并通过查找FAQ找到答案，显示出对技术原理的兴趣。
• [lostmsu] 调侃Tenstorrent销售张量加速器却不提及TOps（tera operations per second），质疑其性能透明度。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论（如[rasengan0]和[littlestymaar]）对Tenstorrent硬件的规格和市场定位提出了具体建议和批评，特别是关于内存容量和价格的讨论。
• 技术细节（如RISC-V的作用和TOps的缺失）也成为讨论焦点，表明用户对Tenstorrent产品的技术实现和透明度有一定要求。
• 整体来看，讨论反映出对Tenstorrent产品在性能、市场竞争力和应用场景方面的不同期待和关注。

Tenstorrent Launches Blackhole™ Developer Products at Tenstorrent Dev Day
Tenstorrent launched the next generation Blackhole™ chip family today at their DevDay event in San Francisco.
Share this article
Featuring all new RiscV cores, Blackhole™ is built to handle massive AI workloads efficiently and offers an infinitely scalable solution.
Blackhole™ products are now available for order on
tenstorrent.com
:
Blackhole™ p100, powered by one processor without Ethernet, active-cooled: available for $999
Blackhole™ p150, powered by one processor with Ethernet, and available in passive-, active-, and liquid-cooled variants: available for $1,299
TT-Quietbox, a liquid-cooled desktop workstation powered by 4 Blackhole™ processors: available for $11,999
Tenstorrent’s Blackhole™ PCIe cards have been updated to 6nm manufacturing, faster Network-on-Chip (NoC), higher memory density, and additional integrated RiscV cores.
Tenstorrent also launched the
Developer Hub
- a platform designed to offer model support, tutorial videos, bounties and resources to the developer community working on the Tenstorrent platform.
The Blackhole™ cards and TT-Quietbox are fully supported by Tenstorrent’s open source TT-Forge™, TT-NN™ TT-Metalium™, and TT-LLK software stacks, and can be found at
www.github.com/tenstorrent
.
About Tenstorrent
Tenstorrent is a next-generation computing company that builds computers for AI. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with U.S. offices in Austin, Texas, and Silicon Valley, and global offices in Belgrade, Tokyo, Bangalore, and Seoul, Tenstorrent brings together experts in the field of computer architecture, ASIC design, advanced systems, and neural network compilers. Tenstorrent is backed by Eclipse Ventures and Real Ventures, among others. Learn more at tenstorrent.com.

data.title: New nanoparticle therapies target two major killers
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国联邦政府对mRNA疫苗研究的资金支持是否会受到影响，以及该研究未来发展的前景。

不同观点：
• [对资金支持受影响的担忧] ceejayoz 引用了KFF Health News的报道，指出美国国立卫生研究院（NIH）的官员要求科学家从资助申请中删除所有关于mRNA技术的内容，暗示联邦对mRNA疫苗研究的支持可能面临风险。特别是，这一决定与卫生部长、长期反对疫苗的Robert F. Kennedy Jr.有关，这进一步加剧了对mRNA疫苗研究前景的担忧。

• [质疑科学机构的角色] pwdiscflatmajor 用讽刺的语气质疑科学和AAAS（美国科学促进会）是否成了“杀手”，暗示如果科学机构无法支持mRNA研究，可能会带来严重后果。这一评论可能反映了对科学研究受到政治干预的担忧。

• [对临床应用的期待] fnord77 关注mRNA疫苗研究的临床应用时间表，询问多久能实现临床部署。这一观点反映了对mRNA技术实际应用的期待，以及对研究进展的关注。

• [对动物实验的关注] moffkalast 提到目前的研究仅限于小鼠，暗示mRNA疫苗研究可能还处于早期阶段，尚未准备好进行大规模临床应用。这一观点强调了研究从实验室到临床应用之间可能存在的差距。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于联邦政府对mRNA疫苗研究的支持是否真的会受到政治干预，以及这种干预对研究进展和公共健康可能带来的影响。
• 各方对研究进展的实际状态（如是否仅在动物实验阶段）以及未来应用的时间表有不同看法，反映了对科学研究进展的关注和期待。

data.title: Show HN: GitMCP is an automatic MCP server for every GitHub repo
data.author: liadyo
data.article_summary: GitMCP 是一个能够为任何 GitHub 项目创建远程 MCP 服务器的工具。通过将 GitHub 项目 URL 中的 "github.com" 或 "github.io" 替换为 "gitmcp.io"，用户可以为 AI 助手提供更准确的代码上下文信息，提升其回应的准确性和相关性。GitMCP 支持读取代码仓库中的文件如 llms.txt、llms-full.txt 和 readme.md，并能与 GitHub Pages 及任何公开的 GitHub 仓库无缝协作。设置简单，兼容 Claude、Cursor、Windsurf 和 VSCode Insiders 等主流 MCP 兼容的 AI 工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitMCP项目的目的、实现方式、使用场景及其技术细节

不同观点：
• [kiitos] 对GitMCP的文档和使用说明表示不满，认为 landing page 缺乏足够的信息来理解项目的功能、要求、限制和约束。用户对于如何解析和转换数据以及实现MCP的具体内容感到困惑。
• [liadyo] 解释了GitMCP作为一个开源的远程MCP服务器，能够自动处理GitHub项目的文档，并提供了项目链接，说明了如何通过替换域名来访问该功能。
• [the_arun] 对GitMCP在GitHub仓库中的使用场景表示不理解，质疑为什么需要一个MCP服务器。
• [pcwelder] 建议使用一个单一的MCP服务器，通过工具调用参数接收repo路径或URL，以避免频繁配置的麻烦。
• [qwertox] 认为GitMCP的实现较为复杂，关注其在私有仓库（如GitLab或Bitbucket）上的应用，并建议提供Dockerfile以便于本地运行。
• [xena] 关心如何选择退出该服务，以避免自己的仓库被处理。
• [eagleinparadise] 遇到使用Cursor时的技术问题，并询问如何强制使用MCP服务器。
• [fallat] 对MCP的快速普及感到惊讶。

data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2022年感染新冠期间，尝试在自制的486电脑（原本是Compaq Deskpro 4/33i，后升级为83MHz Pentium Overdrive处理器）上安装AIX PS/2 v1.3操作系统的过程。作者从WinWorld下载了AIX 1.3，解压出94张软盘镜像，但由于系统为IDE接口，最初的引导镜像不兼容。经过多次尝试和排错，作者发现需要使用支持IDE驱动的特殊更新U436295，并重新制作安装盘。在解决VGA接口物理阻塞问题和更换硬盘后，最终成功进入安装界面，但因缺乏必要工具，未能完成安装。作者还提到安装过程中遇到的各种技术问题和调试步骤。

Installing AIX PS/2 v1.3 on a 486
Saturday, August 27, 2022
In late August of 2022, after two years of remaining relatively healthy, COVID-19 finally caught
up with me. Cut off from friendly gathering, working out, and even food that wasn’t protein bars,
a completely normal thought occurred to me: “How about I install AIX on my old 486?”
My 486 is, as I assume most extant 486es are today, a franken-486: a hodgepodge of pieces collected
over the course of thirty years, ultimately a
Ship of Theseus
of opportunity (yard sales!) and necessity (30 year old capacitors!). In my case, it’s actually not
correct to even call it a 486 anymore - while it might have started life as a Compaq Deskpro 4/33i
with a proper 33MHz 486DX CPU, it’s now sporting an 83MHz
Pentium Overdrive
.
But in my heart, it’s still my first computer.
I downloaded
AIX 1.3 from WinWorld
. This nicely
expanded into 94 floppy images! While I’m certain I don’t have 94 working floppies, I
do
have a
box of Verbatim DataLife floppies, which have a lifetime warranty (suppose they’d honor it?)…
and so far, haven’t let me down.
The floppy images
Boot_(ESDI)_01.img
,
Boot_(SCSI)_01.img
, and
Install.img
looked promising,
but I have an IDE system. I started out with
Install.img
(not bootable), then the ESDI image
(
also
not bootable). The SCSI image, at least, did bring me to a bootstrapper. Let’s try
“Boot from Diskette”…
In this menu, I selected the defaults -
unix.gen
,
Single User
, and
No
. I’m hoping that
translates to a kernel image on one of the install floppies, to bring the system up off the
floppies in single-user mode, and to not attempt a boot from the hard drive…
not
to give me a
single-user UNIX install, booted from floppies every time.
Switching floppies. I did this quite a bit.
I was then prompted to switch to the Installation Disk, which curiously, had to be writeable.
After loading this floppy, I briefly got some garbled video, and the machine reset. Assuming it was
a fluke, I tried again, and got the same behavior. Something very similar happens when this machine
boots Windows NT, even though it
does
eventually boot, so I decided to take my ATI Mach64 card
out, and try to install with the built-in VGA controller. There won’t be any Super VGA here.
And… the VGA cable won’t fit? It turns out that Compaq interpreted the VGA spec a little bit too
literally, and physically blocked pin 9 -
a key / no connect pin
.
I’ve barely ever seen a cable without pin 9 populated, so I ended up making one with a pair of
needlenose pliers and some elbow grease.
After restarting the process, I can now see some video output. Figuring the  hex address in the panic
output might be useful to Google, I turned up a
guide on running AIX in VirtualBox
. That, in turn, linked to an
install guide
, both of which were
helpful in later debugging.
I pursued a couple of other avenues after finding this:
I’d accidentally started asking it to load from the hard drive between reboots, and turned that
off, but saw no change.
This odd comment made me recreate the install disk - and left me mildly concerned about what
this would’ve meant if you’d bought the disks straight from IBM.
NOTE: In case of a bungled install, the Installation diskette will most likely be munged. If you are attempting an AIX install and it crashes and burns attempting to load the Install disk, recreate the install diskette.
A
blog post comment
made me
aware of the U436295 update, which supports IDE drives. I ended up finding the boot and install
images for those at
an entirely different site
-
note that the images in question are the ones suffixed with
-0024
.
These enabled me to get a bit further - once to a failed boot, with a
/bin/sh
that lacked anything
of substance in on its
PATH
- even
ls
wasn’t available, but the shell supported globbing
(
echo *
). I poked around for a bit, but didn’t find anything helpful. I
do
have device entries
for
/dev/rhd00
and
/dev/rhd32
, so I think drives were at least enumerated - but lacking any
tools, I can’t really tell if these correspond to my actual drives.
Some things I tried from here:
Assuming a fluke, I rebooted and hung during init. Several reboots didn’t help here - either/or
funtionality was possible. The message about hard drives was interesting, though - I’ve also had
problems while installing Windows 98 (though not NT), so I decided to try a different drive.
Unfortunately, I don’t exactly keep IDE drives around - but I
do
still have a CompactFlash-to-IDE
adapter from my old NAS. That needed a second floppy power connector, and I didn’t have one, so I
decided to test out this theory with a donor computer. A lot of re-jiggering my desk later, this
didn’t help.
An interesting thing I noted is that the sound of the floppy drive changed after the kernel loaded.

data.article_summary: Hatchet 是一个用于运行后台任务的平台，基于 Postgres 构建，帮助用户管理和分发任务，而无需自行维护任务队列或发布/订阅系统。它支持将复杂任务链组合成工作流、任务失败时发出警报、增强任务可靠性，并通过实时 web 仪表板查看任务状态。主要功能包括任务队列、任务编排（如 DAGs）、以及对任务的监控和调试支持。它适用于需要处理高负载、复杂任务逻辑以及任务可视化的场景，支持 Python、TypeScript 和 Go 等多种语言。通过 Hatchet，用户可以简化后台任务管理，提升应用的稳定性和可扩展性。

What is Hatchet?
Hatchet is a platform for running background tasks, built on top of Postgres. Instead of managing your own task queue or pub/sub system, you can use Hatchet to distribute your functions between a set of workers with minimal configuration or infrastructure.
When should I use Hatchet?
Background tasks are critical for offloading work from your main web application. Usually background tasks are sent through a FIFO (first-in-first-out) queue, which helps guard against traffic spikes (queues can absorb a lot of load) and ensures that tasks are retried when your task handlers error out. Most stacks begin with a library-based queue backed by Redis or RabbitMQ (like Celery or BullMQ). But as your tasks become more complex, these queues become difficult to debug, monitor and start to fail in unexpected ways.
This is where Hatchet comes in. Hatchet is a full-featured background task management platform, with built-in support for chaining complex tasks together into workflows, alerting on failures, making tasks more durable, and viewing tasks in a real-time web dashboard.
Features
📥 Queues
Hatchet is built on a durable task queue that enqueues your tasks and sends them to your workers at a rate that your workers can handle. Hatchet will track the progress of your task and ensure that the work gets completed (or you get alerted), even if your application crashes.
This is particularly useful for:
Ensuring that you never drop a user request
Flattening large spikes in your application
Breaking large, complex logic into smaller, reusable tasks

43572733.article_summary: Hatchet 是一个用于运行后台任务的平台，基于 Postgres 构建，帮助用户管理和分发任务，而无需自行维护任务队列或发布/订阅系统。它支持将复杂任务链组合成工作流、任务失败时发出警报、增强任务可靠性，并通过实时 web 仪表板查看任务状态。主要功能包括任务队列、任务编排（如 DAGs）、以及对任务的监控和调试支持。它适用于需要处理高负载、复杂任务逻辑以及任务可视化的场景，支持 Python、TypeScript 和 Go 等多种语言。通过 Hatchet，用户可以简化后台任务管理，提升应用的稳定性和可扩展性。

data.article_summary: 本文作者分享了在个人和工作中使用AI编程工具的积极体验，尤其是在提升生产力和代码质量方面取得了显著效果。尽管一些开发者反馈AI工具效果不佳，但作者认为，经验丰富的开发者实际上能够更有效地利用这些工具。AI助手像一个拥有丰富编程知识但缺乏具体项目架构 oversight的“高级开发者”，需要开发者进行策略性指导才能发挥其最大潜力。作者提出了三个关键能力：明确的需求、工具限制和文件关键帧。他通过具体项目示例展示了AI如何自动完成整个编码过程，例如创建“平台问题监控”应用，而作者本人并不熟悉Python语言。作者建议软件开发社区应尽早接纳AI工具，以推动整个行业的发展。

主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在软件开发中的应用及其对开发者的影响

不同观点：
• **necovek**：对使用LLM生成的代码质量持批评态度，认为代码质量低，像是初级开发者所写，存在设计和实现上的问题（如日志配置、竞态条件等）。
• **conductr**：作为业余编程爱好者，感到LLM和生成式编程正在削弱个人创造力，造成心理上的矛盾，既觉得LLM可以提供功能性解决方案，但又因为缺乏亲手构建的满足感而感到沮丧。
• **only-one1701**：指出LLM在绿地项目（从零开始的新项目）中表现良好，但在棕地项目（已有项目的维护和扩展）中效果较差。
• **burntcaramel**：支持LLM的使用，认为可以通过“探索”方式学习新知识，并提出使用测试驱动开发（TDD）来约束和验证生成的代码，以应对LLM生成代码的不确定性。
• **rs186**：反对使用LLM生成代码，认为生成代码的调试和修正成本太高，不如自己编写代码来得省心。
• **ramoz**：认为随着AI技术的进步，高级开发者和初级开发者之间的差距会缩小，AI将对高级开发者产生威胁，并提出通过设置适当的框架，高级工程师可以更自主地使用AI。
• **yoyohello13**：对LLM持积极态度，使用Claude CLI提高工作效率，尤其在编写单元测试和处理特定任务时，认为LLM可以有效分担工作。
• **jonnycoder**：认为编写详细的提示词是使用LLM成功的关键，并提出通过创建个人应用和个人品牌来应对AI时代的挑战。
• **mmazing**：分享使用LLM的实际经验，指出LLM在处理简单算法、诊断错误和讨论潜在策略时的价值，但认为实际编码的价值在于战略性思考和减少试错。
• **denkmoon**：认为高级开发者的核心技能（如需求分析、团队协调、项目管理等）不会被LLM取代，编码只是工作中的一小部分。
• **thisdougb**：对LLM的实际应用持谨慎态度，希望看到更多实际代码案例，并对AI生成代码的质量和文档水平提出疑问。
• **Quarrelsome**：认为LLM的实际应用填补了“AI取代工作”论述中的空白，特别指出通过前期设计可以自动化大部分工作，类似于瀑布模型的复兴。
• **scandox**：怀念与人类初级开发者互动的过程，认为这种互动有助于个人和团队的成长。
• **windows2020**：认为编写代码是一种自然的放松方式，LLM并未显著提高其工作效率，编码过程中的反思和理解更为重要。
• **noodletheworld**：质疑一些文章中声称“完全没有手写代码”的说法，认为这些说法不实且令人困惑。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：LLM生成代码的质量和实用性是主要争议点，一些开发者认为其生成的代码质量低，调试成本高，而另一些开发者则认为通过适当的方法和工具，LLM可以有效提高工作效率。
• **心理影响**：部分开发者（如conductr）感到LLM削弱了他们的创造力和满足感，而另一些开发者（如yoyohello13和mmazing）则认为LLM可以有效分担工作，提高效率。
• **高级开发者的角色**：一些观点（如denkmoon和ramoz）认为高级开发者的核心技能不会被LLM取代，但也有观点（如ramoz）认为AI将对高级开发者产生威胁。
• **实际应用**：讨论中涉及了LLM在绿地项目和棕地项目中的不同表现，以及通过TDD和框架设置来约束和验证生成代码的方法。

43573755.article_content:
Introduction
Over the past few months, I have been experimenting with AI-powered coding tools in both my personal and professional projects. The experience has been overwhelmingly positive, both for me and my team of software engineers at work.
We’ve achieved better results in less time, and in many cases, the quality of our output has significantly improved.
Interestingly, this experience contrasts with the feedback I’ve received from some fellow software developers who report that AI tools aren’t working well for them.
I’m now convinced that AI-assisted software development has the potential to elevate our craft to the next level in terms of productivity. This is why I believe our community should embrace it sooner rather than later — but like all tools and practices, with the right perspective and a measured approach.
My motivation for sharing these experiences and the best practices I’ve identified is to help move the needle forward in terms of AI adoption within the broader software development community — even if realistically, it’s only by some micrometers.
The Current State of AI Coding
Beyond “Vibe Coding”
My Twitter feed suggests that AI-powered coding tools are already generating significant buzz in a specific niche: non-professional developers who are having great fun building software products. For them, these tools primarily serve as enablers, allowing them to tackle projects they might never have considered without such assistance.
More power to them — it’s exciting to witness their journey of struggles and breakthroughs.
However, this represents just one segment of potential users, and certainly not the only group for whom these tools can provide immense value.
The Senior Developer Advantage
My current conclusion, though preliminary in this rapidly evolving field, is that not only can seasoned developers benefit from this technology — they are actually in the optimal position to harness its power.
Here’s the fascinating part: The very experience and accumulated know-how in software engineering and project management — which might seem obsolete in the age of AI — are precisely what enable the most effective use of these tools.
The AI Assistant: A Senior Coder, Junior Colleague
While I haven’t found the perfect metaphor for these LLM-based programming agents in an AI-assisted coding setup, I currently think of them as “an absolute senior when it comes to programming knowledge, but an absolute junior when it comes to architectural oversight
in your specific context
.”
This means that
it takes some strategic effort to make them save you a tremendous amount of work
.
And who better to invest that effort in the right way than a senior software engineer?
As we’ll see, while we’re dealing with cutting-edge technology, it’s the time-tested, traditional practices and tools that enable us to wield this new capability most effectively.
Key Areas of Expertise
I’ve identified three critical areas of expertise needed when working with AI-assisted coding:
Well-structured Requirements
Tool-based Guard Rails
File-based Keyframing
Before diving into these concepts, let me share some real-world examples of how I’ve used AI in my projects.
I will give examples for two categories of projects: green-field and brown-field.
For both categories, I’ll focus on cases where AI handled the entire implementation, or very nearly so.
While I do sometimes use AI as a “better autocomplete” or as a chat-only companion for general discussions, this article focuses on what I call the “real deal” — where AI tooling operates in an agentic mode and handles all the heavy lifting.
Development Environment
My current tool of choice for these projects is
Cursor
, powered by Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 3.7 model. For optimal developer experience, I prefer not to manually copy-paste generated code into my codebase and need the AI assistant to execute commands directly on my local command line. Cursor provides this capability, and I expect similar products would yield comparable results.
Example 1: Platform Problem Monitoring
This setup, combined with the expertise areas I’ll discuss, enabled me to create and fully implement a green-field application:
Platform Problem Monitoring
. You can find the source code at
https://github.com/dx-tooling/platform-problem-monitoring-core
.
The application connects hourly to our ELK stack’s Elasticsearch server, reads the latest error messages, and sends us a well-formatted email summarizing the current state of problems on our web platform:
For more details, check out the
“New project: Platform Problem Monitoring”
post.
What makes this example particularly interesting is that the entire source code was written by Cursor/Claude, without any manual coding from me.
This is especially noteworthy because I don’t actually know Python. Yes, with 25+ years of software development experience, I could probably write a few lines of working Python code if pressed — but I don’t truly
know
the language. I lack the musc

data.title: Banked Memories for Soft SIMT Processors
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了软SIMT处理器的分组存储器设计，旨在实现高带宽（最多16端口）和高速度（超过770 MHz）。作者比较了9种不同的存储架构，包括简单的多端口存储，并通过51个基准测试（涵盖不同算法和数据大小）进行评估，以帮助读者为特定应用选择合适的存储架构。结果表明，简单但更耗资源的多端口存储在许多情况下（尤其是小内存时）性能更高，但随着数据集增大，其资源消耗变得不可行。本文的分组存储实现提供了高带宽、高密度和高Fmax，适用于FPGA应用如高层次综合（HLS）。

Computer Science > Hardware Architecture

(cs)
[Submitted on 31 Mar 2025]
Title:
Banked Memories for Soft SIMT Processors
Authors:
Martin Langhammer
,
George A. Constantinides
View a PDF of the paper titled Banked Memories for Soft SIMT Processors, by Martin Langhammer and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Recent advances in soft GPGPU architectures have shown that a small (<10K LUT), high performance (770 MHz) processor is possible in modern FPGAs. In this paper we architect and evaluate soft SIMT processor banked memories, which can support high bandwidth (up to 16 ports) while maintaining high speed (over 770 MHz). We compare 9 different memory architectures, including simpler multi-port memories, and run a total of 51 benchmarks (different combinations of algorithms, data sizes and processor memories) to develop a comprehensive set of data which will guide the reader in making an informed memory architecture decision for their application. Our benchmarks are comprised of matrix transpositions (memory intensive) and FFTs (split between memory accesses, floating point, and integer computations) to provide a balanced evaluation. We show that the simpler (but more memory block intensive) multi-port memories offer higher performance than the more architecturally complex banked memories for many applications, especially for smaller memories, but the effective footprint cost of the multi-port memories quickly becomes prohibitive as dataset sizes increase. Our banked memory implementation results - high bandwidth, high Fmax, and high density - can be used for other FPGA applications as well, such as HLS (High Level Synthesis).

43573879.article_summary: 本文探讨了软SIMT处理器的分组存储器设计，旨在实现高带宽（最多16端口）和高速度（超过770 MHz）。作者比较了9种不同的存储架构，包括简单的多端口存储，并通过51个基准测试（涵盖不同算法和数据大小）进行评估，以帮助读者为特定应用选择合适的存储架构。结果表明，简单但更耗资源的多端口存储在许多情况下（尤其是小内存时）性能更高，但随着数据集增大，其资源消耗变得不可行。本文的分组存储实现提供了高带宽、高密度和高Fmax，适用于FPGA应用如高层次综合（HLS）。

data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了VMS操作系统的大小，特别是其源代码的行数。作者通过自定义程序统计了VMS多个版本（V6.2、V7.2、V8.2、V9.2-3）中15个核心组件的源代码行数，排除了空白行和注释行。结果显示，这15个组件在V8.2版本中总计约16.6万行代码，且这些组件的代码量在不同版本中几乎翻了三倍。VMS最初使用BLISS和MACRO-32编写，后来逐步转向C语言。每个新版本大约增加40万行代码，显示出VMS在不断发展和扩展。文章还提到，VMS源代码库包含409个组件，大小不一，共同构成了多平台的VMS操作系统。
