43573738.article_content:
How Big Is VMS?
This question was asked during my Boot Camp presentation last fall in Boston, and over the past 35 years dozens of times people have asked, how big is VMS? That translates into "how many lines of code are in VMS"? I thought it was time to at least make a stab at pursuing some insight into the answer. I wrote some command procedures to count the number of source lines in .B32, .B64, .C, .MAR, .M64, and .S files. Not counted are blank lines and lines beginning with the standard comment characters and miscellaneous directives for the particular language.
First, I needed a baseline definition of  'VMS'.
Does it include layered products, networking, compilers, RTLs, debuggers, open source, etc.?
Is it the code on a particular running system?
Does it include command procedures?
I said 'no' to all of the above and as a starting point chose 15 facilities which are representative of identifiable components of the system: ACPI , AUDSRV, CLUSTER, DCL, DRIVER, F11X, JOBCTL, LAN, PCSI, RMS, SCSI, SDA, SHADOWING, SYS, XFC.
I chose the following releases for comparison:
V6.2:       May / 1995 - port to Alpha
V7.2:       Feb / 1999 - kernel threads, 64-bit APIs, Galaxy, and more
V8.2:       Feb /  2005 - port to Itanium
V9.2-3:     Dec / 2024 - port to x86
The LINES.COM procedure, which invokes a set of nested procedures, fetches all of the source files with the extensions mentioned above, in the SCSI facility that are in the release stream V8.2, gets the line counts, and produces the text file below. This was done for each of the 15 facilities in each of the four release streams.
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$ @lines scsi "V8.2" V82
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$ type [.scsi]total-line-counts-v82.txt
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.BLISS]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 2
Total source lines = 7770
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.C]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 64
Total source lines = 119609
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.M64]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 1
Total source lines = 885
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.MAR]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 34
Total source lines = 38414
WORK10:[GRANT.LOC.SCSI.S]TOTALS.TXT;1
Total source files = 0
Total source lines = 0
Grand Totals
Total source files = 101
Total source lines = 166678
MTMERU-V8.4-2L2$
Here are all the totals for V8.2. There is a similar chart for each of the other three releases.
Here is the lines of code summary for the four releases. You can find a graphical representation of the table below at this
link
.
Notes and Observations:
Not all code in a facility is in every release, but it is or has been in one or more releases.
There are 409 facilities in the VMS source pool - some big, some small. They contribute to the VMS operating system build for one or more platforms.
These 15 facilities chosen comprise close to two million lines of code and their total has nearly tripled in size during the last three releases.
There were many changes and additions to VMS between V8.2 and V9.2-3 prior to the x86 porting work.
Given a relatively small delta, each release has increased by about 400,000 lines of code.
The emergence of C code is another aspect of VMS that is part of the story. In the beginning, VMS was written in BLISS and MACRO-32 (VAX assembler). During the latter stages of the port to Alpha, we declared that all new code would be written in C. There are exceptions, of course, but for the most part we followed this guideline. Not shown in the data above, but part of this investigation, is the following which reflects the 15 facilities. (The 31 C modules in V6.2 were all written during the port to Alpha.)
It might be interesting to look into why some facilities have changed so much over time. Some seem obvious but others do not. If you have suggestions for a future post, please speak up.

data.title: Show HN: The Algorithm Behind the Topological Sort Library TopoSort
data.author: ww520
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了TopoSort算法的原理和实现，该算法基于Kahn算法，通过处理节点集而非单个节点来进行拓扑排序，并能识别无依赖子集和图中的循环节点。算法通过反复寻找并移除图中的根集（无依赖节点集）来实现拓扑排序，具体步骤包括：

1. 找到图的第一个根集；
2. 移除根集中的节点；
3. 重复以上步骤直到图为空。

每个根集内的节点相互无依赖，可以并行处理。通过记录节点是否已成为根节点，算法能够检测到图中的循环，并在出现循环时跳过相关节点，最终生成部分拓扑排序结果。未在根集列表中的节点即为循环的一部分。

TopoSort Algorithm
William Wong, 2025-04-02
The algorithm used in TopoSort is a variant to the Kahn's algorithm
in working on the nodes as sets instead of as individual nodes,
with the additions on finding dependence-free subsets and finding cyclic nodes.
Overview
The main idea is to iteratively find the successive root sets of the graph after
removing them at each round.  Here's a high level outline of the algorithm.
Find the first root set of the graph.
Remove the nodes of the root set from the graph.
Find the next root set. Go to 2 until the graph is empty.
The successively removed root sets form a topological order.
The nodes within each root set are dependence free in the root set.
Further the nodes are a topological order when lined up in the order
of the root sets.
Example
For a graph with nodes
{a, b, c, d, e, f}
, successively removed root sets look like:
{a, b} | {c, d, e, f}
{a, b} {d} | {c, e, f}
{a, b} {d} {c, e} | {f}
{a, b} {d} {c, e} {f}
Rationale
By definition, a topological order of the nodes of a directed acyclic graph (DAG)
is that the nodes are linearly ordered in such a way that
a node has no dependence on any other nodes coming after it.
In a DAG graph, there exist some nodes which depend on no other nodes.
These are the root nodes of the graph, where graph traversal begins from them.
These form the inital root set.
We define that when a node y depends on x, node y has an incoming link from x.
When node x is removed, the incoming link to y is removed as well.
Removing the nodes of a root set from the graph causes the remaining nodes
depending on them to have one less dependence, i.e. their incoming links decremented.
For the nodes whose incoming links reaching 0, they become the new root nodes
since they depend on no one.
We define that set A has no dependence on set B when all members of A have
no dependence on any member of B.
It follows that each root set removed during the iteration has no dependence
on any other root sets coming after it, thus the sequence of successively removed
root sets forms a topological order.
Dependence Free Subsets
The nodes in a root set have no dependence among themselves since root nodes
by definition depend on no other nodes.  These dependence free nodes in
a root set allow parallel processing within the scope of the root set.
When the nodes of all the root sets are lining up in the order of the root sets,
they form a topological order, too.
Cyclic Node Detection
A "rooted" list is used to track whether a node has become a root.
When traversing the dependents of a root node to find the next set of roots,
a dependent in the rooted list means it has already become a root
before.  That means a cycle exists in the graph linking an already rooted
node as a dependent for another node.
Instead of aborting, the traversing of the dependent of a root node can be
merely skipped. This stops going into the cycle and allows the algorithm to
continue with the rest of the nodes.  A partial list of the topological order
nodes can be produced at the end.
After the main iteration, any nodes not in the "rooted" list can be classified
as parts of the cycles since they were not reachable due to the prior cycle
skipping when traversing the dependents of root nodes.

data.title: A university president makes a case against cowardice
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 2025年，美国高等教育面临严峻挑战，特朗普第二任政府对高校的多样性、公平和包容努力展开调查，削减联邦资金，并驱逐参与亲巴勒斯坦活动的国际学生。哥伦比亚大学因联邦政府压力，同意改变政策，随后获得资金恢复，但其校长随后辞职。许多高校领导因担心职位和预算而不愿公开反对政府政策，但韦斯利安大学校长迈克尔·罗斯是个例外。罗斯自2007年起担任校长，积极发表文章，呼吁高校坚持原则。2023年，韦斯利安大学因最高法院裁决终止了传承录取政策。罗斯支持言论自由，并在加沙战争抗议中与学生发生冲突。他批评其他高校领导采用1967年芝加哥大学的《卡尔文报告》中的中立原则，认为这不过是避免麻烦的借口。面对特朗普政府对学术界的攻击，罗斯持续发声，敦促同行捍卫原则。在与作者的对话中，罗斯表示现实比他预期的更糟糕，许多高校不愿公开支持非党派活动，显示出对参与公共事务的犹豫。

不同观点：

• **对大学种族考虑的批评**：rahimnathwani指出，Wesleyan大学在招生过程中考虑种族因素，并为此在法律案件中辩护，这与自由民主的原则相悖。他认为，如果大学坚持这种做法，就不应获得任何形式的纳税人资助。

• **对捐赠者和财富影响的担忧**：mmooss提到，超级富豪正在形成一个主导阶层，影响大学的自由和民主。他质疑这些财富是否在攻击大学自由，并指出某些事件（如哈佛领导层的退出）可能与此相关。

• **反制措施的建议**：siliconc0w建议大学可以通过拒绝录取持有反教育政策的学生来捍卫其价值观。这种激进的做法旨在维护大学的教育使命。

Last Friday could have passed for a lovely spring day on the Connecticut campus of Wesleyan University. Students with books and laptops dotted a green hillside; flocks of admissions visitors trailed tour guides; baseball season had just begun, and practice was under way. It was almost possible to forget the grim straits of American higher education in 2025.
Colleges and universities have been early targets of the second Trump Administration. In the past month, the Administration has announced it will investigate diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts at more than fifty schools; cut hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding from such institutions as Johns Hopkins and the University of Pennsylvania; and sought to deport international students involved in pro-Palestinian activism. Columbia received a letter from the federal government issuing demands—which included making changes to discipline and admission policies, and placing the department of Middle East, South Asian, and African Studies under “academic receivership”—to be met as a “precondition” for negotiating the restoration of four hundred million dollars in federal funding. The university agreed to these demands the following week; the week after that, the university’s president resigned.
Columbia’s capitulation was in line with a general trend toward circumspection. The memory of Congress grilling university presidents in 2023 seems to be fresh among leaders in higher ed: few want to risk either their jobs or their budgets by saying the wrong thing. A handful of exceptions have stood out; for example, President Christopher Eisgruber, of Princeton, who wrote a piece for
The Atlantic
about “
The Cost of the Government’s Attack on Columbia
.” (This week, the Administration suspended dozens of grants to Princeton.) But perhaps none has been as voluble or persistent as Michael Roth, who has been president of Wesleyan since 2007.
Roth is a historian and a Wesleyan alumnus who, as an undergraduate, designed a major in the history of psychological theory. His scholarship has dealt with Freud and memory but also colleges as institutions, in books such as “
Safe Enough Spaces
” (2019) and “
The Student: A Short History
” (2023). Recent years have brought an increasingly political thrust to both his writing (for national media and his
presidential blog
) and to his work as president. In 2023, in response to the Supreme Court’s ruling against affirmative action, Wesleyan ended legacy admissions.
When Wesleyan students joined the national wave of protests over the war on Gaza, Roth—who describes himself as a supporter of both free speech and Israel’s right to exist—tangled with student protesters as well as with those who wanted him to shut the protests down. Meanwhile, in interviews and essays, he took administrators at other colleges to task for embracing the principles like those found in the “
Kalven report
”—a 1967 document out of the University of Chicago, which advanced the argument that universities should almost always remain scrupulously neutral. (Such stances were, he told me, “a cover for trying to stay out of trouble.”) As the Trump Administration has ramped up its attacks on the academy, Roth has continued to publish widely, urging fellow-leaders to stand up for their principles. “Release Mahmoud Khalil! Respect freedom of speech!” he concluded in
a recent column for
Slate
, which argued that the Columbia activist’s arrest “should terrify every college president.”
Roth and I met in his office, which is dominated by a round  table where he meets with both students and his cabinet. Wearing Blundstones and polka-dot socks, he was loose-limbed and gregarious, and our conversation (which has been edited for length and clarity) was punctuated by the bright sound of batting from the baseball diamond just outside.
You wrote last year, before the election, that colleges and universities weren’t ready for what was coming. How has the reality compared to your expectations?
It’s much worse than I expected.
I had this idea—alas, it was in 2020, just as
COVID
was happening—that it would be great if colleges and universities took our civic responsibilities more seriously and really incentivized students to participate in the public sphere: work on a campaign, zoning commission, whatever. Rigorously agnostic about what they chose to work on. We found a few hundred schools that agreed in principle and we created a network. Before the 2024 election, we reactivated that group, and this time around, the institutions were much less likely to want to be publicly in support of even something so nonpartisan.
We’re really small—three thousand students or so—and I wanted University of Texas at Austin, and Michigan, other big places. Some of them did agree in principle, but this time, in 2024—in the spring, let’s say, when Biden was still in the race, it was clear Trump was going to be the candidate—th
43568655.article_summary: 2025年，美国高等教育面临严峻挑战，特朗普第二任政府对高校的多样性、公平和包容努力展开调查，削减联邦资金，并驱逐参与亲巴勒斯坦活动的国际学生。哥伦比亚大学因联邦政府压力，同意改变政策，随后获得资金恢复，但其校长随后辞职。许多高校领导因担心职位和预算而不愿公开反对政府政策，但韦斯利安大学校长迈克尔·罗斯是个例外。罗斯自2007年起担任校长，积极发表文章，呼吁高校坚持原则。2023年，韦斯利安大学因最高法院裁决终止了传承录取政策。罗斯支持言论自由，并在加沙战争抗议中与学生发生冲突。他批评其他高校领导采用1967年芝加哥大学的《卡尔文报告》中的中立原则，认为这不过是避免麻烦的借口。面对特朗普政府对学术界的攻击，罗斯持续发声，敦促同行捍卫原则。在与作者的对话中，罗斯表示现实比他预期的更糟糕，许多高校不愿公开支持非党派活动，显示出对参与公共事务的犹豫。

• [Animats] 指出，文章讨论的是20世纪70年代的无线电控制玩具伺服，这些设备没有反馈输出，属于低端机械设备，至今仍主导低端市场，因此文章可能重点不在高级技术细节。

• [Animats] 对低端伺服电机缺乏反馈机制的历史背景进行了补充，指出这些设备仍然在低端市场占主导地位。

• [brcmthrowaway] 遇到了伺服电机噪音问题，寻求更高质量的替代方案。

• 文章的技术深度是否足够解释伺服电机的工作原理（[viraptor] 与 [Animats] 之间的不同看法）。

data.title: Declarative Web Push
data.author: janandonly
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了**Declarative Web Push**及其在WebKit中的实现，旨在提高能效和隐私保护。与传统Web Push依赖服务工作线程（service worker）处理推送通知不同，Declarative Web Push允许开发者在不使用服务工作线程的情况下显示通知，从而减少电池消耗和隐私风险。它通过直接描述用户可见的通知内容，避免了因服务工作线程故障而无法显示通知的问题。此外，WebKit强制要求推送订阅时设置`userVisibleOnly`标志，确保所有推送都会显示通知，防止网站偷偷进行后台操作。文章还讨论了隐私保护的重要性，尤其是通过Intelligent Tracking Prevention（ITP）等机制保护用户数据隐私。Declarative Web Push更易用、更高效，并兼容现有Web Push系统。

主要讨论点：浏览器推送通知（Web Push Notifications）的技术实现、用户体验、隐私保护及其与原生应用的比较

不同观点：
• fidotron和alana314指出当前浏览器推送通知在不同平台（Android和iOS）上的实现存在问题，尤其在延迟、通知管理和用户体验方面。alana314认为推送通知没有实际用途，并且用户经常被请求权限的提示轰炸，因此选择关闭通知功能。
• hackernudes和alabastervlog则关注技术细节，特别是iOS中“Declarative Web Push” API的实现方式，以及其与原生应用推送通知服务（APNs）的关系。他们好奇iOS如何处理来自网站的推送，以及新的API是否简化了开发流程。
• mirkodrummer和joekrill对浏览器推送通知和原生应用之间的不公平待遇提出质疑。他们认为，尽管浏览器推送通知被限制以保护隐私和电池寿命，但原生应用却没有类似的限制，质疑这是否是故意让原生应用更具优势。
• notepad0x90强调了推送通知技术被滥用的风险，尤其是恶意网站利用通知进行垃圾信息推送。他们建议加强浏览器和操作系统对推送通知的审核机制，如引入EV TLS证书或信任评估机制，以减少滥用。
• ftbsqcfjm和EGreg对新的“Declarative Web Push” API持乐观态度，认为这是一种简化开发流程的进步，但同时担心其可能带来的性能影响和灵活性降低问题。EGreg还希望未来不再需要用户手动将网页添加到主屏幕以接收推送通知。

补充讨论：
• mary-ext提到对ITP（智能跟踪预防）机制的影响的关注，质疑新提案是否会豁免自动清理机制，并对ITP的正当性提出质疑。
• butz关注浏览器的“Alarms API”实现，表示期待利用该API开发提醒类应用。
• therein分享了对WebKit命名方式的个人理解，指出其与其他Apple框架（如AppKit、UIKit）的相似性。
• andrewmcwatters批评苹果允许企业将广告推送到用户锁屏界面的做法，认为这降低了用户体验。

争议焦点：
• 浏览器推送通知的限制是否真的出于保护隐私和电池寿命，还是为了打压网页应用以维护原生应用的市场优势。
• 新的API是否能真正解决现有问题，并平衡开发者需求与用户体验。

43533994.article_content:
Meet Declarative Web Push
Mar 27, 2025
by
Brady Eidson
Contents
The status quo
How to use Declarative Web Push
A note on backwards compatibility
What if I can’t send the notification description through the internet?
Standards work
Web Push notifications are a powerful and important part of the web platform.
As someone’s very famous uncle once said,
with great power comes great responsibility
. When we added Web Push to WebKit we knew it was imperative to maintain people’s expectations of power efficiency and privacy.
We took a deliberate approach to maintain those expectations when implementing
Web Push for Safari
on macOS, for
web apps saved to the Home Screen
on iOS and iPadOS, and
web apps on Mac
.  We knew running extra code to display notifications could impact battery life. We knew that Web Push’s reliance on service worker JavaScript was at odds with our broad approach to user privacy on the web. We learned that the protections we felt necessary for user privacy challenged assumptions web developers had about Web Push in other browsers. So we challenged ourselves to
propose something better
for end users, web developers, and browsers.
Declarative Web Push allows web developers to request a Web Push subscription and display user visible notifications without requiring an installed
service worker
. Service worker JavaScript can
optionally
change the contents of an incoming notification. Unlike with original Web Push, there is no penalty for service workers failing to display a notification; the declarative push message itself is used as a fallback in case the optional JavaScript processing step fails.
Declarative Web Push is more energy efficient and more private by design. It is easier for you, the web developer to use. And it’s backwards compatible with existing Web Push notifications.
Keep reading for our thinking on the challenges that result from how Web Push works today. Or jump straight to
how to use Declarative Web Push
. You can test it out in iOS and iPadOS 18.4.
The status quo
Existing Web Push notifications were designed with a JavaScript-first mindset. Instead of a remote push directly describing a user visible notification, the more abstract concept of a “push message” is handled by the website’s service worker JavaScript.
The website first needs to have a service worker registered. It can then use that
ServiceWorkerRegistration
to create a
PushSubscription
, which gives the website the information it needs to remotely send a push message to the browser.
To give users direct control, WebKit requires you as the developer to always show a notification; no silent push messages are allowed. Therefore we require push subscriptions to set the
userVisibleOnly
flag to
true
. While this can be frustrating, the original Web Push design made this necessary to protect user privacy and battery life.
Once a push message is received on the device, the browser makes sure there is an instance of the service worker JavaScript and then dispatches a
PushEvent
to it. The code handling that event inspects the data in the push message, using it to make a call to
ServiceWorkerRegistration.showNotification(...)
to display the user visible notification.
While some popular JavaScript libraries abstract away some of these complexities, there’s a lot of code involved, and a lot can subtly go wrong.
Challenge 1 — Silent push protection
Recall that WebKit requires the
userVisibleOnly
flag be set to true when registering for a push subscription. The JavaScript in a ServiceWorker’s
PushEvent
handler has the responsibility of showing that user visible notification. Allowing websites to remotely wake up a device for silent background work is a privacy violation and expends energy. So if an event handler doesn’t show the user visible notification for any reason we
revoke its push subscription
Unfortunately bugs in a service worker script, networking conditions, or local device conditions all might prevent a timely call to
showNotification
. These scenarios might not always be the fault of the script author and can be difficult to debug. It would be better if there were technical enforcement of the
userVisibleOnly
promise and therefore the silent push penalty box could be ignored.
Challenge 2 — Tracking data
We’ve
blogged about it before
and we’ll blog about it again; Privacy is a fundamental human right.
Since the first version of Safari we’ve focused on privacy. WebKit goes above and beyond the privacy protections required by web standards. As the web platform evolved, so did our strategies to protect user privacy. This now includes active blocking and removal of website data, like with
Intelligent Tracking Prevention
(shortened as ITP).
ITP deletes all website data for websites you haven’t visited in a while. This includes service worker registrations. While this can be frustrating to web developers, it’s key to protecting user privacy. It’s a hard tradeoff we make intentionally given how committed we are to protecting u

data.title: Measuring Acceleration Structures
data.author: luu
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了硬件加速光线追踪中的加速结构（acceleration structure）及其内存消耗问题。具体来说，文章比较了不同厂商的GPU在处理相同场景（Amazon Lumberyard Bistro）时，加速结构的内存使用情况，重点分析了AMD、NVIDIA和Intel的显卡差异。实验结果显示，NVIDIA显卡在加速结构上的内存消耗明显低于AMD，甚至最新AMD显卡的内存使用量仍是NVIDIA老款显卡的2.5倍。此外，驱动程序对内存消耗也有显著影响，例如AMD的开源驱动程序radv导致更高的内存使用。文章最后尝试建立模型，帮助理解这些数据，并探讨了不同厂商和驱动对加速结构的影响。

Measuring acceleration structures
31 Mar 2025
Hardware accelerated raytracing, as supported by DirectX 12 and Vulkan, relies on an abstract data structure that stores scene geometry, known as “acceleration structure” and often referred to as “BVH” or “BLAS”. Unlike geometry representation for rasterization, rendering engines can not customize the data layout; unlike texture formats, the layout is not standardized across vendors.
It may seem like a trivial matter - surely, by 2025 all implementations are close to each other in memory consumption, and the main competition is over ray traversal performance and new ray tracing features? Let’s find out.
Experimental setup
It’s going to be difficult to make any generalized claims here; and testing this requires using many different GPUs by many different vendors, which is time consuming. So for the purpose of this post, we will just look at a single scene -
Amazon Lumberyard Bistro
, or more specifically a somewhat customized variant by Nvidia which uses more instancing than the default FBX download.
The results are captured by running
niagara
renderer; if you’d like to follow along, you will need Vulkan 1.4 SDK and drivers, and something along these lines:
git clone https://github.com/zeux/niagara --recursive
cd niagara
git clone https://github.com/zeux/niagara_bistro bistro
cmake . && make
./niagara bistro/bistro.gltf
The
code
will parse the glTF scene, convert the meshes to use fp16 positions, build a BLAS for every mesh
1
, compact it using the relevant parts of
VK_KHR_acceleration_structure
extension, and print the resulting compacted sizes. While a number of levels of detail are built as the scene is loaded, only the original geometry makes it into acceleration structures, for a total of 1.754M triangles
2
.
The builds are using
PREFER_FAST_TRACE
build mode; on some drivers, using
LOW_MEMORY
flag allows to reduce the BLAS size further at some cost to traversal performance, which we will ignore for now.
Experimental results
Running this on the latest (as of end of March) drivers of all respective vendors, on a host of different GPUs, we get the following results; the total BLAS size is presented alongside approximate “bytes/triangle” number - which is not really correct to compute but we will do this anyway.

Now, that’s quite a gap! The delta between earlier AMD GPUs and the latest NVIDIA GPUs is 3x; comparing the latest AMD and NVIDIA GPUs, we still see a 2.5x disparity in memory consumption. Intel
3
is a little ahead of RDNA4, at 2.4x larger BLAS vs NVIDIA.
Now, this table presents each BLAS memory consumption as a function of the GPU - it’s clear that there’s some effect of the GPU generation on the memory consumption. However, another important contributing factor is the software, or more specifically the driver. For AMD, we can compare the results of the various driver releases during the last year, as well as an alternative driver,
radv
4
, on the same GPU - Radeon 7900 GRE:

As we can see, over the last 9 months, BLAS memory consumption on the same AMD GPU and the same driver codebase has progressively improved by 1.5x
5
, whereas if you use radv, your BLAS consumption is now 2.4x larger than official AMD drivers, not to mention the latest NVidia GPU
6
.
Well… that’s certainly a lot of different numbers. Let’s try to make sense of at least some of them.
Mental model
Let’s try to build some models to help us understand what we should expect. Is 100 MB good for 1.754M triangles? Is 241 MB bad? It’s time to talk about what a BVH actually is.
First, let’s contextualize this with how much data we are feeding in. The way Vulkan / DX12 APIs work is that the application provides the driver with geometry description, which is either a flat list of triangles, or a vertex-index buffer pair. Unlike rasterization where a vertex may carry various attributes packed in the way the application wants, for raytracing you only specify a position per vertex, and the formats are more strictly specified

data.title: The Life of a Dairy Cow
data.author: Luc
data.article_summary: 《Future Perfect》栏目中的文章《奶牛的一生》由Marina Bolotnikova撰写，插图由Cat Willett创作，深入探讨了美国940万头奶牛的生活。文章揭示了牛奶生产背后的真相，从奶牛出生到死亡的经历，特别关注工厂化养殖中的动物福利问题。作者指出，了解这些真相后，人们再也无法以同样的眼光看待牛奶。文章还引用了多项研究和报道，如《牛奶的神话》和《新生的奶牛犊 endure 漫长而艰苦的旅程》等，以支持其观点。通过这篇文章，作者呼吁读者关注并思考奶牛在现代农业中的命运。加入Vox会员，可以支持此类深入报道，推动有意义的变革。

• [whycome] 认为现代奶牛被培育成每天生产近8加仑的牛奶，相当于人类每天跑一到两场马拉松，质疑这种生产方式的合理性和可持续性，尤其是从卡路里消耗的角度提出疑问。

补充讨论：
• [yesfitz] 强调了替代品的便捷性和创新性，尤其是通过提供具体例子（Bored Cow）来展示现代科技在解决伦理问题上的潜力。
• 争议的焦点在于现代奶牛产业的可持续性和伦理问题，以及消费者在选择乳制品时的责任和替代品的实际效果。

The life of a dairy cow
The surprising truth about milk is hiding in plain sight.
by
Marina Bolotnikova
Illustrations by Cat Willett
Apr 3, 2025, 10:00 AM UTC
Facebook
Link
Cat Willett for Vox
Marina Bolotnikova
is a deputy editor for Vox’s Future Perfect section. Before joining Vox, she reported on factory farming for national outlets including the Guardian, the Intercept, and elsewhere.
At Vox, I specialize in writing and editing all sorts of stories about animal agriculture and the future of food, from the
strange ritual of eating turkeys on Thanksgiving
to the policy debates around the fate of
mother pigs in the pork industry
. But the lives of America’s 9.4 million dairy cows have always been especially close to my heart, and to many people who care about farm animals, for reasons that will become clear as you read this comic. I’d
written
a bit about dairy cows before, but to truly do the story justice, I knew I needed to narrate and illustrate, in depth, a dairy cow’s life from birth to death (and even then, there was so much from my research that had to be left on the cutting-room floor). Once you really see it, it’s impossible to look at milk the same way again.

data.title: The Slow Collapse of Critical Thinking in OSINT Due to AI
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了开源情报（OSINT）领域中由于生成式人工智能（GenAI）工具的广泛使用，分析师的批判性思维能力逐渐减弱的问题。作者Nico Dekens指出，过去OSINT强调思维分析，但现在越来越多的人依赖AI完成任务，如总结文档、翻译文本、生成报告等，导致分析师的批判性思考和验证工作减少。研究表明，对AI的信任增加会降低用户的批判性思维，使他们更少质疑和验证信息。文章警告，过度依赖AI可能使OSINT从业者失去判断力与专业 integrity，从调查者变为自动化操作者。文章呼吁业内人士重拾批判性思维，避免在AI辅助下失去思考能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（AI）工具（如生成型AI）在工作流程中的影响，尤其是对批判性思维和信息验证的影响。

不同观点：
• **BrenBarn**：认为文章虽然声称不是对AI的抱怨，但实际上提出了严重的警示。他将AI的使用比作毒品成瘾，指出免费向所有人分发AI工具可能带来风险，因为这种方式容易导致人们依赖AI而不再自主思考。
• **Aurornis**：反驳关于AI让人变得懒惰的观点，认为那些依赖AI的人之前也依赖其他媒体（如播客、新闻、社交媒体），AI只是提供了更便捷的意见来源。AI用户和沉迷于TikTok视频以获取知识的人没有本质区别。
• **0hijinks**：质疑AI在研究和发现任务中的有效性，指出如果用户必须对AI的答案进行详细验证，那还不如自己从头做起。他怀疑使用AI是否真的能提高效率。
• **jruohonen**：同意文章的观点，指出人们在使用AI时确实减少了批判性思考，例如不再形成假设、验证来源和评估多个视角，这种情况已经在实际工作流程中出现。
• **sepositus**：质疑专业人士因为AI的快速、自信和清晰的回答而停止批判性思考的说法，认为如果专业人士没有研究AI的局限性，那就是懒惰。
• **treyfitty**：支持AI工具的实用性，例如在查询基本信息时，AI可以快速提供答案，减少不必要的努力。
• **tqi**：对文章中关于AI导致批判性思维崩溃的预测表示怀疑，认为这可能是作者的确认偏误，而不是理性分析的结果。
• **roenxi**：文章没有讨论AI对分析质量的影响，指出AI虽然不像类型检查器那样绝对正确，但在某些方面可能比人类平均水平要好。他认为AI的影响不一定是负面的。

补充讨论：
• **palmotea**：指出AI的广泛适用性，认为文章讨论的问题不仅限于开放源情报（OSINT）领域，而是在所有采用AI工具的领域都存在。
• **pcj-github**：分享了个人经验，指出AI在学习新技能时虽然能降低入门门槛，但可能延缓深入掌握技能的过程，因为用户容易依赖AI进行思考。
• **BariumBlue**：提到AI的自信语气容易让人误以为其答案准确，这是用户需要注意的问题。
• **zora_goron**：提出“人类->AI推理转移”的概念，指出AI工具在帮助完成非推理任务时也可能悄然影响人类的推理过程，因为AI决定了哪些信息重要。
• **Barrin92**：质疑专业分析师的专业性，认为如果连基本的分析能力（如区分巴黎和比利时）都需要AI帮助，那是令人担忧的。他批评文章没有深入探讨信息验证和批判性思考的基本要求。

争议焦点：
• AI工具是否导致用户减少批判性思考和自主验证。
• AI工具在工作流程中的实际效率和影响，尤其是对分析质量的影响是正面还是负面。
• 用户依赖AI是否因为工具的便捷性或自身的懒惰。

总结：评论中对AI工具的影响存在分歧，一些人认为AI导致用户减少批判性思考和自主验证，另一些人则认为AI只是提供了便捷的意见来源，用户的责任更大。此外，AI对分析质量的实际影响也存在争议。

The Slow Collapse of Critical Thinking in OSINT due to AI
Nico Dekens | dutch_osintguy
19 hours ago
9 min read
OSINT used to be a thinking game. Now it’s becoming a trusting game and that should terrify you.
I’ve seen it firsthand, analysts running solid investigations, then slowly shifting more and more of the thinking to GenAI tools. At first, it’s small. You use ChatGPT to summarise a document or translate a foreign post. Then it’s helping draft your reports. Then it’s generating leads. And eventually, you’re not thinking as critically as you used to. You’re verifying less, questioning less, relying more.
We tell ourselves we’re “working smarter.” But somewhere along the way, we stop noticing how much of the actual thinking is being offloaded.
This isn’t a rant against AI. I use it daily, ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, Gemini. They’re in my workflow like everyone else’s. But the tradecraft is slipping. Analysts are skipping the hard parts. They’re trusting GenAI to do the heavy cognitive lifting, and it’s changing how we operate at a foundational level.
When OSINT becomes too easy, too efficient, too comfortable… you should be worried. Tradecraft isn’t just about speed, it’s about judgment. And judgment doesn’t come from a language model. If we keep going down this path without pushing back, without actively preserving the critical habits that define our profession, we risk becoming operators of automation instead of investigators.
This blog is a wake-up call. For myself. For anyone working in OSINT. For the people teaching it, and the people just getting started. If we don’t reclaim the thinking side of this game, we’ll lose the game entirely.
The Study That Should Alarm You
In early 2025, a team from Carnegie Mellon and Microsoft Research published something every OSINT analyst should read, but most haven’t. It was a large-scale survey of 319 knowledge workers using GenAI tools like ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, and Gemini in their daily work.
What they found is a warning shot.
The study revealed a clear pattern: the more confidence users had in the AI, the less they thought critically. In contrast, the more confident they were in themselves, the more likely they were to question the output, verify the information, and think deeply about the task.
Let that sink in: Confidence in AI replaces confidence in self and with it, the thinking disappears.
Here’s the punchline:
High trust in GenAI consistently led to reduced critical thinking and less cognitive effort across the board.
Participants weren’t lazy. They were experienced professionals. But when the tool responded quickly, confidently, and clearly they stopped doing the hard part. They stopped questioning. Stopped verifying. Stopped applying the mental friction that separates automation from investigation.
The scary part is that many users still believed they were thinking critically, because GenAI made them feel smart.
The researchers saw a new type of behavior emerge:
•  Instead of forming hypotheses, users asked the AI for ideas.
•  Instead of validating sources, they assumed the AI had already done so.
•  Instead of assessing multiple perspectives, they integrated and edited the AI’s summary and moved on.
This isn’t hypothetical. This is happening now, in real-world workflows. And if you’re in OSINT, you know how dangerous that is.
In our line of work, you can’t afford false confidence. You can’t afford a hallucinated source, a mistranslated post, or a manipulated summary. But the more trust you place in GenAI, without friction, without skepticism, the more you risk exactly that.
The study didn’t focus on OSINT directly. But it doesn’t have to. The findings hit home harder here than anywhere else. Because if we lose critical thinking in this field, we don’t just lose accuracy, we lose integrity.
What This Means for OSINT
In OSINT, we deal in fragments. Nothing is handed to us neatly. We build context from chaos:   tweets, photos, forums, leaks, metadata, satellite images, dead links, weird file names. Every good analyst knows that the work isn’t just collecting data. It’s thinking with it.
That’s what’s at risk.
The
Lee et al. study
wasn’t about OSINT specifically, but it described exactly what’s happening in OSINT shops, government teams, threat intel units, and open-source communities around the world. The creeping shift from thinking to prompting, from analyst to editor. Let’s talk real.

You upload a protest photo into a tool like Gemini and ask, “Where was this taken?” It spits out a convincing response: “Paris, near Place de la République.” It sounds right. You move on.
But a trained eye would notice the signage is Belgian. The license plates are off. The architecture doesn’t match. You trusted the AI and missed the location by a country.

You use Claude to summarize a person’s online presence. It generates a clean narr

data.title: Bonobos' calls may be the closest thing to animal language we've seen
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 瑞士苏黎世大学的进化人类学家Melissa Berthet及其团队研究发现，倭黑猩猩能够将基本的叫声（如咕哝、吱吱叫、尖叫、咕咕声和口哨声）组合成具有更复杂意义的结构，这种能力被称为非平凡组合性，以往被认为仅人类独有。研究人员建立了包含700个倭黑猩猩叫声的数据库，并使用分布语义学方法解码这些叫声。通过分析叫声的上下文，他们发现不同叫声组合传达了特定信息，如“一起做我在做的事”或“让我们呆在一起”，甚至用于协调行动或表达情感。虽然研究揭示了倭黑猩猩复杂的交流方式，但仍可能存在更细微的声学差异有待探索。这项研究为我们理解倭黑猩猩的交流提供了新的视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：复杂发声交流的概述及相关研究，包括动物智能、种群分布及研究方法的讨论。

不同观点：
• robwwilliams 认为文章对复杂发声交流做了很好的概述，并提到Farley Mowat在《Never Cry Wolf》一书中对狼的类似研究，同时推测鲸类动物可能也有类似情况。
• ViktorRay 对Bonobos（倭黑猩猩）表现出兴趣，并推荐了一本书《Our Inner Ape》，认为该书对理解人类与倭黑猩猩的联系非常有帮助。
• thebeardisred 提出问题，询问是否有研究尝试对这种类型的交流进行"tokenization"（标记化）的处理。
• readthenotes1 对文章的准确性提出质疑，指出文章第一句有错误，将倭黑猩猩的栖息地误写为刚果共和国，而根据维基百科，它们实际生活在刚果民主共和国。

补充讨论：
• 讨论涉及了对动物交流和智能的广泛兴趣，包括狼和倭黑猩猩等不同物种。
• readthenotes1 对内容的准确性提出批评，强调了核实信息的重要性，并引用了维基百科作为参考。
• thebeardisred 的问题引发了对研究方法的关注，尤其是如何对复杂的发声交流进行结构化分析。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在内容的准确性上，特别是对倭黑猩猩栖息地的描述错误，这可能影响对文章整体可信度的评价。
• 另一个潜在的讨论点是研究方法的有效性，特别是如何对动物的发声交流进行科学的标记化和分析。

Bonobos, great apes related to us and chimpanzees that live in the Republic of Congo, communicate with vocal calls including peeps, hoots, yelps, grunts, and whistles. Now, a team of Swiss scientists led by Melissa Berthet, an evolutionary anthropologist at the University of Zurich, discovered bonobos can combine these basic sounds into larger semantic structures. In these communications, meaning is something more than just a sum of individual calls—a trait known as non-trivial compositionality, which we once thought was uniquely human.
To do this, Berthet and her colleagues built a database of 700 bonobo calls and deciphered them using methods drawn from distributional semantics, the methodology we’ve relied on in reconstructing long-lost languages like Etruscan or Rongorongo. For the first time, we have a glimpse into what bonobos mean when they call to each other in the wild.
Context is everything
The key idea behind distributional semantics is that when words appear in similar contexts, they tend to have similar meanings. To decipher an unknown language, you need to collect a large corpus of words and turn those words into vectors—mathematical representations that let you place them in a multidimensional semantic space. The second thing you need is context data, which tells you the circumstances in which these words were used (that gets vectorized, too). When you map your word vectors onto context vectors in this multidimensional space, what usually happens is that words with similar meaning end up close to each other. Berthet and her colleagues wanted to apply the same trick to bonobos’ calls. That seemed straightforward at first glance, but proved painfully hard to execute.
“We worked at a camp in the forest, got up super early at 3:30 in the morning, walked one or two hours to get to the bonobos’ nest. At [the] time they would wake up, I would switch my microphone on for the whole day to collect as many vocalizations as I could,” Berthet says. Each recorded call then had to be annotated with a horribly long list of contextual parameters. Berthet had a questionnaire filled with queries like: is there a neighboring group around; are there predators around; is the caller feeding, resting, or grooming; is another individual approaching the caller, etc. There were 300 questions that had to be answered for each of the 700 recorded calls.
But when all this data was finally vectorized and the team started working their distributional semantics magic, gathering it proved worth the effort.
Bonobo dictionary
Berthet started with establishing the tentative meaning of the basic calls: singular grunts or yelps. Grunts appeared in many different contexts, including grooming, feeding, or moving, and the team interpreted them as intended to get another’s attention, a bit like saying “look at me.” Yelps meant “let’s do this” as an imperative, while peeps had a very similar meaning, but were more of a suggestion—think “I would like to…” Bonobos also used peeps or yelps when they wanted others to join them. Low hoots were translated as “I am excited,” while high hoots signaled the presence and location of the caller in dangerous situations. Whistles meant “let’s stay together.”
Once the basic calls were sorted, Berthet started looking at their different combinations. Bonobos combined yelps and grunts into a trivial compositional structure meaning “let’s do what I do.” This was mostly used when the group was building night nests—platforms made high in the trees out of broken branches, sometimes lined with leaves.
However, the team also found examples of non-trivial compositionality, the first such discovery outside of humans.
The first non-trivial combination was high hoot-low hoot that was translated as a distress call. But it was also used to stop other individuals’ display behaviors—dramatic, exaggerated actions or gestures bonobos perform to assert dominance or attract attention. The second was either peep or yelp in the “join” meaning paired with high hoot to form a structure used for coordinating with others before traveling. Finally, the “I would like to” peep followed by “let’s stay together” whistle was used for initiating more romantically inclined interactions bonobos are famous for indulging in.
Berthet said her team managed to record a few more calls but could not use them in her study because they were too rare to gather meaningful context data. Still, she expects we have much more to learn about bonobos’ communication.
Gestures and sounds

data.author: jihadjihad
data.article_summary: 设计师Dori the Giant受到Twitter标志由13个完美圆形构成的启发，进行了一项设计挑战：用13个圆形创作出13种动物。这些简约而美观的作品展示在她的个人作品集中，并受到许多人的赞赏和询问，部分作品可出售印刷品。她还提到使用Adobe Illustrator和形状生成工具来完成这些设计，并分享了一个教程链接。许多网友表示希望获得高清壁纸或购买这些作品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用圆形进行创作的艺术性和技术性

不同观点：
• [DrNosferatu] 提到使用参数拟合复杂形状（如大象）的著名说法，暗示仅用少量参数可以创建复杂图形，质疑单纯使用圆形创作的必要性。引用了冯·诺依曼的“大象与参数”例子。
• [ezekg] 认为仅用圆形创作标志具有挑战性且令人满足，并分享了自己作为设计师时创作的几个例子，展示了一些完全由圆形构成的设计作品。
• [rob74] 对比了Twitter旧logo（由13个完美圆形构成）与新logo，指出新logo似乎完全没有使用圆形元素，并提到新logo类似于数学符号“双击资本X”。
• [sverhagen] 认为这种设计风格类似于Ubuntu背景，暗示这种设计可能过于简单或重复。
• [nonethewiser] 对如何实际操作这种设计感到好奇，质疑是否先创建图形再调整为圆形，或者直接从圆形开始设计。
• [iamwil] 提到曾看到过关于Twitter鸟logo也是由圆形构成的讨论，并分享了相关的Reddit帖子。
• [apankrat] 分享了自己15年前用类似方法创作的个人标志，展示了自己的创作经验。
• [thesz] 认为这种使用圆形并结合并集、交集或差集的操作是低复杂度艺术的例子，并提到了低复杂度音乐（bytebeat）的相关性。
• [abeppu] 提到Schmidhuber在1990年代中期的相关工作，提供了进一步的学术参考。
• [enqk] 提到日本家徽（Mon）几乎完全由圆形和线条构成，常常描绘蔬菜或动物，展示了这种设计风格的文化背景。

• [vismit2000] 提到3b1b视频中关于傅里叶级数的“用圆形绘图”内容，暗示一切都可以用圆形构成。
• [saunved_42] 对这种设计风格表示喜爱，并设想了一个使用这些角色制作短片的实验。

• 讨论中涉及了圆形创作的实际操作性、文化背景、艺术性和技术性限制等方面。
• 争议的焦点在于单纯使用圆形创作是否必要以及这种设计风格的艺术价值。
• 提供了多个实际例子和参考链接，展示了不同创作者使用圆形进行设计的经验和成果。

data.title: Declarative Schemas for simpler database management
data.author: kiwicopple
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了声明式 schema 如何简化复杂数据库的管理。声明式 schema 将数据库的最终期望状态存储在 `.sql` 文件中，便于集中管理和版本控制。相比直接修改数据库 schema，声明式 schema 具有以下优势：单一管理界面，减少冗余和错误；版本化迁移，确保不同环境中的一致性；简明的代码审查，无需重复复杂迁移脚本。

随着数据库 schema 复杂性增加，传统迁移方法难以维护，因为缺乏单一的整体视图。例如，在 Supabase 中，复杂的 `projects` 表涉及私有表、RLS（行级安全）、视图和触发器，修改时需多步操作，容易导致冲突。

声明式 schema 通过集中管理 schema，简化了开发流程，提高了开发效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据库迁移和声明式 schema 管理的优缺点

不同观点：
• [支持声明式 schema，但反对自动生成迁移]：xyzzy_plugh 认为声明式 schema 是有必要的，但不应自动生成迁移，因为这可能带来问题。他建议手动编写迁移并测试，以确保 schema 变更符合预期。
• [有限支持声明式 API]：webster451 认为声明式 API 在某些场景下非常强大，但并不适用于所有情况。他认为程序员对变更的控制能带来更好的结果，并指出 Kubernetes 等工具虽然提供声明式基础设施，但实现非常复杂且容易出错。
• [支持自动生成迁移]：bartvk 总结了一种新方法，即通过修改 CREATE TABLE 语句并自动生成差异迁移。他认为这种方法简化了数据库变更的管理。
• [Rails 的做法更好]：neutralino1 认为 Rails 已经实现了更好的方案，通过保持迁移和 schema.sql 文件的同步，方便测试和数据库重建。
• [需要 IDE 支持的声明式管理]：Guillaume86 希望有一个类似微软 SSDT 的工具，用于 Postgres，提供声明式 schema 管理、错误检查和更好的开发体验。
• [自动生成迁移可能导致问题]：joshAg 认为自动生成迁移可能导致一些复杂的变更（如 enum 变更、数据迁移）难以处理，建议手动编写迁移以确保灵活性。
• [关注手动编辑自动生成迁移的能力]：ucarion 关心是否可以手动编辑自动生成的迁移，以实现更复杂的操作，如并发创建索引。
• [结合 IDE 工具提升开发体验]：kiwicopple 提到结合 Postgres Language Server，可以在 IDE 中直接执行 SQL 语句，提高开发效率。
• [自动生成迁移的风险]：geocar 警告自动生成迁移可能在团队中引入严重错误，导致长期问题。
• [其他工具]：xaas 提到使用 ZenStack 并指出其未来版本将不再依赖 Supabase。
• [质疑新方法的价值]：mylons 质疑新方法相比原始 SQL 的优势，认为差别不大。
• [提供相关参考资料]：wmanley 提供了关于 SQLite 声明式迁移的文章链接，并披露自己是该文章的合著者。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于自动生成迁移的可靠性和灵活性，以及声明式 schema 管理的优缺点。
• 不同开发者对声明式和命令式方法的偏好，以及对工具支持和开发体验的需求各不相同。
• 实际应用中，如何平衡自动化和手动控制的比例，以及如何确保数据库迁移的安全性和可维护性，是重要的讨论点。

Declarative Schemas for Simpler Database Management
03 Apr 2025
•
7 minute read
Qiao Han
Engineering
Today we’re releasing declarative schemas to simplify managing and maintaining complex database schemas. With declarative schemas, you can define your database structure in a clear, centralized, and version-controlled manner.
What are declarative schemas?
#
Declarative schemas store the final desired state of the database in
.sql
files that can be saved and versioned alongside a project. For example, here is the declarative schema for a classic
products
table:
_
10
create table "products" (
_
10
"id" serial primary key,
_
10
"name" text not null,
_
10
"description" text,
_
10
"price" numeric(10,2) not null,
_
10
"created_at" timestamp default now()
_
10
);
_
10
_
10
alter table "products"
_
10
enable row level security;
Declarative schemas offer numerous benefits over making changes to your database schema directly:
Single pane of glass
. Maintain your entire database schema in one place, reducing redundancy and potential errors.
Versioned migrations
. Automatically generate migration files, ensuring consistent schema updated across environments. Store your declarative schema files alongside your project files in your version control system.
Concise code reviews
. Easily review changes to tables, views, and functions without manually repeating complex migration scripts.
Declarative schemas vs migrations
#
It's best practice to use
Migrations
to track and apply changes to databases. Every time you make a change, you create a new new file with all the changes, keeping changes versioned and reproducible.
However, as the complexity of a database schemas grows, it becomes increasingly difficult to develop using versioned migrations as there isn't a single place to see the entire database schema.
For example, at Supabase we have a complex and frequently-updated
projects
table. Here's partially what it looks like with RLS enabled:
_
32

_
32
id              bigint    not null,
_
32
name            text      not null,
_
32

_
32

32

32
);

_

enable row level security;
_
32

32
on private.projects
_
32
for insert
_

to authenticated

32
with check auth.can_write(project_id);
_
32

_
32
on private.projects
_
32

_

43572544.article_summary:
本文介绍了声明式 schema 如何简化复杂数据库的管理。声明式 schema 将数据库的最终期望状态存储在 `.sql` 文件中，便于集中管理和版本控制。相比直接修改数据库 schema，声明式 schema 具有以下优势：单一管理界面，减少冗余和错误；版本化迁移，确保不同环境中的一致性；简明的代码审查，无需重复复杂迁移脚本。

随着数据库 schema 复杂性增加，传统迁移方法难以维护，因为缺乏单一的整体视图。例如，在 Supabase 中，复杂的 `projects` 表涉及私有表、RLS（行级安全）、视图和触发器，修改时需多步操作，容易导致冲突。

声明式 schema 通过集中管理 schema，简化了开发流程，提高了开发效率。

主要讨论点：数据库迁移和声明式 schema 管理的优缺点

不同观点：
• [支持声明式 schema，但反对自动生成迁移]：xyzzy_plugh 认为声明式 schema 是有必要的，但不应自动生成迁移，因为这可能带来问题。他建议手动编写迁移并测试，以确保 schema 变更符合预期。
• [有限支持声明式 API]：webster451 认为声明式 API 在某些场景下非常强大，但并不适用于所有情况。他认为程序员对变更的控制能带来更好的结果，并指出 Kubernetes 等工具虽然提供声明式基础设施，但实现非常复杂且容易出错。
• [支持自动生成迁移]：bartvk 总结了一种新方法，即通过修改 CREATE TABLE 语句并自动生成差异迁移。他认为这种方法简化了数据库变更的管理。
• [Rails 的做法更好]：neutralino1 认为 Rails 已经实现了更好的方案，通过保持迁移和 schema.sql 文件的同步，方便测试和数据库重建。

• [自动生成迁移可能导致问题]：joshAg 认为自动生成迁移可能导致一些复杂的变更（如 enum 变更、数据迁移）难以处理，建议手动编写迁移以确保灵活性。
• [关注手动编辑自动生成迁移的能力]：ucarion 关心是否可以手动编辑自动生成的迁移，以实现更复杂的操作，如并发创建索引。
• [结合 IDE 工具提升开发体验]：kiwicopple 提到结合 Postgres Language Server，可以在 IDE 中直接执行 SQL 语句，提高开发效率。
• [自动生成迁移的风险]：geocar 警告自动生成迁移可能在团队中引入严重错误，导致长期问题。
• [其他工具]：xaas 提到使用 ZenStack 并指出其未来版本将不再依赖 Supabase。
• [质疑新方法的价值]：mylons 质疑新方法相比原始 SQL 的优势，认为差别不大。
• [提供相关参考资料]：wmanley 提供了关于 SQLite 声明式迁移的文章链接，并披露自己是该文章的合著者。

I Want a Better Mac, so Iâm Cheering for a Better Linux
By
Timothy R. Butler
| Posted at
11:04 PM
My
recent column
on Appleâs declining software quality hit a nerve. So why do any of us put up with software that grows increasingly buggy? One word: hardware.
Telling in many of the comments about my piece was a repeated refrain, âAppleâs software keeps getting worse, but I canât imagine going through the downgrade to other hardware.â Apple knows how to turn out very good quality pieces of hardware and, for many purposes, stands alone.
Thatâs been largely true for the last couple of decades. The half-decade of Apple Silicon has cemented this position. At any price point Apple contends, Macs, iPads and iPhones are either without peers or at the top of the market in build quality and processing power. The Mac mini isnât the cheapest computer, nor is the base iPad the cheapest tablet, but they are the cheapest
good
options and so it goes on up.
Appleâs hardware is not just good; it is designed carefully to work together. While making the case about software bugs, I alluded to various functions that make abandoning ship more than just a downgrade in pure hardware quality. Even with a âgood enoughâ tablet, acceptable earbuds and a decent phone, nothing works together at the same level Apple has achieved.
Do I want to give up using my tablet as an instantaneously available wireless display that automatically shares my laptopâs keyboard and touchpad? Do I want to give up having earbuds that flow between devices without so much as a button press?
Even buggy software gains a sheen in an environment of close integration of excellent devices. Had Steve Jobs embraced Mac clones in the late 1990s, an idea that would have made Apple primarily a software company, the flaws in MacOS and iOS — if they even still existed — would be only more glaring.
Uniquely well crafted and integrated hardware covers a multitude of software sins. We always use hardware and software together, so the sum of the parts is what matters. Even with diminishing quality, MacOS and iOS hold this card over the Windows-Android alternative, hamstrung as it is by a vast array of manufacturersâ varied, often contradictory, and routinely inferior hardware design choices.
Numerous responses to my piece on software hit a similar impulse to my own: if only there were hardware that was as good and worked together as well as Appleâs, jumping ship to Linux would be awfully attractive at this juncture. The mainstream Linux desktop, an ever elusive goal
this publication was founded to advocate for a quarter century ago
, feels so incredibly, tantalizingly close today.
For Apple aficionados troubled by the state of MacOS, the modern GNOME desktop on Linux beckons as a more faithful implementation of the ideals of MacOS than current MacOS does. GNOME is painstakingly consistent across its different apps and exudes the minimalist philosophy with which Appleâs hardware shines. Gone are the rough edges that always hindered the Linux desktop when I used to write about it regularly.
I helped a number of friends and colleagues make the jump to Linux desktops against the currents in the early 2000s when it was still weird. But, none of those Linux âmigrationâ projects, even my own, stuck over the long haul. The intersection where software meets hardware was always the problem. Some part of the computer wouldnât fully work under Linux or some necessary peripheral couldnât talk to it. That was bad in a largely desktop era; itâs a non-starter in the laptop, tablet and phone era.
My first attempt at a non-Windows laptop was a Dell Pentium III laptop retrofit with a then-current variant of Linux. It worked ok, but not great. One upside: anything worked better than the Windows ME it came with. (Credit: Timothy R. Butler)
And this was before something like a tablet seamlessly sharing a mouse and keyboard with a computer was even a dream.
Recent editions of MacOS and iOS may not work as well as we users would like, but thereâs no current combination of computers and accessories that can achieve a complete replacement. Apple reigns here, while Windows at least benefits from broad manufacturer support. Linux still suffers from largely being a platform added onto hardware and made to work with accessories intended for something else.
The Windows-Android complex is largely content with middling software on subpar hardware. Apple offers something better in terms of hardware, but it isnât âhungryâ enough in the post-Jobs era. Tim Cookâs iteration of the company is content to coast with the minimally acceptable software quality it can pass off to sell that hardware.
So long as no one is competing on making better quality software, the present software quality morass will continue.

data.title: Digital Archivists: Protecting Public Data from Erasure
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了哈佛大学法学院的图书馆创新实验室如何利用API技术保存公共信息，避免其消失在"记忆黑洞"中。该项目专注于创建Data.gov网站的存档，该网站包含31.1万个公共数据集。通过这种方法，数字档案管理员确保了重要公共数据的长久保存和可访问性，为未来的研究和分析提供了宝贵的资源。文章强调了技术在保护和维护公共信息方面的重要性，展示了创新技术如何应用于信息保存领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据存档、公开记录以及隐私问题

不同观点：
• dmillar：许多犯罪记录，无论是轻微还是严重的，都是公开记录。即使是被删除或撤销的违规记录，仍可能在背景调查中出现，因为公司会存档公共数据。因此，即使是撤销的记录也有可能被公开。

• badlibrarian：在数据存档领域存在很多恐慌和重叠工作，需要一种协调这些努力的方法。Internet Archive等组织虽然引起了关注并做出了承诺，但最终因无法处理大量数据而让志愿者停止存档工作。同时，也提到了其他团队的努力，如Archive Team和Webrecorder。

• nla：引用BBC档案负责人的观点，强调一旦进行了格式转换，就需要一直进行格式转换。因此，建议尽可能保留原始资料。

• Damogran6：假设政府领导人宣布删除数据，引发 rush 去备份数据，随后政府领导人宣称他们将维护数据的成本转移出了政府，从而实现了更小、更高效的政府。对此表示反感。

• mikrl：讨论了与dox相关的问题，如果个人在公共场所发布了身份识别或 incriminating 信息，第三方存储并可能让他人访问这些信息。如果原始发布者删除了信息但无法彻底清除，这些信息是否仍被视为公开的？它是否曾经真正公开过？

补充讨论：
• Teever：提到之前提交的相关内容被标记，强调讨论这些内容的重要性，希望当前提交的内容不会被标记。

• hsuduebc2：提出区块链技术是否可以在数据存档和隐私问题上提供有效解决方案的疑问。

争议焦点：
• 数据一旦公开或存档后，是否能够以及如何彻底删除或保护隐私。特别是在第三方存档和区块链技术的应用上存在不同看法。

data.title: Bikes in the Age of Tariffs
data.author: bobchadwick
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了关税对自行车行业的影响，特别是对Rene Herse Cycles等公司的冲击。美国对进口产品加征高额关税，旨在促进国内生产，但同时导致进口商品价格上涨。虽然自行车行业长期以来已有不同类别的关税，但新关税按原产国设定，尤其是针对中国，目前中国制造的自行车关税已高达69%。这对高端自行车影响较小，因为其生产已转移出中国，但碳纤维车架和组件可能因模具专用性仍部分依赖中国生产。总体而言，关税将导致自行车价格上升，并对行业造成深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关税政策的影响及相关政治动机

不同观点：
• [mullingitover] 认为，面对加税，最大限度地投入资金以惩罚相关方是财务上负责任的做法。这暗示了通过政治捐赠来对抗税收政策的立场。
• [whynotmaybe] 通过具体计算展示了关税对商品价格的直接影响，例如儿童自行车成本的增加。这说明了关税如何导致商品价格上涨。
• [rstarast] 提出，不同国家之间的关税差异可能会导致进口商品的重新routing和重新label。他们质疑现有控制措施的有效性。

Bikes in the Age of Tariffs
Jan Heine
2025-04-03T10:22:33-07:00
Today’s post was going to be about a new product we’re introducing—but we need to hold off while we recalculate our prices. You’ve probably seen the news: Virtually all imports into the United States will be subjected to additional, steep import taxes, also called tariffs. The goal is to radically re-orient how manufacturing is done, and to make things domestically. Tariffs tend to be reciprocal, so most countries will increase their tariffs on American-made goods, too.
Our rulers seem to think that the U.S. imports more than it exports, so the net effect will be positive. Whether that is true is open to debate. Look at the graphic above, published in the
Wall Street Journal
. What strikes me is how large the volume of imports and exports really is. Sure, there is a trade deficit, but the size of the exports (the green part) is far greater than the deficit. And all that will also be affected by the new tariffs in one way or another.
The bike industry isn’t even an afterthought in these decisions, and yet it’ll be affected deeply by all of them. Let’s look at how the tariffs will reshape our industry and our sport.
What are tariffs?
Tariffs are a tax on imported goods. They are assessed when those goods enter the country, and the importer pays them. Usually, they are added to the freight costs. Shipments are released by customs only after any applicable tariffs (and associated fees) are paid.
Some have suggested that foreign suppliers will pay at least for part of the tariffs by reducing their prices to remain competitive in the U.S. In our experience, that is unlikely. At least in the bike industry, most suppliers are unaware of the tariffs that their good face after leaving the country. They never see them. They calculate their prices based on their cost structure. Even retail giants like Walmart reportedly have been rebuffed when asking suppliers for price breaks to account for part of the tariffs. The simple reality is that in a free market system, only suppliers with lean cost structures survive. There isn’t room for cutting prices by 10, 20, 30% or more.
In summary, tariffs are an added tax on imported goods. Like all sales taxes, it’s regressive, because those with less income spend a larger percentage of their money on buying things.
Existing tariffs
There have been tariffs on bicycles all along. They varied by category, since they were intended to protect domestic producers. Complete bicycles were assessed an 11% tax upon import, but lightweight adult bikes saw only 5.5%. This made sense. Way back, companies like Huffy and Schwinn made the vast majority of kid’s and adult bikes domestically, but high-end bikes were usually imported. The same applied to parts: 11% was the base rate, but parts like freewheel hubs and cotterless aluminum cranks did not have any import duty. Nor did bicycle tires. Because nobody was making these parts in the U.S.
The general idea was to protect certain domestic industries against imports, no matter where they came from. And for things that nobody in the U.S. was making, the idea was to facilitate importing them. As an example, Schwinn made almost everything they needed to build bicycles in their huge Chicago factory (above)—but even they imported derailleurs and other parts for high-end bikes.
A new way to do tariffs
The new tariffs are different: The rates are set not by product category, but by country of origin. Instead of protecting specific domestic industries, the goal appears to be punishing certain countries—and, by extension, American companies that source their products from these countries.
This article is about the impact on the bike industry. How will these country-by-country rates affect the bike world and Rene Herse Cycles in particular?
China — 69%
Tariffs on China have been in the headlines for years. For made-in-China bicycles, a 10% tariff has been in place since the mid-2010s, plus another 25% tariff was enacted in 2018. Yesterday, a 34% tariff was added. If my math is correct, that would put the tariff at a whopping 69%.
However, the impact of the new tariffs on performance bikes will be small. The earlier tariffs added 35% to the price of Chinese bikes and frames. They had the effect of moving most bicycle production out of China, at least for high-end products where manufacturing (and not shipping, warehousing and marketing) makes up most of the costs. One possible exception is the manufacture of carbon frames and components (especially rims), where some companies have significant investments in molds at Chinese factories. Generally, tooling is specific to the machines and techniques of one supplier and cannot be moved from factory to factory, much less from country to country.
Small wheel companies that source their rims in China have put downward pressure on the market for carbon wheels in recent years. (Prices gener

data.title: Rewriting my site in vanilla web
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
作者讲述了重构自己网站的经历，从使用各种库和框架，到自己创建名为 *compose-html* 的静态网站生成器，最终发现复杂度不减反增。于是，作者尝试使用纯 HTML/CSS/JS 重写网站，避免不必要的构建步骤和框架。

作者选择通过 Web Components 实现重复内容（如页眉、页脚）的模块化，利用浏览器对 HTML 标签的宽容性，省略一些常见标签。为了保持代码简洁和可维护性，作者遵循以下原则：
1. **语义化 HTML**：使用有意义的标签而非泛滥的 `div` 和 `span`。
2. **TAC CSS 方法**：使用自定义标签而非类选择器（如 BEM），简化 CSS。
3. **轻量级 Web Components**：避免 Shadow DOM 的复杂性，直接操作 Light DOM。

最终，作者认为这种方法可行，既减少了构建复杂性，又保持了灵活性，适合实际需求。

43574701.article_content:
I rewrote this website in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. Here’s the story. But why? Over the years, I’ve used a bunch of libraries & frameworks to build this website , before finally making my own static site generator that I called compose-html . As the name suggests, it composes HTML files together, very much like Astro . compose-html’s README I like systems that have a small set of tight abstractions that are easy to understand. I’m not a fan of rigid, non-atomic concepts like “pages” and “layouts”, “themes”, “frontmatters”—I mean, these are just ‘components’ and ‘data’! I dislike those that dictate your project directory structure and coding style. If your documentation has a ‘Project structure’ section, I’m out! So I built my own simple site builder and that was nice BUT it didn’t end up making life easier. The real world is messy, and HTML more so. Simply composing pieces of HTML together isn’t that straightforward and the abstraction leaked. My compose-html framework eventually turned into a 2k LoC that was more liability than freedom. Though it served me very well, it was a dead end. Maybe nothing can solve my problem… As in, literally nothing. No framework. No build steps. What if HTML wasn’t a render target, but was both the authoring and publishing medium? What if I rewrote my site in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS? A crazy idea infiltrated my conciousness. Is it feasible? A common reason for adding complexity is to avoid repetitive work like copying headers & footers to every page. So we have PHP, Handlebars, Next.JS. Modern HTML/JS now has Web Components , custom elements which could be used to encapsulate repetitive sections! This was already possible without Web Components, but it makes it nicer. My page's content

data.author: shidoshi
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了通过互惠关税来平衡美国与其贸易伙伴之间的双边贸易逆差问题。由于美国长期存在贸易逆差，传统贸易模型假设的贸易自动平衡并未实现。贸易逆差由关税和非关税壁垒等多种因素导致，包括监管障碍、税收差异、货币操纵等，这些因素抑制了美国商品出口，导致贸易失衡。为解决此问题，文章提出计算能使贸易逆差归零的关税水平，即互惠关税。通过模型推导和参数选择，文章计算出互惠关税率范围在0%至99%之间，未加权平均为20%，按进口加权平均为41%。这些关税率旨在抵消导致贸易失衡的政策和经济因素，以实现公平贸易。

43574751.article_content:
Executive Summary
Reciprocal tariffs are calculated as the tariff rate necessary to balance bilateral trade deficits between the U.S. and each of our trading partners. This calculation assumes that persistent trade deficits are due to a combination of tariff and non-tariff factors that prevent trade from balancing. Tariffs work through direct reductions of imports.
Reciprocal tariff rates range from 0 percent to 99 percent, with unweighted and import-weighted averages of 20 percent and 41 percent.
Introduction
To conceptualize reciprocal tariffs, the tariff rates that would drive bilateral trade deficits to zero were computed. While models of international trade generally assume that trade will balance itself over time, the United States has run persistent current account deficits for five decades, indicating that the core premise of most trade models is incorrect.
The failure of trade deficits to balance has many causes, with tariff and non-tariff economic fundamentals as major contributors. Regulatory barriers to American products, environmental reviews, differences in consumption tax rates, compliance hurdles and costs, currency manipulation and undervaluation all serve to deter American goods and keep trade balances distorted.  As a result, U.S. consumer demand has been siphoned out of the U.S. economy into the global economy, leading to the closure of more than 90,000 American factories since 1997, and a decline in our manufacturing workforce of more than 6.6 million jobs, more than a third from its peak.
While individually computing the trade deficit effects of tens of thousands of tariff, regulatory, tax and other policies in each country is complex, if not impossible, their combined effects can be proxied by computing the tariff level consistent with driving bilateral trade deficits to zero.
If trade deficits are persistent because of tariff and non-tariff policies and fundamentals, then the tariff rate consistent with offsetting these policies and fundamentals is reciprocal and fair.
Basic Approach
Consider an environment in which the U.S. levies a tariff of rate τ_i on country i and ∆τ_i reflects the change in the tariff rate. Let ε<0 represent the elasticity of imports with respect to import prices, let φ>0 represent the passthrough from tariffs to import prices, let m_i>0 represent total imports from country i, and let x_i>0 represent total exports. Then the decrease in imports due to a change in tariffs equals ∆τ_i*ε*φ*m_i<0. Assuming that offsetting exchange rate and general equilibrium effects are small enough to be ignored, the reciprocal tariff that results in a bilateral trade balance of zero satisfies:
Parameter Selection
To calculate reciprocal tariffs, import and export data from the U.S. Census Bureau for 2024. Parameter values for ε and φ were selected. The price elasticity of import demand, ε, was set at 4.
Recent evidence suggests the elasticity is near 2 in the long run (Boehm et al., 2023), but estimates of the elasticity vary. To be conservative, studies that find higher elasticities near 3-4 (e.g., Broda and Weinstein 2006; Simonovska and Waugh 2014; Soderbery 2018) were drawn on.  The elasticity of import prices with respect to tariffs, φ, is 0.25. The recent experience with U.S. tariffs on China has demonstrated that tariff passthrough to retail prices was low (Cavallo et al, 2021).
Findings
The reciprocal tariffs were left-censored at zero. Higher minimum rates might be necessary to limit heterogeneity in rates and reduce transshipment. Tariff rates range from 0 to 99 percent. The unweighted average across deficit countries is 50 percent, and the unweighted average across the entire globe is 20 percent. Weighted by imports, the average across deficit countries is 45 percent, and the average across the entire globe is 41 percent. Standard deviations range from 20.5 to 31.8 percentage points.
References
Boehm, Christoph E., Andrei A. Levchenko, and Nitya Panalai-Nayar (2023), “The long and short of (run) of trade elasticities, American Economic Review, 113(4), 861-905.
Broda, Christian and David E. Weinstein (2006). “Globalization and the gains from variety,” Quarterly Journal of Economics, 121(2), 541-585.
Pujolas, Pau and Jack Rossbach (2024). “Trade deficits with trade wars.” SSRN.
Simonovska, Ina and Michael E. Waugh (2014). “The elasticity of trade: Estimates and evidence,” Journal of International Economics, 92(1), 34-50.
Soderberry, Anson (2018). “Trade elasticities, heterogeneity, and optimal tariffs,” Journal of International Economics, 114, 44-62.

data.title: Porting Tailscale to Plan 9
data.author: adriangrigore
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Tailscale团队在2025年4月1日愚人节宣布将Tailscale移植到Plan 9操作系统的背后故事。最初，团队认为只需简单调整构建标签和路径即可完成移植，但在实际操作中发现Go编译器对Plan 9的支持已经退化，导致运行时崩溃。经过多番努力，包括修复Go编译器中的Plan 9特殊情况以及解决SSE指令和内存管理问题，最终在2025年3月完成了实际可运行的Plan 9移植版本。团队特别感谢前Go团队成员Russ Cox的帮助，他解决了Plan 9内核中保存和恢复SSE寄存器的问题，使得移植得以成功。最终，Tailscale现在确实能够在Plan 9上运行。

43557790.article_content:
Blog
|
insights
April 02, 2025
Porting Tailscale to Plan 9
It’s been said that nothing helps land a joke like explaining it, so here we are to explain yesterday’s
Tailscale Plan 9 announcement
, even at the risk of killing the joke.
But really, if we had to kill a joke by explaining it, there’s no better type of joke to kill than a corporate April Fools’ Day post. They’re admittedly pretty terrible in general. I’m of the opinion that if you’re going to do such a joke, you better put some effort into it;
it
should
actually
work
. (Otherwise it’s 100% sad instead of whatever percent sad yesterday’s post was.)
And to be super clear today on April 2nd because nobody believes anything on April 1st: Tailscale now actually works on Plan 9. For reals.
We were amused to find everybody in shock that there was
a PR
attached to yesterday’s blog post so let’s dig into that PR a bit, and other work that went on.
First off: I don’t really know Plan 9. I know
of
Plan 9, and I know people who know Plan 9, but I’m a Plan 9 newbie and I apologize in advance if I offend any Plan 9 people with my ignorance. I tried to check my cluelessness with others to make sure it’s not
too
stupid, but there are surely some inaccuracies in these posts and bugs and shortcuts and simplifying assumptions in the code.
Anyway.
As the quip goes, “We chose to port Tailscale to Plan 9 not because it was easy, but because we thought it would be easy.” Naively it kinda seems like you’d take Tailscale’s two Go binaries and build them with
GOOS=plan9 GOARCH=386 go install ./cmd/tailscale{,d}
and call it a day. Sure, I expected some
syscall
or
x/net
or
x/sys/unix
symbols to not exists with
GOOS=plan9
and some
//go:build
tag adjustments and some special cases for
runtime.GOOS == "plan9"
to use different default disk paths like we previously
did for AIX
, etc. So that’s
what I tried
in August 2023 when a local acquaintance here in Seattle
asked me for Plan 9 support
and I finally caved and said okay (after initially rejecting the idea). I tweaked some build tags & paths & compiled it and ….
Boom
. The binary crashed at runtime in weird ways. Turns out the Go compiler support for Plan 9 had bitrot. Plan 9 wasn’t one of Go’s
first-class ports
and nobody had noticed the regressions. Or maybe Tailscale just pushed Go a bit harder than it had been pushed on Plan 9 before.
In any case, the Tailscale Plan 9 effort stalled out through all of 2024, beyond my time and/or ability to fix.
At the beginning of March 2025, a coworker mentioned April Fools’ Day and I suddenly remembered our Plan 9 port.
I reached out to
Russ Cox
(a former coworker from the Go team with a lot of Plan 9 history) and told him I thought it’d be fun (& funny) to finish up in time for April 1st. He replied:
“Sure I’m in.
We should fix the plan 9 kernel to save those registers and then not have that special case anymore.”
It’s possible that Russ didn’t know what he was signing himself up for.
SSE
In 1999, Intel introduced the Pentium III processor with
SSE instructions
. Yesterday’s blog post is dated 1999 because that’s kinda where this whole adventure begins.
The “special case” that Russ was referring to above is how the Go compiler
tried to avoid using SSE anywhere
for Plan 9 targets because the Plan 9 kernel doesn’t allow SSE in “note handlers” (think: signal handlers), as it didn’t save/restore them. And because the Go compiler didn’t know which code was being used during a note handler, it conservatively tried to disable SSE everywhere. But that code was regularly breaking and there were too many
plan9
special
cases
throughout the compiler.
Ideally the Plan 9 kernel would just save/restore the SSE registers/context in note handlers, then Go could remove the Plan 9 special cases and treat it like every other operating system. So Russ did that.
For 386, the Plan 9 fix was
sys/src/9: allow floating point in note handlers
(and updating the docs in
sys/man/2: update notify
).
For amd64 (the 9k kernel), we ran into a
bunch more issues
. Russ fixed various things:
sys/src/9k: fix bug aliasing parent and child FP state after fork
sys/src/9k: allow floating point and simd in note handlers
sys/src/9k: fix noted(NCONT) losing registers
sys/src/libmach: fix default amd64 binary mapping
sys/src/cmd/ktrace: fix for new k10 kernel trap routine
… but by this time we’d both pretty much resigned to just focusing on making the demo work on
GOARCH=386
.
With the corresponding Go fix to
stop (incorrectly) special casing Plan 9’s code generation
,
tailscaled
could now start up and run (for longer) without crashing. I could then start working on the bits that I could fix.
IPC
Now it was crashing due to out of memory errors instead of stack corruption. It turns out an earlier attempt at porting Tailscale to Plan 9 had a bug resulting in launching an infinite number of goroutines. Fixing that bug in our
safesocket
IPC package to just boringly using localhost TCP fixed that and now
tailscaled
would run without cras

data.title: Countries apply lower tariffs on products by high-emitting "dirty" industries
data.author: TaurenHunter
data.article_summary: 一篇由加州大学伯克利分校经济学教授Joe Shapiro撰写的研究论文发现，全球各国对高碳排放的“脏”行业产品征收的进口关税显著低于“清洁”行业产品。这种“环境偏向”存在于多个国家的贸易政策中，导致高污染行业实际上获得了每吨二氧化碳85至120美元的隐性补贴。这一差额远高于经济学家估算的每吨碳排放的社会成本（约40至50美元）。造成这种偏向的原因之一是上游原材料（如钢铁、铝）的生产通常比下游产品（如汽车、手机）更依赖化石燃料，而 lobbying 活动也影响了关税设置。研究指出，调整这一偏向可在不显著影响全球收入的情况下大幅降低碳排放，并可能获得污染行业的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关税在国际贸易中的作用及其对市场公平性的影响

不同观点：
• [perrygeo的观点] 支持关税的理论基础是防止他国通过违反环境或劳工权益来压低价格。例如，美国木材公司需遵守环境法并支付合理工资，而海外竞争者可能无需遵守这些规定，从而以低价冲击市场。关税可以平衡竞争环境，使美国公司无需通过非法或不道德行为参与竞争。然而，该评论者指出，实际情况与此理论相反，各国似乎乐于从境外的剥削中获利。

• [隐含的反对观点] 尽管[perrygeo]支持关税的理论基础，但指出实际效果与预期不符。各国在实践中并未通过关税来抵制剥削，反而可能默许或从中获利。这暗示了关税政策在实际操作中的无效性或矛盾性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于关税是否能够有效防止市场中的不公平竞争行为。理论上，关税可以作为一种工具来保护本国市场免受不道德商业行为的冲击，但实际操作中，各国可能并未严格执行这一原则。

• 例子中的美国木材公司与海外竞争者的对比，突显了在全球化背景下，不同国家间的法律和道德标准差异如何影响市场竞争。

• 评论还暗示了对全球化经济中道德与经济利益冲突的深层次思考，即各国在追求经济利益时，是否真正关注境外的劳工权益和环境问题。

43573564.article_content:
Business & economics
,
Research
,
Science & environment
Forget carbon tariffs: Existing trade policies give dirty industries a boost
Countries around the world consistently apply lower import taxes on products produced by high-emitting "dirty" industries than “clean” ones
By
Kara Manke
May 4, 2020
Countries around the world consistently apply lower tariffs on products produced by “dirty” industries than by “clean” ones, finds a new analysis. (iStock photo)
In the United States and around the globe, products produced by “dirty” or high-carbon-emitting industries are facing significantly lower import taxes than their cleaner counterparts, finds
a new paper
from the University of California, Berkeley.
Fixing this “environmental bias” in trade policy could significantly lower global carbon emissions, while having little impact on overall global income, argues study author Joe Shapiro, an associate professor of economics and of agriculture and resource economics at UC Berkeley.
“It’s rare to find a systematic pattern that happens in many countries with broadly similar magnitude, but that’s what happens here,” said Shapiro. “This suggests that when countries go negotiate their trade policies, there is scope for that to have important large effects on the environment.”
The analysis was
published online
May 4 as part of the UC Berkeley’s
Energy Institute Working Paper Series
.
The finding comes at a time when many politicians — including 2020 presidential candidate Joe Biden — have proposed implementing higher import taxes, otherwise known as carbon tariffs, on goods produced by dirty industries.
Instead, existing trade policy grants what is essentially an $85 to $120 subsidy to polluting industries per ton of carbon dioxide produced, the study found.
“If you took two arbitrary bundles of goods that showed up in some port around the world, if one of those bundles of goods emitted one additional ton of carbon dioxide to produce, those dirtier goods would face an average of approximately $85 to $120 less in tariffs and in non-tariff barrier obstacles,” Shapiro said.
The approximate “carbon tariff,” or difference between tariffs on low-emitting and high-emitting industries, calculated for various countries around the world. Note that many countries that are considered to have strong environmental protections, such as those in the E.U., also have some of the strongest “environmental biases” in their trade policies, with significantly lower tariffs for dirty industries than for clean industries. (UC Berkeley graphic by Joe Shapiro)
That number is startling, given that many economists estimate that the global “social cost” of carbon emissions — and therefore, the optimal tax on carbon emissions — to be $40 or $50 per ton of carbon dioxide produced.
The significant discrepancy between tariffs on dirty and clean industries is likely due to a factor that economists like to call “upstreamness,” Shapiro found.
Raw goods, like steel and aluminum, are used as precursors to consumer goods, like automobiles and cell phones, and therefore are considered more “upstream” than the end products. The production of upstream raw materials is usually more fossil-fuel intensive than that for their downstream counterparts, which often include “clean” inputs, like software or design.
Powerful lobbying groups, like those representing automobile or technology industries, often push politicians to keep tariffs on raw goods low — so these industries have cheaper access to materials — while advocating for high tariffs on their own products, to protect their consumer bases.
While higher tariffs on dirty industries may impact consumer prices, they are also “one of the few environmental policies I am aware of which appeals to environmentalists and to polluting industries,” Shapiro said.
“Some environmental policies increase the cost of producing pollution-intensive goods, and so pollution-intensive industries lobby against them,” Shapiro said. “This is an environmental policy that protects the dirty industries, so they may lobby for it, and it has the potential to decrease carbon emissions.”
Youtuber econimate explores Shapiro’s findings in this illustrated video.
RELATED INFORMATION

(Energy Institute Working Paper Series)
International Trade Policies Subsidize Pollution
(Energy Institute Blog)

主要讨论点：Ben Eater的6502项目及其教育价值和实际操作体验

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun: 对Ben Eater的项目持积极态度，赞赏其通过长视频详细解释CPU工作原理的方式，并表达了对过去技术可理解性的怀念。他认为这个项目有展示和教育价值，甚至想将其装裱挂在墙上。
• rs186: 虽然通过该项目成功实现了斐波那契数列的显示并学到很多，但不推荐新手尝试。理由包括：时间与金钱成本高、部分设计选择有问题、教程过时且缺乏更新、零件难以获取、调试过程繁琐。他认为有其他更高效的学习方式。
• brucehoult: 强调该项目的计算机仅有16字节的内存，功能非常有限，仅能完成如斐波那契数列这样的简单任务。尽管如此，它是一个真正的冯·诺依曼架构计算机，且易于理解。
• atum47: 对Ben Eater的视频内容质量表示赞赏，认为其解释清晰，是优秀的学习资源，并表示至今仍是其粉丝。
• roland35: 分享了自己在大学期间通过搭建CPU学习数字逻辑的积极体验，认为这是非常有趣且有教育意义的项目。
• nabaraj: 提到自己在大学期间曾做过类似的8位GPU项目，认为这是一个有趣的项目，尽管细节已经记不太清。
• apricot: 认为Ben Eater的面包板CPU项目在教育上是有价值的，但其性能相对于使用的芯片数量来说较弱，推荐关注Gigatron项目，后者使用相同数量的TTL芯片但性能更强。
• userbinator: 对现代网页需要启用JavaScript才能查看内容表示不满，认为理想情况下，内容应该能在像自己搭建的8位计算机这样简单的设备上查看。

补充讨论：
• 该项目的教育价值和实际操作体验存在争议。一方面，JKCalhoun和atum47等用户对其教育价值给予高度评价；另一方面，rs186和apricot等用户则指出其时间成本高、设计问题和零件获取困难等实际操作中的挑战。
• rs186特别提到项目的教程过时且缺乏更新，导致新手可能需要额外调试和寻求帮助。
• apricot提出了一个对比项目Gigatron，认为其在性能上更具优势，为学习者提供了另一种选择。
• 用户对现代网页技术的要求与简单设备兼容性的讨论，反映了对技术简化和可访问性的不同期望。

• JKCalhoun: 对Ben Eater的项目持积极态度，赞赏其通过长视频详细解释CPU工作原理的方式，并表达了对过去技术可理解性的怀念。他认为这个项目有展示和教育价值，甚至想将其装裱挂在墙上。
• rs186: 虽然通过该项目成功实现了斐波那契数列的显示并学到很多，但不推荐新手尝试。理由包括：时间与金钱成本高、部分设计选择有问题、教程过时且缺乏更新、零件难以获取、调试过程繁琐。他认为有其他更高效的学习方式。
• brucehoult: 强调该项目的计算机仅有16字节的内存，功能非常有限，仅能完成如斐波那契数列这样的简单任务。尽管如此，它是一个真正的冯·诺依曼架构计算机，且易于理解。
• atum47: 对Ben Eater的视频内容质量表示赞赏，认为其解释清晰，是优秀的学习资源，并表示至今仍是其粉丝。
• roland35: 分享了自己在大学期间通过搭建CPU学习数字逻辑的积极体验，认为这是非常有趣且有教育意义的项目。
• nabaraj: 提到自己在大学期间曾做过类似的8位GPU项目，认为这是一个有趣的项目，尽管细节已经记不太清。
• apricot: 认为Ben Eater的面包板CPU项目在教育上是有价值的，但其性能相对于使用的芯片数量来说较弱，推荐关注Gigatron项目，后者使用相同数量的TTL芯片但性能更强。
• userbinator: 对现代网页需要启用JavaScript才能查看内容表示不满，认为理想情况下，内容应该能在像自己搭建的8位计算机这样简单的设备上查看。

补充讨论：
• 该项目的教育价值和实际操作体验存在争议。一方面，JKCalhoun和atum47等用户对其教育价值给予高度评价；另一方面，rs186和apricot等用户则指出其时间成本高、设计问题和零件获取困难等实际操作中的挑战。
• rs186特别提到项目的教程过时且缺乏更新，导致新手可能需要额外调试和寻求帮助。
• apricot提出了一个对比项目Gigatron，认为其在性能上更具优势，为学习者提供了另一种选择。
• 用户对现代网页技术的要求与简单设备兼容性的讨论，反映了对技术简化和可访问性的不同期望。

data.author: EvgeniyZh

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕GW-BASIC源代码及其历史背景的讨论

不同观点：
• stkai和zabzonk等人赞赏GW-BASIC源代码的质量和历史意义，特别是其中有趣的注释以及当年技术实现的难度。stkai引用了源代码中的幽默注释，zabzonk则通过分享自己用FORTRAN77编写Intel 8080模拟器的经历，表达了对早期技术成就的钦佩。
• billforsternz批评了网站的用户体验，认为其动画设计过于花哨，不符合1970年代的技术风格，建议使用更简洁、轻量的技术来呈现信息。
• winrid和jer0me则对网页设计和源代码的展示形式提出意见，winrid开玩笑说网站错过了使用win98.css的机会，jer0me提供了源代码的链接，并提醒文件大小为100 MB。

补充讨论：
• 关于源代码的法律风险，switch007开玩笑地提到阅读源代码可能会引发法律诉讼，反映了人们对代码泄露事件的敏感性。
• 对微软及比尔·盖茨的评价存在分歧，santiagobasulto指出尽管微软在黑客社区中不受欢迎，但盖茨和艾伦对技术发展的贡献不可否认。rayiner则对微软的市场成功持批评态度，认为其成功与实际技术能力不符。
• 技术实现的历史细节引发了讨论，starik36好奇当年源代码是如何输入到Altair计算机中的，是否需要重新输入或通过某种早期的存储介质。
• 其他如froggertoaster和Seanambers的评论较为个人化，前者提到与比尔·盖茨的短暂会面，后者则批评文章对读者的技术水平定位不准。

争议焦点：
• 网站设计是否应更贴近1970年代的真实体验，以及微软及比尔·盖茨在技术历史中的地位评价。

data.title: Supervisors often prefer rule breakers, up to a point
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：规则的制定原因、执行方式以及是否/何时可以打破规则

不同观点：
• [seeknotfind] 认为理解规则制定的原因并确保规则制定者会满意是关键，强调对规则背后意图的理解。
• [madrox] 作为主管，更倾向于信任员工的判断和内在动机，而不是强制执行规则。只有当员工的判断力不再可信时，才会依赖规则进行外部激励。
• [pdpi] 指出规则通常伴随着妥协，简单的规则在复杂情况下可能会限制良好的行为并允许一些不良行为。了解如何利用这些空间是有价值的。
• [rblatz] 通过传闻指出，某些环境中（如运动员使用类固醇）规则的违反可能实际上是被默许甚至鼓励的，因为它们有助于控制团队。
• [taeric] 认为有目的性地打破规则是可以接受的，但当这种“成本”判断与主管的看法不一致时，问题就会出现。

补充讨论：
• [neilv] 强调了规则的来源和组织对规则的重视程度对是否可以打破规则有重要影响。还提到管理者与组织在规则上的利益是否一致，也会影响规则的执行和打破。
• [neuroelectron] 认为打破规则可以让组织获利而无需承担责任，难以看到负面影响。
• [ungreased0675] 指出讨论中提到的研究仅适用于NHL，可能不适用于其他情境。
• [jbmsf] 表示制定规则主要是为了防止最坏的情况发生，但如果员工表现良好，规则通常有变通余地。
• [jvanderbot] 提到可以“训斥”规则破坏者，然后在他们不再违反规则时获得功劳。
• [nitwit005] 认为在体育界，员工可能是在遵循雇主的指示去违反体育联盟的规则，而非真正违反雇主的规则。
• [userbinator] 作为主管，认为战略性地打破规则的能力是其成功的重要因素，且这种能力在员工中也被注意到。

争议焦点：
• 规则是否应当被打破以及何时可以打破。部分人认为规则可以为了实际需求而打破，而另一些人则担心这样可能引发不良行为或不符合组织利益。
• 规则的制定背景和执行力度的差异，尤其是在不同行业和组织中的适用性。

data.title: The cultural evolution of distortion in music
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： distortion（失真）在音乐中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• Tade0认为，电吉他失真的波形通常接近锯齿波，而不是三角波，除非弦在正中拨动。他还提到失真的音色会根据弹奏技巧和设备的不同而变化，例如不同放大器（如Mesa Boogie）和效果器（如BOSS DS-1）如何通过技术限制产生独特的音色。Tade0还强调了失真在动态和音色变化中的作用。

• Kazinator指出，单音失真（如电吉他独奏）在主流音乐中较快被接受，因为电路技术不断改进。然而，过于刺耳的失真音色仍然是小众的，只在特定音乐风格中（如重金属）得到广泛应用。他还讨论了失真如何影响和声结构，特别是在重金属音乐中通过失真创造出复杂的音调关系。

• Driggs对原文的长篇分析持批评态度，认为其过于学术化，缺乏艺术性表达。Driggs更欣赏如Henry Rollins和Don Was之间的对话，这种更直接、贴近艺术本身的讨论。

• Myself248分享了个人经历，通过播放Pink Floyd的音乐向他人解释失真，并提出了一个理论，即失真吉他声音类似于发动机的声音，象征着自由，这可能是年轻人被摇滚乐吸引的原因之一。

• Drops引用了Brian Eno的话，强调失真是媒介超越其承载能力的标志，是“失败的声音”，这种声音最终会被珍惜和模仿。Drops的观点强调了失真在现代艺术中作为一种突破媒介限制的表现形式。

补充讨论：
• 失真在不同音乐风格中的接受度和应用方式不同，尤其是重金属和爵士/摇滚融合音乐中失真的使用差异。
• 失真音色的变化与设备的技术限制和演奏技巧密切相关，如放大器和效果器的设计如何影响音色。
• 失真作为艺术表现的一部分，其美学价值和象征意义被不同评论者从个人经历和哲学角度进行了探讨。
